The bearer of the document (sahib al-sahifa) came to him with his document, and he refrained from them and from the people of his household. He then destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and threw carrion into it. The Romans assisted him in its destruction, because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya. He also took away with him the notables of the Children of Israel, and took Daniel and a group of the sons of the prophets. He took with him the head of Jalut as well. When he arrived in Babil, he found that Sakhabin had died, so he became king in his place. The most honored people in his presence were Daniel and his companions. The Magians envied them and denounced them to him, saying: "Daniel and his companions do not worship your god, and they do not eat your slaughtered animals." He asked them, and they said: "Indeed, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat of your slaughter." The king ordered a trench to be dug for them, and they were thrown into it. There were six of them. He also threw in with them a ferocious beast to devour them. They went away, then returned in the morning and found them sitting, with the beast stretched out its forelegs beside them, not having scratched any of them. They also found with them a seventh man. He said: "What is this seventh? There were only six of them." The seventh came out, and he was an angel. He struck him a slap, so [Bukhtnassar] was among the wild beasts, and God transformed him for seven years.

Wahb related that God transformed Bukhtnassar into an eagle among birds, then transformed him into a bull among domestic animals, then transformed him into a lion among wild beasts. His transformation lasted seven years, while his heart remained a human heart throughout. Then God returned his kingdom to him, and he believed. Wahb was asked: "Was he a believer?" He said: "I found that the People of the Book disagreed about him. Some said he was a believer, and others said he burned Bayt al-Maqdis and its scriptures and killed the prophets, so God became angry with him and did not accept his repentance."

As-Suddi said: When Bukhtnassar returned to his form after the transformation, and God restored his kingdom to him, Daniel and his companions were the most honored people in his sight. The Magians envied them and said to Bukhtnassar: "When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot control himself from urinating," and this was considered a disgrace among them. So [the king] prepared food and drink for them, and they ate and drank. He told the doorkeeper: "Watch for the first one who comes out to urinate, and strike him with the tabarzin (a heavy mace). If he says, 'I am Bukhtnassar,' say, 'You lie, Bukhtnassar ordered me.'" The first to rise to urinate was Bukhtnassar. When the doorkeeper saw him, he attacked him. [Bukhtnassar] said: "Woe to you! I am Bukhtnassar." He replied: "You lie, Bukhtnassar ordered me," and he struck him and killed him.

This is what was mentioned in al-Mubtada' (The Beginning, a historical work). However, the report of those who narrated that Bukhtnassar raided the Children of Israel at the time they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya is an error according to the scholars of biographical history (ahl al-siyar). Rather, they unanimously agree that Bukhtnassar only raided the Children of Israel when they killed Shi'ya' (Isaiah) in the time of Armiya' (Jeremiah). From the time of Armiya' and Bukhtnassar's destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis until the birth of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was four hundred and sixty-one years. [The people] used to count from the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis by Bukhtnassar until its rebuilding in the time of Kirash ibn Akhshurash ibn Usayhid in Babil, under Bahman ibn Isfandiyar [seventy years]. Then from its rebuilding until Alexander's conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis was eighty-eight years. Then from his rule until the birth of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was three hundred and sixty years [[The bracketed phrase is absent from manuscript "B".]].

The sound view on this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned.

His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book﴾, meaning: We informed them and told them, through the scriptures We gave them, that they would cause corruption.

Qada' (decree) has several meanings. It can mean command, as in His saying: "And your Lord has decreed" [al-Isra': 23]. It can mean judgment, as in His saying: "Indeed, your Lord will judge between them" [Yunus: 93; al-Nahl: 78]. It can mean creation, as in His saying: "And He completed them as seven heavens" [Fussilat: 12].

Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: it means "And We decreed against them," and "ila" here has the meaning of "ala" (upon). By "the Book" is meant the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿You will surely﴾: the lam here is the lam of oath, its meaning being "By God, you will surely." ﴿cause corruption in the land twice﴾ through sins. By "the land" is meant the land of al-Sham and Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿And you will surely become haughty﴾, meaning you will be arrogant and will surely wrong people, ﴿with great arrogance﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 2–4 (part 1 of 4):

The words of the Most High, ﴿And We gave Musa the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, that﴾, meaning, "that," ﴿do not take besides Me a trustee﴾, meaning, a lord and a guardian.

Abu 'Amr read "لَا يَتَّخِذُوا" (la yattakhidhu, "they should not take") with the yā' (ي), because it is a report about them. The others read it with the tā' (ت), meaning: "We said to them, 'Do not take.'"

﴿Offspring of those whom We carried﴾. Mujahid said: this is a form of address, meaning, "O offspring of those whom We carried ﴿with Nuh﴾ in the ship, so We saved them from the flood. ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾." Nuh, peace be upon him, when he ate food, drank a drink, or wore a garment, would say: "Al-hamdu lillah" (all praise is for Allah). So he was named "a grateful servant," meaning one who gives abundant thanks.[[Narrated by Ibn Jarir, 15/19, from Salman, Mujahid, Qatadah and others. Al-Hakim authenticated it according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, 2/360. Al-Suyuti mentioned a number of reports on this, see al-Durr al-Manthur, 5/236–237. Imam Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a meal or drinks a drink and praises Allah for it." In al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith of intercession, he said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection..." and in it: "They will come to Nuh and say: 'O Nuh, you are the first of the messengers to the people of the earth, and Allah has named you a grateful servant. So intercede for us with your Lord.'" And he mentioned the whole hadith.]]

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture﴾, and the verses.

Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:[[Narrated by al-Tabari. See al-Tafsir, 15/22–43; Tarikh al-Tabari, 1/532–557; al-Durr al-Manthur, 5/243–244. These numerous reports that the author, may Allah have mercy on him, cites concerning those who were empowered over the Children of Israel are among the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Jewish and Christian sources) and fabrications. They contain wonders, oddities and exaggerations that are not credible, and some of them may also be true. Ibn Jarir narrated much of this from Ibn Ishaq, and it is clear that Ibn Ishaq explicitly names the People of the Book, saying that they say such-and-such, or that they have such-and-such. We are sufficient without all of these reports. Here we place a valuable statement of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, as a commentary on these reports. He said: "The exegetes, from the early and later generations, have differed about who these empowered enemies were. From Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah it is related that it was Jalut (Goliath) and his armies. From Sa'id ibn Jubayr it is related that it was the king of Mosul, Sinjarib, and his armies. Also from him: it was Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), king of Babylon. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned a strange story about how he rose from one condition to another until he ruled the lands..." Then Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Jarir has narrated in this place a hadith with a chain going back to Hudhayfah, raised to the Prophet, a lengthy one, which is the hadith that al-Baghawi cites here, and it is undoubtedly a fabricated hadith. Anyone with even a little knowledge of hadith would not doubt this. How strange it is, with all his stature and leadership, that it was accepted by him! Our teacher, the Hafiz, the scholar Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, may Allah have mercy on him, declared it fabricated and false, and wrote this in the margin of the book." Then he said, pointing to the rest of the reports: "Many Isra'ili reports have come in this matter, but I did not see fit to lengthen the book by mentioning them, because some of them are fabrications invented by some of their heretics, and some of them may possibly be true. We are sufficient without them, praise be to Allah. What Allah has related to us in His Book suffices us over all other books before it, and neither Allah nor His Messenger has made us in need of them. Allah has informed us about them: that when they transgressed and rebelled, Allah sent their enemy against them, who plundered their domain, went through the inner parts of their houses, and humiliated and subdued them, as a fitting recompense, and your Lord is not unjust to the servants, because they had rebelled and killed a multitude of prophets and scholars. Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Bukhtnassar prevailed over al-Sham, destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and killed them. Then he came to Damascus and found there blood boiling on a rock, and he asked them what this blood was... so seventy thousand of the Muslims and others were killed over that blood, and it became calm. This chain is authentic up to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and this is the well-known account, that he killed their nobles and scholars until no one remained who had memorized the Torah, and he took with him from them captives, including sons of prophets and others. Many events and occurrences took place, which would take long to mention. Had we found something authentic or close to authentic, it would be permissible to write and narrate it. And Allah knows best."[[See also: al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahbah, pp. 327–334.]]

"Indeed, when the Children of Israel transgressed and killed the prophets, Allah sent against them the king of Persia, 'Bukhtnassar,' and Allah had given him kingship for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Bayt al-Maqdis, besieged it, conquered it, and killed seventy thousand over the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon him. Then he took its people captive [and the children],[[Omitted from manuscript "B".]] and plundered the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and extracted from it seventy thousand and one hundred thousand golden bracelets' worth of ornaments." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, was Bayt al-Maqdis great?" He said: "Yes. Sulayman ibn Dawud built it of gold, silver, rubies and chrysolite, and its pillars were of gold. Allah granted him that, and subjected the devils to him, who brought him these things in the blink of an eye. Bukhtnassar carried them away until he settled in Babylon. The Children of Israel remained in his hand for one hundred years, enslaved by the Magians and the sons of the Magians, and among them were prophets. Then Allah had mercy on them, and revealed to a king of the kings of Persia called 'Kurash,' who was a believer, that he should march to them to rescue the remnant of the Children of Israel. So Kurash marched to the Children of Israel and seized the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis and returned them to it. The Children of Israel then remained there, obedient to Allah the Exalted, for one hundred years. Then they returned to sins, so Allah empowered over them a king called 'Antaniyus,' who raided the Children of Israel until he came to them at Bayt al-Maqdis, took its people captive, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis. He said to them: 'O Children of Israel, if you return to sins, we will return against you a second time [with captivity].'[[Addition in manuscript "B".]] They returned, so Allah empowered over them the king of Rome called 'Faqis ibn Astiyanus,' who raided them by land and sea, took them captive, took the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is part of the description of the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Mahdi will return them to Bayt al-Maqdis, by means of one thousand seven hundred ships which will be cast upon Yafa until they are transported to Bayt al-Maqdis, and by it Allah will gather the first and the last."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The Children of Israel had among them misdeeds and sins, and Allah was overlooking them and doing good to them. The first thing that befell them because of their sins, as Allah informed through the tongue of Musa, peace be upon him, was that a king among them called "Sidiqah"[[In the original it is with the hā' (ه); in al-Tabari it is with the tā' marbuta (ة).]] ruled. Whenever Allah made a king rule over them, He sent with him a prophet to support and guide him. He did not send them new scriptures; rather, they were commanded to follow the Torah and the rulings in it.

When that king ruled, Allah sent with him "Sha'ya' ibn Asfiya," and that was before the mission of Zakariyya, Yahya and 'Isa, peace be upon them all. Sha'ya' is the one who gave glad tidings of 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. He said: "Rejoice, O Jerusalem, now there comes to you the rider on the donkey, and after him the owner of the camel." That king ruled the Children of Israel and Bayt al-Maqdis for a time. When his reign ended, misdeeds grew widespread among them, while Sha'ya' was still with them. Allah sent against them "Sinjarib"[[In the history of al-Tabari it is "Sanhârib" with the unpointed h.]] king of Babylon, with six hundred thousand banners. He advanced until he camped around Bayt al-Maqdis, while the king was ill with an ulcer in his leg. The prophet Sha'ya' came to him and said: "O king of the Children of Israel, Sinjarib king of Babylon has descended upon you with his armies, six hundred thousand banners, and the people have been frightened and scattered." This weighed heavily on the king, and he said: "O prophet of Allah, has any revelation come to you from Allah about what has happened, so that you may inform us how Allah will deal with us and with Sinjarib and his armies?"

He said: "No revelation has come to me." While they were in that state, Allah revealed to the prophet Sha'ya': "Go to the king of the Children of Israel and command him to make his will, and to appoint as successor over his kingdom whomever he wishes from among his family." So Sha'ya' came to the king of the Children of Israel, "Sidiqah," and said to him: "Your Lord has revealed to me that I should command you to make your will and to appoint as successor over your kingdom whomever you wish from among your family, for you are dying." When Sha'ya' said that to Sidiqah, he turned toward the qiblah, prayed, supplicated and wept, and he said while weeping, humbling himself before Allah with a sincere heart: "O Allah, Lord of lords and God of gods, O Holy One of the Holy, O Compassionate, O Merciful, O Kind, O You whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, remember me for my deed and my conduct and my good judgment over the Children of Israel. All of that was from You, and You know it better than I do. My secret and my open affairs are for You, and You are the Compassionate." So He responded to him, for he was a righteous servant. Allah the Exalted revealed to Sha'ya' that he should inform Sidiqah that his Lord had responded to him, had shown him mercy, had postponed his term by fifteen years, and had saved him from his enemy Sinjarib. Sha'ya' came to him and informed him of that. When he told him, the pain departed from him, the sorrow left him, and he fell down in prostration and said: "O my God and God of my fathers, to You I prostrate, and I glorify, magnify and exalt You. You are the One who gives kingship to whom You will, and strips kingship from whom You will, honors whom You will, and humbles whom You will. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You are the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and You are merciful and You answer the prayer of the distressed. You are the One who answered my prayer and had mercy on my humble supplication."

When he lifted his head, Allah revealed to Sha'ya': "Say to the king Sidiqah: he should command one of his servants to bring him fig water, and he should put it on his ulcer, and he will be healed; he will wake in the morning and he will be cured." [205/b] He did so, and was healed.

The king said to Sha'ya': "Ask your Lord to give us knowledge of what He will do with this enemy of ours."

Allah said to Sha'ya': "Tell him: I have sufficed you against your enemy and saved you from them, and they will all become dead by morning, except Sinjarib and five men of his scribes."

When they woke in the morning, a crier came and cried out at the gate of the city: "O king of the Children of Israel, Allah has sufficed you against your enemy, so go out, for Sinjarib and those with him have perished." When the king went out, he searched for Sinjarib but did not find him among the dead. The king sent men to seek him, and the seekers found him in a cave with five of his scribes, one of whom was Bukhtnassar. They brought them to the Children of Israel's king in chains. When he saw them, he fell down in prostration from sunrise until the afternoon prayer. Then he said to Sinjarib: "How do you see the action of our Lord toward you? Did He not kill you by His power and might, while we and you were heedless?" Sinjarib said to him: "The news of your Lord and His victory for you has reached me, and of His mercy by which He had mercy on you before I went out from my land. I did not obey a guide, and nothing cast me into misery except [humiliation in this world and punishment in the Hereafter]. If I had listened or understood, I would not have attacked you."

Sidiqah said: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has sufficed us against you as He willed. Our Lord did not let you and those with you remain out of honor for you before your Lord; rather He let you and those with you remain only so that you would increase in misery in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, and so that you would inform those behind you of what you saw of the action of our Lord toward you, and warn those after you. Had it not been for that, He would have killed you. Your blood and the blood of those with you is less valuable to Allah than the blood of a tick, even if you had been killed."

Then the king of the Children of Israel ordered the commander of his guard, who fastened collars (al-jawami') around their necks and paraded them for seventy days around Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and Iliya. He gave each man of them two loaves of barley bread each day.

Sennacherib (Sanjarib) said to the king of the Children of Israel: "Death is better than what you are doing to us." So the king sent them to the prison of death. Then God revealed to Sha'ya (Isaiah), peace be upon him: "Tell the king of the Children of Israel: Let Sennacherib and those with him go forth to warn those behind them, and let him honour them, carry them, until they reach their lands." Sha'ya conveyed this to the king, and [the king, Siddiqa,] did as he was commanded. Sennacherib and those with him set out until they came to Babylon (Babil). When they arrived, he gathered the people and informed them how God had dealt with his armies. His soothsayers (kuhhan) and sorcerers (sahara) said to him: "O king of Babylon, we used to relate to you the news of their Lord, the news of their prophet, and the revelation God sent to their prophet, but you did not obey us. They are a nation that no one can withstand with their Lord." The affair of Sennacherib was a warning for them; then God sufficed them, as a reminder and a lesson.

After that, Sennacherib remained for seven years, then died. Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), the son of his son, was made his successor, doing as his grandfather had done. He remained for seventeen years. Then God took the soul of the king of the Children of Israel, Siddiqa. The affairs of the Children of Israel fell into disorder, they competed for kingship until some of them killed others, and their prophet Sha'ya was with them, but they would not accept from him.

When they did this, God said to Sha'ya: "Stand among your people; I will reveal through your tongue." So when the prophet Sha'ya stood up, God made his tongue speak the revelation. He said: "O heaven, hear! O earth, be silent! For God wishes to recount the affair of the Children of Israel, whom He nurtured with His favour, chose for Himself, singled out with His honour, and preferred over His servants. They are like sheep scattered without a shepherd. He gathered their strays, collected their lost ones, set their broken bones, healed their sick, fattened their emaciated ones, and guarded their fat ones. But when He did this, they became arrogant, and their rams butted one another until some of them killed others, until no sound bone remained to which a broken one could be set. Woe to this sinful nation who do not know from where good has come to them! The camel remembers its homeland and so returns to it; the donkey remembers the pasture on which it was fed and so goes back to it; the bull remembers the meadow in which it grew fat and so returns to it. Yet these people do not remember from where good has come to them. They are people of intellect and understanding; they are neither cattle nor donkeys. I will strike for them a parable, so let them listen. Say to them: What do you think of a land that was empty for a time, desolate, dead, without any habitation, and it had a Lord, wise and mighty, who turned to it with cultivation, disliked that His land should be ruined while He was mighty, or that it should be said He was negligent while He was wise? So He surrounded it with a wall, built palaces in it, dug a river, planted in it saplings of olives, pomegranates, date palms, grapes, and all kinds of fruits, and entrusted that to a man of judgement and resolve, a vigilant, strong, trustworthy guardian. But when it blossomed, its blossom bore carob (kharrub) instead."

They said: "Evil is this land. We see that its wall and palace should be demolished, its river filled in, its guardian dismissed, and its plants burned, until it becomes as it was at first: desolate, dead, without habitation." God said: He said to them: "The wall is My religion; the palace is My law; the river is My Book; the guardian is My prophet; the plants are they (the people); and the carob that bore the plants is their evil deeds. I have decreed against them the judgement they passed against themselves. This is a parable I have coined for them: they draw near to Me by slaughtering cattle and sheep, yet meat does not reach Me, nor do I eat it; and they neglect to draw near to Me by piety and refraining from slaying the souls I have forbidden. Their hands are stained with them, and their garments are soaked with their blood. They build houses for Me as mosques and purify their insides, yet they defile their hearts and bodies and soil them; they adorn the mosques for Me and beautify them, yet they ruin their minds and dreams and corrupt them. What need have I of building houses when I do not dwell in them? What need have I of adorning mosques when I do not enter them? I only commanded that they be raised so that I might be remembered and glorified therein."

They say: "We fasted, but our fasting was not raised; we prayed, but our prayer was not illuminated [and we prayed, but our prayer was not made luminous]; we gave charity, but our charity was not purified; we called upon Him like the moaning of doves and wept like the howling of wolves, yet in all of this we are not answered."

God said: "Ask them: what prevents Me from responding to them? Am I not the Hearer of hearers, the Seer of seers, the Nearest of those who respond, and the Most Merciful of the merciful? How can I raise their fasting when they clothe it with false speech and strengthen themselves by it through unlawful food? Or how can I illuminate their prayer when their hearts incline toward one who wars against Me, opposes Me, and violates My sanctities? Or how can their charities be purified before Me when they give charity from the wealth of others? Rather, I reward its owners, who were wronged. Or how can I respond to their supplication, when it is only words on their tongues, while action is far from it? I only respond to the one who calls humbly, and I only hear the words of the modest, needy one; and among the signs of My pleasure is the pleasure of the needy."

They say when they hear My words and My message reaches them: "These are transmitted sayings and inherited narratives, a composition of the kind sorcerers and soothsayers compose." They claim that if they wished they could bring a discourse like it, and if they wished they could gain knowledge of the unseen through what the devils reveal to them, they would have attained it. I have decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth a decree that I affirmed and made binding upon Myself, and I placed before it a term, appointed, which must certainly come to pass. So if they are truthful in what they claim of knowledge of the unseen, let them tell you when I shall execute it, or in what time it will occur. If they are able to bring about whatever they wish, let them bring the like of this power by which I have enacted it, for I shall make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it. And if they are able to say whatever they wish, let them say the like of the wisdom by which I manage the execution of that decree, if they are truthful. I decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth that I would place prophethood among hired labourers, sovereignty among shepherds, honour among the humble, strength among the weak, wealth among the poor, knowledge among the ignorant, and wisdom among the unlettered. So ask them: when will this be, who will carry it out, and who are the helpers and supporters of this matter, if they know? I shall raise for this a prophet, unlettered, trustworthy, neither harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets, nor adorned with obscenity, nor one who speaks foul words. I shall guide him to every goodness and bestow upon him every noble character. I shall make tranquillity his garment, righteousness his inner garment, piety his inner consciousness, wisdom his understanding, truthfulness and fidelity his nature, pardon and kindness his character, justice his conduct, [truth his law,] guidance and [the Qur'an] his leader, Islam his creed, and Ahmad his name. Through him I shall guide after error, teach after ignorance, raise after obscurity, make famous after anonymity, increase after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and join together hearts that are at odds, desires that are scattered, and nations that are dispersed. I shall make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, in affirmation of My oneness, faith, and sincerity toward Me. They will pray standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating; they will fight in My cause in ranks and in waves; they will leave their homes and their wealth seeking My good pleasure. I shall inspire them with glorification (takbir), declaration of oneness (tawhid), praise of Me (tasbih), commendation (tahmid), eulogy, and exaltation (tamjid) in their journeys, their gatherings, their resting places, their places of rising, and their abodes. They will proclaim takbir, tahlil, and taqdis upon the heights; they will purify their faces and extremities for Me; they will fold their garments in the middle. Their offering is their blood, and their Gospels are in their chests. They are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I bestow on whom I will, and I am the Lord of Great Bounty."

When Sha'ya finished his speech, they rushed upon him to kill him. He fled from them, and a tree met him and split open for him, so he entered it. Satan overtook him and seized a fringe of his garment, and he showed it to them. They placed the saw in the middle of the tree and sawed it until they cut it through, and they cut him in its middle.

After that, God appointed over the Children of Israel a man from among them called Nashiya ibn Amus, and He sent to them Irmiya (Jeremiah) ibn Hilqiya as a prophet. He was from the tribe of Harun ibn Imran.

Ibn Ishaq mentioned that he was al-Khidr, and his name was Irmiya. He was called al-Khidr because he sat on a white patch of ground, then rose from it, and it was trembling green.

So God sent Irmiya (Jeremiah) to that king to guide and direct him. Then the transgressions among the Children of Israel grew great. They indulged in sins and made lawful what God had forbidden. God revealed to Irmiya: "Go to your people, the Children of Israel. Relate to them what I command you, remind them of My blessings, and inform them of their misdeeds." Irmiya said: "My Lord, I am weak unless You strengthen me. I am incapable unless You convey (the message) through me. I am forsaken unless You support me." God, exalted is He, said: "Do you not know that all affairs proceed from My will, and that hearts and tongues are in My hand? I turn them as I wish. Indeed, I am with you, and nothing will reach you while I am with you." Irmiya stood among them, not knowing what to say, so God inspired him at that moment with an eloquent sermon in which he explained the reward of obedience and the punishment of disobedience. At the end of it he said, on behalf of God, exalted is He: "I have sworn by My might that I will bring upon them a trial in which the forbearing will be bewildered, and I will set over them a tyrannical, harsh ruler. I will clothe him in awe and remove mercy from his heart. A host like the blackness of the dark night will follow him."

Then God revealed to Irmiya: "I am going to destroy the Children of Israel through Yafith, and Yafith is from the people of Babil (Babylon), as we mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah." So God set over them Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar). He set out with six hundred thousand banners, entered Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) with his armies, trod upon al-Sham (Greater Syria), and killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them. He destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and ordered each of his soldiers to fill his shield with dirt and then hurl it into Bayt al-Maqdis. They did so until they had filled it. Then he ordered them to gather everyone in the towns around Bayt al-Maqdis, and every young and old person among the Children of Israel assembled before him. He selected from them seventy thousand boys. When the spoils of his army were brought out and he wished to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said to him: "O king, all the spoils are yours. Divide among us these boys whom you have chosen from the Children of Israel." So he distributed them among the kings who were with him, and each man received four young boys. He divided the remaining Children of Israel into three groups: one third he settled in al-Sham, one third he took captive, and one third he killed. He took the young men of Bayt al-Maqdis and the seventy thousand boys with him until he brought them to Babil. This was the first calamity that God sent upon the Children of Israel because of their wrongdoing. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might﴾, meaning Bukhtansar and his companions.

Then Bukhtansar remained in his rule for as long as God willed. Then he saw a dream that amazed him, for he saw something that troubled him, but God made him forget what he had seen. He summoned Daniyal (Daniel), Hananiya, Azaraya, and Mishaʾil, who were descendants of the prophets, and asked them about it. They said: "Tell us the dream, and we will tell you its interpretation." He said: "I do not remember it. If you do not tell me it and its interpretation, I will surely tear off your shoulders." So they left him and called upon God and humbled themselves before Him, and God informed them of what he had asked them about. They came to him and said: "You saw a statue whose feet and shins were of clay, whose knees and thighs were of bronze, whose belly was of silver, whose chest was of gold, and whose head and neck were of iron." He said: "You have spoken truly." They said: "While you were looking at it and it pleased you, God sent down a rock from the sky, which shattered it. That is what made you forget it." He said: "You have spoken truly." He said: "What is its interpretation?" They said: "Its interpretation is that you saw the kingdoms of the kings. Some of them were softer in rule, some were better in rule, and some were stronger in rule. The clay is the weakest, above it is the bronze, which is stronger than it, above the bronze is the silver, which is better and superior to that, and gold is better and superior to silver. Then the iron is your kingdom, and it is stronger and mightier than what came before it. The rock that you saw, which God sent from the sky and which shattered it, is a prophet whom God will send from the sky, and he will shatter all of that, and the affair will pass to him."

Then the people of Babil said to Bukhtansar: "Have you considered these boys from the Children of Israel whom we asked you to give to us, and you did? We have denied our women since they have been with us. We have seen that our women's faces have turned away from us toward them. So either expel them from among us or kill them." He said: "The matter is yours regarding them. Whoever among you wishes to kill those in his possession, let him do so."

When they brought them out to be killed, they wept to God, exalted is He, and said: "O Lord, we have been afflicted by the sins of others." God promised to answer them. So they were killed, except for those whom Bukhtansar spared from among them: Daniyal, Hananiya, Azaraya, and Mishaʾil.

Then when God intended to destroy Bukhtansar, he rose up and said to those among the Children of Israel who were in his possession: "Have you considered this House that I destroyed, and the people I killed from among them? And what is this House?" They said: "This is the House of God, and these are its people. They were descendants of the prophets, but they committed wrongdoing and transgressed, so you were empowered over them because of their sins. Their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and the Lord of all creation. He honored and strengthened them. When they did what they did, God destroyed them and gave power over them to others. You became arrogant and thought that by your tyranny you did this to the Children of Israel." He said: "Then tell me how I can ascend to the highest heaven, kill whoever is in it, and take it as my kingdom, for I have finished with the earth." They said: "No creature is able to do that." He said: "You will do it, or I will kill you all to the last one." So they wept and humbled themselves before God, exalted is He. Then God, by His power, sent a gnat which entered his nostril until it bit the root of his brain. He could neither stay still nor rest, and his head was struck on the root of his brain until it was split open. When he died, they split open his head and found the gnat biting the root of his brain, so that God might show His servants His power. God delivered those of the Children of Israel who remained in his possession, and they returned them to al-Sham, where they built and multiplied until they were in the best state they had ever been.

They claim that God brought back to life those who had been killed, and they joined them. Then when they entered al-Sham, they entered it without any covenant from God, and the Tawrah (Torah) had been burned. Uzayr (Ezra) was among the captives in Babil, and he returned to al-Sham weeping over it night and day. He had withdrawn from the people. While he was in that state, a man approached him and said: "O Uzayr, what makes you weep?" He said: "I weep over the Book of God and His covenant that was among us, which nothing else can set right for our worldly life and our hereafter." He said: "Would you like it to be returned to you? Go, fast, purify yourself, and purify your garments. Then let your appointment be this place tomorrow." So Uzayr went, fasted, purified himself, and purified his garments. Then he made his way to the place he had been promised and sat there. That man came to him with a vessel containing water, and he was an angel whom God had sent to him. He gave him to drink from that vessel, and the Tawrah took form in his chest. He returned to the Children of Israel and set the Tawrah before them, and they loved him so much that they never loved anything as they loved him. Then God took him, and after that the Children of Israel began to commit misdeeds. God would turn back toward them and send messengers to them, but some they called liars and some they killed. The last of the prophets God sent among them were Zakariyya (Zechariah), Yahya (John), and Isa (Jesus), and they were from the house of Dawud (David). Zakariyya died, though it was also said that Zakariyya was killed. When God raised Isa from among them, and they killed Yahya, God set over them a king from the kings of Babil called Khardush. He marched against them with the people of Babil until he entered al-Sham upon them. When he prevailed over them, he ordered a commander among his soldiers, named Biyurzadhan, who was in charge of killing, and said: "I had sworn by my god that if I prevailed over the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, I would surely kill them until their blood flowed in the middle of my camp. But I do not find anyone to kill." So he ordered him to kill them, until Biyurzadhan reached that point among them. He entered Bayt al-Maqdis and stood in the place where they used to offer their sacrifices, and he found blood there boiling. He asked them: "O Children of Israel, what is the matter with this blood that is boiling? Tell me its story." They said: "This is the blood of a sacrifice of ours that we offered, but it was not accepted from us. That is why it boils. We have been offering sacrifices for eight hundred years, and they were accepted from us, except for this one." He said: "You have not told me the truth." They said: "If it were like the earliest times of ours, it would have been accepted from us. But kingship, prophethood, and revelation have been cut off from us, and that is why it was not accepted from us." So Biyurzadhan slaughtered seven hundred and seventy pairs of their leaders on that blood, but it did not subside. Then he ordered that seven hundred boys from among them be brought, and he slaughtered them on the blood, but it did not subside. Then he ordered seven thousand of their elders and their wives to be brought, and he slaughtered them on the blood, but it did not cool. When Biyurzadhan saw that the blood did not subside, he said to them: "O Children of Israel, woe to you! Tell me the truth and be patient with the command of your Lord. You have ruled on earth for a long time, doing whatever you wished before I leave not a single fire-blower, male or female, among you without killing him." When they saw the hardship and the severity of the killing, they told the truth. They said: "This blood is the blood of a prophet who used to forbid us many things that anger God. If we had obeyed him in them, it would have been more right for us. He used to inform us of your affair, but we did not believe him, so we killed him. This is his blood." Biyurzadhan said to them: "What was his name?" They said: "Yahya ibn Zakariyya." He said: "Now you have told me the truth. For something like this your Lord has taken vengeance upon you." When Biyurzadhan saw that they had told him the truth, he fell down in prostration and said to those around him: "Close the gates of the city, and expel those from Khardush's army who are here, and leave the Children of Israel alone." Then he said: "O Yahya ibn Zakariyya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you, and what has been killed of them. So be still, by the permission of your Lord, before I leave not a single one of your people." The blood subsided by God's permission. Biyurzadhan lifted the killing from them and said: "I believe in what the Children of Israel believe in, and I am certain that there is no lord other than Him." He said to the Children of Israel: "Khardush commanded me to kill among you until your blood flows in the middle of his camp, and I am not able to disobey him." They said to him: "Do what you have been commanded." So he ordered them, and they dug a trench. He ordered that their livestock, including horses, mules, donkeys, camels, cattle, and sheep, be brought, and he slaughtered them until the blood flowed through the camp. He ordered that the dead who had been killed earlier be thrown onto the animals that had been slaughtered. Khardush did not think otherwise than that what was in the trench was the Children of Israel. When the blood reached his camp, he sent to Biyurzadhan: "Lift the killing from them."

Then he turned back to Babil, having nearly annihilated the Children of Israel, or having done so [[The bracketed phrase "to annihilate them" is absent from manuscript "B".]]. This was the final calamity that God sent upon the Children of Israel, and it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿You will surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾. The first calamity was at the hands of Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his armies, and the second at the hands of Khurdawsh and his armies [[The bracketed phrase "and the second at the hands of Khurdawsh and his armies" is absent from manuscript "B".]]. The second was the greater of the two. After that, no banner of theirs was raised again, and rule over the Levant (al-Sham) and its surrounding regions passed to the Greek Romans (al-Rum al-Yunaniyya), except that remnants of the Children of Israel multiplied, and they held leadership in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and its surroundings, though not as rulers. They lived in prosperity until they altered their ways and introduced innovations. So God set over them Tatyus ibn Isbayanus al-Rumi (Titus, son of Vespasian), who laid waste their lands and expelled them from them. God stripped them of sovereignty and leadership, and abasement was imposed upon them. Wherever they were among nations, they bore humiliation and the poll tax (jizya). Bayt al-Maqdis remained in ruins until the days of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the Muslims rebuilt it at his command.

Qatada said: God sent Jalut (Goliath) against them in the first calamity, and he took captives, killed, and destroyed. ﴿Then We gave you back your turn over them﴾, meaning in the time of Dawud (David). Then, when the promise of the last [calamity] came, God sent Bukhtnassar against them, and he took captives and destroyed. Then He said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾, so God returned to them with mercy. Then the people returned to the worst of their former conduct, so God sent against them whatever He willed of His vengeance and punishment. Then God sent the Arabs against them, as He said: ﴿And when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would afflict them with the worst torment﴾. So they remain under torment until the Day of Resurrection.

As-Suddi related with his chain of narration that a man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis would be at the hands of a young orphan, the son of a widow, from the people of Babil, called Bukhtnassar. They used to be truthful in their dreams, so their dreams came true. He set out to inquire about him until he came down upon his mother while he was gathering firewood. He came with a bundle of wood on his head, threw it down, sat, spoke with him, and then gave him three dirhams, saying: "Buy food and drink with this." He bought meat with one dirham, bread with one dirham, and wine with one dirham. They ate and drank. He did the same on the second day, and on the third day as well. Then he said: "I wish that you would write me a safe-conduct (aman), in case you ever become king one day." [The man] said: "Are you mocking me?" He replied: "I am not mocking you, but what harm is it for you to do me a kindness?" So he wrote him a safe-conduct. Bukhtnassar said: "Tell me, if I come while the people are around you and they stand between me and you, how will you recognize me?" He said: "Raise your document on a reed, and I will recognize you." So he wrote it for him and gave it to him.

Then the king of the Children of Israel honored Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John son of Zechariah) and brought him close to his council. He fell in love with the daughter of his wife, and Ibn Abbas said: "the daughter of his sister." He asked Yahya ibn Zakariyya about marrying her, and Yahya forbade him from marrying her. This reached her mother, who harbored resentment against Yahya ibn Zakariyya. When the king sat down to drink, she deliberately dressed her daughter in thin red garments, perfumed her, adorned her with jewelry, and sent her to the king, ordering her to pour him drinks. If he wanted her for herself, she was to refuse him until he gave her what she asked. When he gave it, she was to request that the head of Yahya ibn Zakariyya be brought to her on a basin (tast). She did so. When he approached her, she said: "I will not do it until you give me what I ask of you." He said: "What do you ask of me?" She said: "The head of Yahya ibn Zakariyya on this basin." He said: "Woe to you! Ask me for something other than this." She said: "I want nothing but this." When he refused her, he sent for it, and his head was brought and placed before him while the head was still speaking and saying: "It is not lawful for you." In the morning, his blood was boiling, so he ordered dirt to be thrown upon it. The blood rose, meaning it climbed up, boiling, and dirt kept being thrown on it until it reached the wall of the city, and it was still boiling.

Then Sakhabin, king of Babil, sent an army against them and appointed Bukhtnassar as its commander. Bukhtnassar and his companions marched until they reached that place. [The people] had fortified themselves in their cities against him. When the siege became severe for them, he wished to return. An old woman from among the old women of the Children of Israel came out to him and said: "Do you want to return before taking the city?" He said: "Yes, my stay has been long and my companions are hungry." She said: "What do you think? If I open the city for you, will you give me what I ask? Will you kill whomever I order you to kill, and will you refrain when I order you to refrain?" He said: "Yes." She said: "In the morning, divide your army into four quarters, and station a quarter at each corner. Then raise your hands to the sky and call out: 'We ask You to grant us victory, O God, by the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya.' It will surely collapse." They did so, and the city collapsed, and they entered from its sides. She said: "Hold your hand," and she took him to the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya and said: "Kill upon this blood until it subsides." He killed upon it seventy thousand until it subsided. When it subsided, she said: "Hold your hand, for God is not pleased that when a prophet is killed, anyone should be slain except the one who killed him and the one who was pleased with his killing." The bearer of the document (sahib al-sahifa) came to him with his document, and he refrained from them and from the people of his household. He then destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and threw carrion into it. The Romans assisted him in its destruction, because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya. He also took away with him the notables of the Children of Israel, and took Daniel and a group of the sons of the prophets. He took with him the head of Jalut as well. When he arrived in Babil, he found that Sakhabin had died, so he became king in his place. The most honored people in his presence were Daniel and his companions. The Magians envied them and denounced them to him, saying: "Daniel and his companions do not worship your god, and they do not eat your slaughtered animals." He asked them, and they said: "Indeed, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat of your slaughter." The king ordered a trench to be dug for them, and they were thrown into it. There were six of them. He also threw in with them a ferocious beast to devour them. They went away, then returned in the morning and found them sitting, with the beast stretched out its forelegs beside them, not having scratched any of them. They also found with them a seventh man. He said: "What is this seventh? There were only six of them." The seventh came out, and he was an angel. He struck him a slap, so [Bukhtnassar] was among the wild beasts, and God transformed him for seven years.

Wahb related that God transformed Bukhtnassar into an eagle among birds, then transformed him into a bull among domestic animals, then transformed him into a lion among wild beasts. His transformation lasted seven years, while his heart remained a human heart throughout. Then God returned his kingdom to him, and he believed. Wahb was asked: "Was he a believer?" He said: "I found that the People of the Book disagreed about him. Some said he was a believer, and others said he burned Bayt al-Maqdis and its scriptures and killed the prophets, so God became angry with him and did not accept his repentance."

As-Suddi said: When Bukhtnassar returned to his form after the transformation, and God restored his kingdom to him, Daniel and his companions were the most honored people in his sight. The Magians envied them and said to Bukhtnassar: "When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot control himself from urinating," and this was considered a disgrace among them. So [the king] prepared food and drink for them, and they ate and drank. He told the doorkeeper: "Watch for the first one who comes out to urinate, and strike him with the tabarzin (a heavy mace). If he says, 'I am Bukhtnassar,' say, 'You lie, Bukhtnassar ordered me.'" The first to rise to urinate was Bukhtnassar. When the doorkeeper saw him, he attacked him. [Bukhtnassar] said: "Woe to you! I am Bukhtnassar." He replied: "You lie, Bukhtnassar ordered me," and he struck him and killed him.

This is what was mentioned in al-Mubtada' (The Beginning, a historical work). However, the report of those who narrated that Bukhtnassar raided the Children of Israel at the time they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya is an error according to the scholars of biographical history (ahl al-siyar). Rather, they unanimously agree that Bukhtnassar only raided the Children of Israel when they killed Shi'ya' (Isaiah) in the time of Armiya' (Jeremiah). From the time of Armiya' and Bukhtnassar's destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis until the birth of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was four hundred and sixty-one years. [The people] used to count from the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis by Bukhtnassar until its rebuilding in the time of Kirash ibn Akhshurash ibn Usayhid in Babil, under Bahman ibn Isfandiyar [seventy years]. Then from its rebuilding until Alexander's conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis was eighty-eight years. Then from his rule until the birth of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was three hundred and sixty years [[The bracketed phrase is absent from manuscript "B".]].

The sound view on this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned.

His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book﴾, meaning: We informed them and told them, through the scriptures We gave them, that they would cause corruption.

Qada' (decree) has several meanings. It can mean command, as in His saying: "And your Lord has decreed" [al-Isra': 23]. It can mean judgment, as in His saying: "Indeed, your Lord will judge between them" [Yunus: 93; al-Nahl: 78]. It can mean creation, as in His saying: "And He completed them as seven heavens" [Fussilat: 12].

Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: it means "And We decreed against them," and "ila" here has the meaning of "ala" (upon). By "the Book" is meant the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿You will surely﴾: the lam here is the lam of oath, its meaning being "By God, you will surely." ﴿cause corruption in the land twice﴾ through sins. By "the land" is meant the land of al-Sham and Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿And you will surely become haughty﴾, meaning you will be arrogant and will surely wrong people, ﴿with great arrogance﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 2–4 (part 1 of 4):

The words of the Most High, ﴿And We gave Musa the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, that﴾, meaning, "that," ﴿do not take besides Me a trustee﴾, meaning, a lord and a guardian.

Abu 'Amr read "لَا يَتَّخِذُوا" (la yattakhidhu, "they should not take") with the yā' (ي), because it is a report about them. The others read it with the tā' (ت), meaning: "We said to them, 'Do not take.'"

﴿Offspring of those whom We carried﴾. Mujahid said: this is a form of address, meaning, "O offspring of those whom We carried ﴿with Nuh﴾ in the ship, so We saved them from the flood. ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾." Nuh, peace be upon him, when he ate food, drank a drink, or wore a garment, would say: "Al-hamdu lillah" (all praise is for Allah). So he was named "a grateful servant," meaning one who gives abundant thanks.[[Narrated by Ibn Jarir, 15/19, from Salman, Mujahid, Qatadah and others. Al-Hakim authenticated it according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, 2/360. Al-Suyuti mentioned a number of reports on this, see al-Durr al-Manthur, 5/236–237. Imam Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a meal or drinks a drink and praises Allah for it." In al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith of intercession, he said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection..." and in it: "They will come to Nuh and say: 'O Nuh, you are the first of the messengers to the people of the earth, and Allah has named you a grateful servant. So intercede for us with your Lord.'" And he mentioned the whole hadith.]]

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture﴾, and the verses.

Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:[[Narrated by al-Tabari. See al-Tafsir, 15/22–43; Tarikh al-Tabari, 1/532–557; al-Durr al-Manthur, 5/243–244. These numerous reports that the author, may Allah have mercy on him, cites concerning those who were empowered over the Children of Israel are among the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Jewish and Christian sources) and fabrications. They contain wonders, oddities and exaggerations that are not credible, and some of them may also be true. Ibn Jarir narrated much of this from Ibn Ishaq, and it is clear that Ibn Ishaq explicitly names the People of the Book, saying that they say such-and-such, or that they have such-and-such. We are sufficient without all of these reports. Here we place a valuable statement of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, as a commentary on these reports. He said: "The exegetes, from the early and later generations, have differed about who these empowered enemies were. From Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah it is related that it was Jalut (Goliath) and his armies. From Sa'id ibn Jubayr it is related that it was the king of Mosul, Sinjarib, and his armies. Also from him: it was Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), king of Babylon. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned a strange story about how he rose from one condition to another until he ruled the lands..." Then Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Jarir has narrated in this place a hadith with a chain going back to Hudhayfah, raised to the Prophet, a lengthy one, which is the hadith that al-Baghawi cites here, and it is undoubtedly a fabricated hadith. Anyone with even a little knowledge of hadith would not doubt this. How strange it is, with all his stature and leadership, that it was accepted by him! Our teacher, the Hafiz, the scholar Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, may Allah have mercy on him, declared it fabricated and false, and wrote this in the margin of the book." Then he said, pointing to the rest of the reports: "Many Isra'ili reports have come in this matter, but I did not see fit to lengthen the book by mentioning them, because some of them are fabrications invented by some of their heretics, and some of them may possibly be true. We are sufficient without them, praise be to Allah. What Allah has related to us in His Book suffices us over all other books before it, and neither Allah nor His Messenger has made us in need of them. Allah has informed us about them: that when they transgressed and rebelled, Allah sent their enemy against them, who plundered their domain, went through the inner parts of their houses, and humiliated and subdued them, as a fitting recompense, and your Lord is not unjust to the servants, because they had rebelled and killed a multitude of prophets and scholars. Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Bukhtnassar prevailed over al-Sham, destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and killed them. Then he came to Damascus and found there blood boiling on a rock, and he asked them what this blood was... so seventy thousand of the Muslims and others were killed over that blood, and it became calm. This chain is authentic up to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and this is the well-known account, that he killed their nobles and scholars until no one remained who had memorized the Torah, and he took with him from them captives, including sons of prophets and others. Many events and occurrences took place, which would take long to mention. Had we found something authentic or close to authentic, it would be permissible to write and narrate it. And Allah knows best."[[See also: al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahbah, pp. 327–334.]]

"Indeed, when the Children of Israel transgressed and killed the prophets, Allah sent against them the king of Persia, 'Bukhtnassar,' and Allah had given him kingship for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Bayt al-Maqdis, besieged it, conquered it, and killed seventy thousand over the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon him. Then he took its people captive [and the children],[[Omitted from manuscript "B".]] and plundered the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and extracted from it seventy thousand and one hundred thousand golden bracelets' worth of ornaments." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, was Bayt al-Maqdis great?" He said: "Yes. Sulayman ibn Dawud built it of gold, silver, rubies and chrysolite, and its pillars were of gold. Allah granted him that, and subjected the devils to him, who brought him these things in the blink of an eye. Bukhtnassar carried them away until he settled in Babylon. The Children of Israel remained in his hand for one hundred years, enslaved by the Magians and the sons of the Magians, and among them were prophets. Then Allah had mercy on them, and revealed to a king of the kings of Persia called 'Kurash,' who was a believer, that he should march to them to rescue the remnant of the Children of Israel. So Kurash marched to the Children of Israel and seized the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis and returned them to it. The Children of Israel then remained there, obedient to Allah the Exalted, for one hundred years. Then they returned to sins, so Allah empowered over them a king called 'Antaniyus,' who raided the Children of Israel until he came to them at Bayt al-Maqdis, took its people captive, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis. He said to them: 'O Children of Israel, if you return to sins, we will return against you a second time [with captivity].'[[Addition in manuscript "B".]] They returned, so Allah empowered over them the king of Rome called 'Faqis ibn Astiyanus,' who raided them by land and sea, took them captive, took the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is part of the description of the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Mahdi will return them to Bayt al-Maqdis, by means of one thousand seven hundred ships which will be cast upon Yafa until they are transported to Bayt al-Maqdis, and by it Allah will gather the first and the last."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The Children of Israel had among them misdeeds and sins, and Allah was overlooking them and doing good to them. The first thing that befell them because of their sins, as Allah informed through the tongue of Musa, peace be upon him, was that a king among them called "Sidiqah"[[In the original it is with the hā' (ه); in al-Tabari it is with the tā' marbuta (ة).]] ruled. Whenever Allah made a king rule over them, He sent with him a prophet to support and guide him. He did not send them new scriptures; rather, they were commanded to follow the Torah and the rulings in it.

When that king ruled, Allah sent with him "Sha'ya' ibn Asfiya," and that was before the mission of Zakariyya, Yahya and 'Isa, peace be upon them all. Sha'ya' is the one who gave glad tidings of 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. He said: "Rejoice, O Jerusalem, now there comes to you the rider on the donkey, and after him the owner of the camel." That king ruled the Children of Israel and Bayt al-Maqdis for a time. When his reign ended, misdeeds grew widespread among them, while Sha'ya' was still with them. Allah sent against them "Sinjarib"[[In the history of al-Tabari it is "Sanhârib" with the unpointed h.]] king of Babylon, with six hundred thousand banners. He advanced until he camped around Bayt al-Maqdis, while the king was ill with an ulcer in his leg. The prophet Sha'ya' came to him and said: "O king of the Children of Israel, Sinjarib king of Babylon has descended upon you with his armies, six hundred thousand banners, and the people have been frightened and scattered." This weighed heavily on the king, and he said: "O prophet of Allah, has any revelation come to you from Allah about what has happened, so that you may inform us how Allah will deal with us and with Sinjarib and his armies?"

He said: "No revelation has come to me." While they were in that state, Allah revealed to the prophet Sha'ya': "Go to the king of the Children of Israel and command him to make his will, and to appoint as successor over his kingdom whomever he wishes from among his family." So Sha'ya' came to the king of the Children of Israel, "Sidiqah," and said to him: "Your Lord has revealed to me that I should command you to make your will and to appoint as successor over your kingdom whomever you wish from among your family, for you are dying." When Sha'ya' said that to Sidiqah, he turned toward the qiblah, prayed, supplicated and wept, and he said while weeping, humbling himself before Allah with a sincere heart: "O Allah, Lord of lords and God of gods, O Holy One of the Holy, O Compassionate, O Merciful, O Kind, O You whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, remember me for my deed and my conduct and my good judgment over the Children of Israel. All of that was from You, and You know it better than I do. My secret and my open affairs are for You, and You are the Compassionate." So He responded to him, for he was a righteous servant. Allah the Exalted revealed to Sha'ya' that he should inform Sidiqah that his Lord had responded to him, had shown him mercy, had postponed his term by fifteen years, and had saved him from his enemy Sinjarib. Sha'ya' came to him and informed him of that. When he told him, the pain departed from him, the sorrow left him, and he fell down in prostration and said: "O my God and God of my fathers, to You I prostrate, and I glorify, magnify and exalt You. You are the One who gives kingship to whom You will, and strips kingship from whom You will, honors whom You will, and humbles whom You will. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You are the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and You are merciful and You answer the prayer of the distressed. You are the One who answered my prayer and had mercy on my humble supplication."

When he lifted his head, Allah revealed to Sha'ya': "Say to the king Sidiqah: he should command one of his servants to bring him fig water, and he should put it on his ulcer, and he will be healed; he will wake in the morning and he will be cured." [205/b] He did so, and was healed.

The king said to Sha'ya': "Ask your Lord to give us knowledge of what He will do with this enemy of ours."

Allah said to Sha'ya': "Tell him: I have sufficed you against your enemy and saved you from them, and they will all become dead by morning, except Sinjarib and five men of his scribes."

When they woke in the morning, a crier came and cried out at the gate of the city: "O king of the Children of Israel, Allah has sufficed you against your enemy, so go out, for Sinjarib and those with him have perished." When the king went out, he searched for Sinjarib but did not find him among the dead. The king sent men to seek him, and the seekers found him in a cave with five of his scribes, one of whom was Bukhtnassar. They brought them to the Children of Israel's king in chains. When he saw them, he fell down in prostration from sunrise until the afternoon prayer. Then he said to Sinjarib: "How do you see the action of our Lord toward you? Did He not kill you by His power and might, while we and you were heedless?" Sinjarib said to him: "The news of your Lord and His victory for you has reached me, and of His mercy by which He had mercy on you before I went out from my land. I did not obey a guide, and nothing cast me into misery except [humiliation in this world and punishment in the Hereafter]. If I had listened or understood, I would not have attacked you."

Sidiqah said: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has sufficed us against you as He willed. Our Lord did not let you and those with you remain out of honor for you before your Lord; rather He let you and those with you remain only so that you would increase in misery in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, and so that you would inform those behind you of what you saw of the action of our Lord toward you, and warn those after you. Had it not been for that, He would have killed you. Your blood and the blood of those with you is less valuable to Allah than the blood of a tick, even if you had been killed."

Then the king of the Children of Israel ordered the commander of his guard, who fastened collars (al-jawami') around their necks and paraded them for seventy days around Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and Iliya. He gave each man of them two loaves of barley bread each day.

Sennacherib (Sanjarib) said to the king of the Children of Israel: "Death is better than what you are doing to us." So the king sent them to the prison of death. Then God revealed to Sha'ya (Isaiah), peace be upon him: "Tell the king of the Children of Israel: Let Sennacherib and those with him go forth to warn those behind them, and let him honour them, carry them, until they reach their lands." Sha'ya conveyed this to the king, and [the king, Siddiqa,] did as he was commanded. Sennacherib and those with him set out until they came to Babylon (Babil). When they arrived, he gathered the people and informed them how God had dealt with his armies. His soothsayers (kuhhan) and sorcerers (sahara) said to him: "O king of Babylon, we used to relate to you the news of their Lord, the news of their prophet, and the revelation God sent to their prophet, but you did not obey us. They are a nation that no one can withstand with their Lord." The affair of Sennacherib was a warning for them; then God sufficed them, as a reminder and a lesson.

After that, Sennacherib remained for seven years, then died. Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), the son of his son, was made his successor, doing as his grandfather had done. He remained for seventeen years. Then God took the soul of the king of the Children of Israel, Siddiqa. The affairs of the Children of Israel fell into disorder, they competed for kingship until some of them killed others, and their prophet Sha'ya was with them, but they would not accept from him.

When they did this, God said to Sha'ya: "Stand among your people; I will reveal through your tongue." So when the prophet Sha'ya stood up, God made his tongue speak the revelation. He said: "O heaven, hear! O earth, be silent! For God wishes to recount the affair of the Children of Israel, whom He nurtured with His favour, chose for Himself, singled out with His honour, and preferred over His servants. They are like sheep scattered without a shepherd. He gathered their strays, collected their lost ones, set their broken bones, healed their sick, fattened their emaciated ones, and guarded their fat ones. But when He did this, they became arrogant, and their rams butted one another until some of them killed others, until no sound bone remained to which a broken one could be set. Woe to this sinful nation who do not know from where good has come to them! The camel remembers its homeland and so returns to it; the donkey remembers the pasture on which it was fed and so goes back to it; the bull remembers the meadow in which it grew fat and so returns to it. Yet these people do not remember from where good has come to them. They are people of intellect and understanding; they are neither cattle nor donkeys. I will strike for them a parable, so let them listen. Say to them: What do you think of a land that was empty for a time, desolate, dead, without any habitation, and it had a Lord, wise and mighty, who turned to it with cultivation, disliked that His land should be ruined while He was mighty, or that it should be said He was negligent while He was wise? So He surrounded it with a wall, built palaces in it, dug a river, planted in it saplings of olives, pomegranates, date palms, grapes, and all kinds of fruits, and entrusted that to a man of judgement and resolve, a vigilant, strong, trustworthy guardian. But when it blossomed, its blossom bore carob (kharrub) instead."

They said: "Evil is this land. We see that its wall and palace should be demolished, its river filled in, its guardian dismissed, and its plants burned, until it becomes as it was at first: desolate, dead, without habitation." God said: He said to them: "The wall is My religion; the palace is My law; the river is My Book; the guardian is My prophet; the plants are they (the people); and the carob that bore the plants is their evil deeds. I have decreed against them the judgement they passed against themselves. This is a parable I have coined for them: they draw near to Me by slaughtering cattle and sheep, yet meat does not reach Me, nor do I eat it; and they neglect to draw near to Me by piety and refraining from slaying the souls I have forbidden. Their hands are stained with them, and their garments are soaked with their blood. They build houses for Me as mosques and purify their insides, yet they defile their hearts and bodies and soil them; they adorn the mosques for Me and beautify them, yet they ruin their minds and dreams and corrupt them. What need have I of building houses when I do not dwell in them? What need have I of adorning mosques when I do not enter them? I only commanded that they be raised so that I might be remembered and glorified therein."

They say: "We fasted, but our fasting was not raised; we prayed, but our prayer was not illuminated [and we prayed, but our prayer was not made luminous]; we gave charity, but our charity was not purified; we called upon Him like the moaning of doves and wept like the howling of wolves, yet in all of this we are not answered."

God said: "Ask them: what prevents Me from responding to them? Am I not the Hearer of hearers, the Seer of seers, the Nearest of those who respond, and the Most Merciful of the merciful? How can I raise their fasting when they clothe it with false speech and strengthen themselves by it through unlawful food? Or how can I illuminate their prayer when their hearts incline toward one who wars against Me, opposes Me, and violates My sanctities? Or how can their charities be purified before Me when they give charity from the wealth of others? Rather, I reward its owners, who were wronged. Or how can I respond to their supplication, when it is only words on their tongues, while action is far from it? I only respond to the one who calls humbly, and I only hear the words of the modest, needy one; and among the signs of My pleasure is the pleasure of the needy."

They say when they hear My words and My message reaches them: "These are transmitted sayings and inherited narratives, a composition of the kind sorcerers and soothsayers compose." They claim that if they wished they could bring a discourse like it, and if they wished they could gain knowledge of the unseen through what the devils reveal to them, they would have attained it. I have decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth a decree that I affirmed and made binding upon Myself, and I placed before it a term, appointed, which must certainly come to pass. So if they are truthful in what they claim of knowledge of the unseen, let them tell you when I shall execute it, or in what time it will occur. If they are able to bring about whatever they wish, let them bring the like of this power by which I have enacted it, for I shall make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it. And if they are able to say whatever they wish, let them say the like of the wisdom by which I manage the execution of that decree, if they are truthful. I decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth that I would place prophethood among hired labourers, sovereignty among shepherds, honour among the humble, strength among the weak, wealth among the poor, knowledge among the ignorant, and wisdom among the unlettered. So ask them: when will this be, who will carry it out, and who are the helpers and supporters of this matter, if they know? I shall raise for this a prophet, unlettered, trustworthy, neither harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets, nor adorned with obscenity, nor one who speaks foul words. I shall guide him to every goodness and bestow upon him every noble character. I shall make tranquillity his garment, righteousness his inner garment, piety his inner consciousness, wisdom his understanding, truthfulness and fidelity his nature, pardon and kindness his character, justice his conduct, [truth his law,] guidance and [the Qur'an] his leader, Islam his creed, and Ahmad his name. Through him I shall guide after error, teach after ignorance, raise after obscurity, make famous after anonymity, increase after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and join together hearts that are at odds, desires that are scattered, and nations that are dispersed. I shall make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, in affirmation of My oneness, faith, and sincerity toward Me. They will pray standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating; they will fight in My cause in ranks and in waves; they will leave their homes and their wealth seeking My good pleasure. I shall inspire them with glorification (takbir), declaration of oneness (tawhid), praise of Me (tasbih), commendation (tahmid), eulogy, and exaltation (tamjid) in their journeys, their gatherings, their resting places, their places of rising, and their abodes. They will proclaim takbir, tahlil, and taqdis upon the heights; they will purify their faces and extremities for Me; they will fold their garments in the middle. Their offering is their blood, and their Gospels are in their chests. They are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I bestow on whom I will, and I am the Lord of Great Bounty."

When Sha'ya finished his speech, they rushed upon him to kill him. He fled from them, and a tree met him and split open for him, so he entered it. Satan overtook him and seized a fringe of his garment, and he showed it to them. They placed the saw in the middle of the tree and sawed it until they cut it through, and they cut him in its middle.

After that, God appointed over the Children of Israel a man from among them called Nashiya ibn Amus, and He sent to them Irmiya (Jeremiah) ibn Hilqiya as a prophet. He was from the tribe of Harun ibn Imran.

Ibn Ishaq mentioned that he was al-Khidr, and his name was Irmiya. He was called al-Khidr because he sat on a white patch of ground, then rose from it, and it was trembling green.

So God sent Irmiya (Jeremiah) to that king to guide and direct him. Then the transgressions among the Children of Israel grew great. They indulged in sins and made lawful what God had forbidden. God revealed to Irmiya: "Go to your people, the Children of Israel. Relate to them what I command you, remind them of My blessings, and inform them of their misdeeds." Irmiya said: "My Lord, I am weak unless You strengthen me. I am incapable unless You convey (the message) through me. I am forsaken unless You support me." God, exalted is He, said: "Do you not know that all affairs proceed from My will, and that hearts and tongues are in My hand? I turn them as I wish. Indeed, I am with you, and nothing will reach you while I am with you." Irmiya stood among them, not knowing what to say, so God inspired him at that moment with an eloquent sermon in which he explained the reward of obedience and the punishment of disobedience. At the end of it he said, on behalf of God, exalted is He: "I have sworn by My might that I will bring upon them a trial in which the forbearing will be bewildered, and I will set over them a tyrannical, harsh ruler. I will clothe him in awe and remove mercy from his heart. A host like the blackness of the dark night will follow him."

Then God revealed to Irmiya: "I am going to destroy the Children of Israel through Yafith, and Yafith is from the people of Babil (Babylon), as we mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah." So God set over them Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar). He set out with six hundred thousand banners, entered Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) with his armies, trod upon al-Sham (Greater Syria), and killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them. He destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and ordered each of his soldiers to fill his shield with dirt and then hurl it into Bayt al-Maqdis. They did so until they had filled it. Then he ordered them to gather everyone in the towns around Bayt al-Maqdis, and every young and old person among the Children of Israel assembled before him. He selected from them seventy thousand boys.
