When the spoils of his army were brought out and he wished to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said to him: "O king, all the spoils are yours. Divide among us these boys whom you have chosen from the Children of Israel." So he distributed them among the kings who were with him, and each man received four young boys. He divided the remaining Children of Israel into three groups: one third he settled in al-Sham, one third he took captive, and one third he killed. He took the young men of Bayt al-Maqdis and the seventy thousand boys with him until he brought them to Babil. This was the first calamity that God sent upon the Children of Israel because of their wrongdoing. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might﴾, meaning Bukhtansar and his companions.

Then Bukhtansar remained in his rule for as long as God willed. Then he saw a dream that amazed him, for he saw something that troubled him, but God made him forget what he had seen. He summoned Daniyal (Daniel), Hananiya, Azaraya, and Mishaʾil, who were descendants of the prophets, and asked them about it. They said: "Tell us the dream, and we will tell you its interpretation." He said: "I do not remember it. If you do not tell me it and its interpretation, I will surely tear off your shoulders." So they left him and called upon God and humbled themselves before Him, and God informed them of what he had asked them about. They came to him and said: "You saw a statue whose feet and shins were of clay, whose knees and thighs were of bronze, whose belly was of silver, whose chest was of gold, and whose head and neck were of iron." He said: "You have spoken truly." They said: "While you were looking at it and it pleased you, God sent down a rock from the sky, which shattered it. That is what made you forget it." He said: "You have spoken truly." He said: "What is its interpretation?" They said: "Its interpretation is that you saw the kingdoms of the kings. Some of them were softer in rule, some were better in rule, and some were stronger in rule. The clay is the weakest, above it is the bronze, which is stronger than it, above the bronze is the silver, which is better and superior to that, and gold is better and superior to silver. Then the iron is your kingdom, and it is stronger and mightier than what came before it. The rock that you saw, which God sent from the sky and which shattered it, is a prophet whom God will send from the sky, and he will shatter all of that, and the affair will pass to him."

Then the people of Babil said to Bukhtansar: "Have you considered these boys from the Children of Israel whom we asked you to give to us, and you did? We have denied our women since they have been with us. We have seen that our women's faces have turned away from us toward them. So either expel them from among us or kill them." He said: "The matter is yours regarding them. Whoever among you wishes to kill those in his possession, let him do so."

When they brought them out to be killed, they wept to God, exalted is He, and said: "O Lord, we have been afflicted by the sins of others." God promised to answer them. So they were killed, except for those whom Bukhtansar spared from among them: Daniyal, Hananiya, Azaraya, and Mishaʾil.

Then when God intended to destroy Bukhtansar, he rose up and said to those among the Children of Israel who were in his possession: "Have you considered this House that I destroyed, and the people I killed from among them? And what is this House?" They said: "This is the House of God, and these are its people. They were descendants of the prophets, but they committed wrongdoing and transgressed, so you were empowered over them because of their sins. Their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and the Lord of all creation. He honored and strengthened them. When they did what they did, God destroyed them and gave power over them to others. You became arrogant and thought that by your tyranny you did this to the Children of Israel." He said: "Then tell me how I can ascend to the highest heaven, kill whoever is in it, and take it as my kingdom, for I have finished with the earth." They said: "No creature is able to do that." He said: "You will do it, or I will kill you all to the last one." So they wept and humbled themselves before God, exalted is He. Then God, by His power, sent a gnat which entered his nostril until it bit the root of his brain. He could neither stay still nor rest, and his head was struck on the root of his brain until it was split open. When he died, they split open his head and found the gnat biting the root of his brain, so that God might show His servants His power. God delivered those of the Children of Israel who remained in his possession, and they returned them to al-Sham, where they built and multiplied until they were in the best state they had ever been.

They claim that God brought back to life those who had been killed, and they joined them. Then when they entered al-Sham, they entered it without any covenant from God, and the Tawrah (Torah) had been burned. Uzayr (Ezra) was among the captives in Babil, and he returned to al-Sham weeping over it night and day. He had withdrawn from the people. While he was in that state, a man approached him and said: "O Uzayr, what makes you weep?" He said: "I weep over the Book of God and His covenant that was among us, which nothing else can set right for our worldly life and our hereafter." He said: "Would you like it to be returned to you? Go, fast, purify yourself, and purify your garments. Then let your appointment be this place tomorrow." So Uzayr went, fasted, purified himself, and purified his garments. Then he made his way to the place he had been promised and sat there. That man came to him with a vessel containing water, and he was an angel whom God had sent to him. He gave him to drink from that vessel, and the Tawrah took form in his chest. He returned to the Children of Israel and set the Tawrah before them, and they loved him so much that they never loved anything as they loved him. Then God took him, and after that the Children of Israel began to commit misdeeds. God would turn back toward them and send messengers to them, but some they called liars and some they killed. The last of the prophets God sent among them were Zakariyya (Zechariah), Yahya (John), and Isa (Jesus), and they were from the house of Dawud (David). Zakariyya died, though it was also said that Zakariyya was killed. When God raised Isa from among them, and they killed Yahya, God set over them a king from the kings of Babil called Khardush. He marched against them with the people of Babil until he entered al-Sham upon them. When he prevailed over them, he ordered a commander among his soldiers, named Biyurzadhan, who was in charge of killing, and said: "I had sworn by my god that if I prevailed over the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, I would surely kill them until their blood flowed in the middle of my camp. But I do not find anyone to kill." So he ordered him to kill them, until Biyurzadhan reached that point among them. He entered Bayt al-Maqdis and stood in the place where they used to offer their sacrifices, and he found blood there boiling. He asked them: "O Children of Israel, what is the matter with this blood that is boiling? Tell me its story." They said: "This is the blood of a sacrifice of ours that we offered, but it was not accepted from us. That is why it boils. We have been offering sacrifices for eight hundred years, and they were accepted from us, except for this one." He said: "You have not told me the truth." They said: "If it were like the earliest times of ours, it would have been accepted from us. But kingship, prophethood, and revelation have been cut off from us, and that is why it was not accepted from us." So Biyurzadhan slaughtered seven hundred and seventy pairs of their leaders on that blood, but it did not subside. Then he ordered that seven hundred boys from among them be brought, and he slaughtered them on the blood, but it did not subside. Then he ordered seven thousand of their elders and their wives to be brought, and he slaughtered them on the blood, but it did not cool. When Biyurzadhan saw that the blood did not subside, he said to them: "O Children of Israel, woe to you! Tell me the truth and be patient with the command of your Lord. You have ruled on earth for a long time, doing whatever you wished before I leave not a single fire-blower, male or female, among you without killing him." When they saw the hardship and the severity of the killing, they told the truth. They said: "This blood is the blood of a prophet who used to forbid us many things that anger God. If we had obeyed him in them, it would have been more right for us. He used to inform us of your affair, but we did not believe him, so we killed him. This is his blood." Biyurzadhan said to them: "What was his name?" They said: "Yahya ibn Zakariyya." He said: "Now you have told me the truth. For something like this your Lord has taken vengeance upon you." When Biyurzadhan saw that they had told him the truth, he fell down in prostration and said to those around him: "Close the gates of the city, and expel those from Khardush's army who are here, and leave the Children of Israel alone." Then he said: "O Yahya ibn Zakariyya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you, and what has been killed of them. So be still, by the permission of your Lord, before I leave not a single one of your people." The blood subsided by God's permission. Biyurzadhan lifted the killing from them and said: "I believe in what the Children of Israel believe in, and I am certain that there is no lord other than Him." He said to the Children of Israel: "Khardush commanded me to kill among you until your blood flows in the middle of his camp, and I am not able to disobey him." They said to him: "Do what you have been commanded." So he ordered them, and they dug a trench. He ordered that their livestock, including horses, mules, donkeys, camels, cattle, and sheep, be brought, and he slaughtered them until the blood flowed through the camp. He ordered that the dead who had been killed earlier be thrown onto the animals that had been slaughtered. Khardush did not think otherwise than that what was in the trench was the Children of Israel. When the blood reached his camp, he sent to Biyurzadhan: "Lift the killing from them."

Then he turned back to Babil, having nearly annihilated the Children of Israel, or having done so [[The bracketed phrase "to annihilate them" is absent from manuscript "B".]]. This was the final calamity that God sent upon the Children of Israel, and it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿You will surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾. The first calamity was at the hands of Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his armies, and the second at the hands of Khurdawsh and his armies [[The bracketed phrase "and the second at the hands of Khurdawsh and his armies" is absent from manuscript "B".]]. The second was the greater of the two. After that, no banner of theirs was raised again, and rule over the Levant (al-Sham) and its surrounding regions passed to the Greek Romans (al-Rum al-Yunaniyya), except that remnants of the Children of Israel multiplied, and they held leadership in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and its surroundings, though not as rulers. They lived in prosperity until they altered their ways and introduced innovations. So God set over them Tatyus ibn Isbayanus al-Rumi (Titus, son of Vespasian), who laid waste their lands and expelled them from them. God stripped them of sovereignty and leadership, and abasement was imposed upon them. Wherever they were among nations, they bore humiliation and the poll tax (jizya). Bayt al-Maqdis remained in ruins until the days of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the Muslims rebuilt it at his command.

Qatada said: God sent Jalut (Goliath) against them in the first calamity, and he took captives, killed, and destroyed. ﴿Then We gave you back your turn over them﴾, meaning in the time of Dawud (David). Then, when the promise of the last [calamity] came, God sent Bukhtnassar against them, and he took captives and destroyed. Then He said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾, so God returned to them with mercy. Then the people returned to the worst of their former conduct, so God sent against them whatever He willed of His vengeance and punishment. Then God sent the Arabs against them, as He said: ﴿And when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would afflict them with the worst torment﴾. So they remain under torment until the Day of Resurrection.

As-Suddi related with his chain of narration that a man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis would be at the hands of a young orphan, the son of a widow, from the people of Babil, called Bukhtnassar. They used to be truthful in their dreams, so their dreams came true. He set out to inquire about him until he came down upon his mother while he was gathering firewood. He came with a bundle of wood on his head, threw it down, sat, spoke with him, and then gave him three dirhams, saying: "Buy food and drink with this." He bought meat with one dirham, bread with one dirham, and wine with one dirham. They ate and drank. He did the same on the second day, and on the third day as well. Then he said: "I wish that you would write me a safe-conduct (aman), in case you ever become king one day." [The man] said: "Are you mocking me?" He replied: "I am not mocking you, but what harm is it for you to do me a kindness?" So he wrote him a safe-conduct. Bukhtnassar said: "Tell me, if I come while the people are around you and they stand between me and you, how will you recognize me?" He said: "Raise your document on a reed, and I will recognize you." So he wrote it for him and gave it to him.

Then the king of the Children of Israel honored Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John son of Zechariah) and brought him close to his council. He fell in love with the daughter of his wife, and Ibn Abbas said: "the daughter of his sister." He asked Yahya ibn Zakariyya about marrying her, and Yahya forbade him from marrying her. This reached her mother, who harbored resentment against Yahya ibn Zakariyya. When the king sat down to drink, she deliberately dressed her daughter in thin red garments, perfumed her, adorned her with jewelry, and sent her to the king, ordering her to pour him drinks. If he wanted her for herself, she was to refuse him until he gave her what she asked. When he gave it, she was to request that the head of Yahya ibn Zakariyya be brought to her on a basin (tast). She did so. When he approached her, she said: "I will not do it until you give me what I ask of you." He said: "What do you ask of me?" She said: "The head of Yahya ibn Zakariyya on this basin." He said: "Woe to you! Ask me for something other than this." She said: "I want nothing but this." When he refused her, he sent for it, and his head was brought and placed before him while the head was still speaking and saying: "It is not lawful for you." In the morning, his blood was boiling, so he ordered dirt to be thrown upon it. The blood rose, meaning it climbed up, boiling, and dirt kept being thrown on it until it reached the wall of the city, and it was still boiling.

Then Sakhabin, king of Babil, sent an army against them and appointed Bukhtnassar as its commander. Bukhtnassar and his companions marched until they reached that place. [The people] had fortified themselves in their cities against him. When the siege became severe for them, he wished to return. An old woman from among the old women of the Children of Israel came out to him and said: "Do you want to return before taking the city?" He said: "Yes, my stay has been long and my companions are hungry." She said: "What do you think? If I open the city for you, will you give me what I ask? Will you kill whomever I order you to kill, and will you refrain when I order you to refrain?" He said: "Yes." She said: "In the morning, divide your army into four quarters, and station a quarter at each corner. Then raise your hands to the sky and call out: 'We ask You to grant us victory, O God, by the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya.' It will surely collapse." They did so, and the city collapsed, and they entered from its sides. She said: "Hold your hand," and she took him to the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya and said: "Kill upon this blood until it subsides." He killed upon it seventy thousand until it subsided. When it subsided, she said: "Hold your hand, for God is not pleased that when a prophet is killed, anyone should be slain except the one who killed him and the one who was pleased with his killing." The bearer of the document (sahib al-sahifa) came to him with his document, and he refrained from them and from the people of his household. He then destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and threw carrion into it. The Romans assisted him in its destruction, because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya. He also took away with him the notables of the Children of Israel, and took Daniel and a group of the sons of the prophets. He took with him the head of Jalut as well. When he arrived in Babil, he found that Sakhabin had died, so he became king in his place. The most honored people in his presence were Daniel and his companions. The Magians envied them and denounced them to him, saying: "Daniel and his companions do not worship your god, and they do not eat your slaughtered animals." He asked them, and they said: "Indeed, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat of your slaughter." The king ordered a trench to be dug for them, and they were thrown into it. There were six of them. He also threw in with them a ferocious beast to devour them. They went away, then returned in the morning and found them sitting, with the beast stretched out its forelegs beside them, not having scratched any of them. They also found with them a seventh man. He said: "What is this seventh? There were only six of them." The seventh came out, and he was an angel. He struck him a slap, so [Bukhtnassar] was among the wild beasts, and God transformed him for seven years.

Wahb related that God transformed Bukhtnassar into an eagle among birds, then transformed him into a bull among domestic animals, then transformed him into a lion among wild beasts. His transformation lasted seven years, while his heart remained a human heart throughout. Then God returned his kingdom to him, and he believed. Wahb was asked: "Was he a believer?" He said: "I found that the People of the Book disagreed about him. Some said he was a believer, and others said he burned Bayt al-Maqdis and its scriptures and killed the prophets, so God became angry with him and did not accept his repentance."

As-Suddi said: When Bukhtnassar returned to his form after the transformation, and God restored his kingdom to him, Daniel and his companions were the most honored people in his sight. The Magians envied them and said to Bukhtnassar: "When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot control himself from urinating," and this was considered a disgrace among them. So [the king] prepared food and drink for them, and they ate and drank. He told the doorkeeper: "Watch for the first one who comes out to urinate, and strike him with the tabarzin (a heavy mace). If he says, 'I am Bukhtnassar,' say, 'You lie, Bukhtnassar ordered me.'" The first to rise to urinate was Bukhtnassar. When the doorkeeper saw him, he attacked him. [Bukhtnassar] said: "Woe to you! I am Bukhtnassar." He replied: "You lie, Bukhtnassar ordered me," and he struck him and killed him.

This is what was mentioned in al-Mubtada' (The Beginning, a historical work). However, the report of those who narrated that Bukhtnassar raided the Children of Israel at the time they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya is an error according to the scholars of biographical history (ahl al-siyar). Rather, they unanimously agree that Bukhtnassar only raided the Children of Israel when they killed Shi'ya' (Isaiah) in the time of Armiya' (Jeremiah). From the time of Armiya' and Bukhtnassar's destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis until the birth of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was four hundred and sixty-one years. [The people] used to count from the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis by Bukhtnassar until its rebuilding in the time of Kirash ibn Akhshurash ibn Usayhid in Babil, under Bahman ibn Isfandiyar [seventy years]. Then from its rebuilding until Alexander's conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis was eighty-eight years. Then from his rule until the birth of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was three hundred and sixty years [[The bracketed phrase is absent from manuscript "B".]].

The sound view on this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned.

His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book﴾, meaning: We informed them and told them, through the scriptures We gave them, that they would cause corruption.

Qada' (decree) has several meanings. It can mean command, as in His saying: "And your Lord has decreed" [al-Isra': 23]. It can mean judgment, as in His saying: "Indeed, your Lord will judge between them" [Yunus: 93; al-Nahl: 78]. It can mean creation, as in His saying: "And He completed them as seven heavens" [Fussilat: 12].

Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: it means "And We decreed against them," and "ila" here has the meaning of "ala" (upon). By "the Book" is meant the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿You will surely﴾: the lam here is the lam of oath, its meaning being "By God, you will surely." ﴿cause corruption in the land twice﴾ through sins. By "the land" is meant the land of al-Sham and Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿And you will surely become haughty﴾, meaning you will be arrogant and will surely wrong people, ﴿with great arrogance﴾.

﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا﴾ *"So when the promise of the first of them came"*. He means: the first of the two times.

Qatadah said: Their corruption in the first time was that they opposed the rulings of the Torah and committed what was forbidden (*al-mahārim*).

Ibn Ishaq said: Their corruption in the first time was the killing of Sha'ya' (Isaiah) between the two trees, and their committing of sins.

﴿بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَنَا﴾ *"We sent against you servants of Ours"*. Qatadah said: This means Jalut al-Khazri (Goliath) and his army, and he is the one whom Dawud (David) killed.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: This means Sanjarib (Sennacherib) from the people of Nineveh.

Ibn Ishaq said: Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar) al-Babili (of Babylon) and his companions. And this is the most apparent view (*al-azhar*).

﴿أُولِي بَأْسٍ﴾ *"possessors of great might"*: possessors of strength. ﴿شَدِيدٍ﴾ *"severe"* in war. ﴿فَجَاسُوا﴾ *"then they went through"*: i.e., they went around and roamed. ﴿خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ﴾ *"between the homes"*: in their midst, seeking you and killing you. *Al-jaws* means seeking a thing with thorough investigation. Al-Farra' said: *jasu* means they killed you among your houses.

﴿وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَفْعُولًا﴾ *"and it was a promise fulfilled"*: a decree that was certain to happen, with no reversal in it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 11–12:

Allah's words, ﴿And man invokes**[**]** (for) evil**[**]**—**[**]**—the waw (و) is elided in pronunciation because of the following unvowelled lam (ل), as in His words, "We will call the guards of Hell" [al-'Alaq: 18]. It is also omitted in the written form, though it is not omitted in meaning. Its meaning is: man invokes (Allah) against his property, his children and himself, ﴿with evil﴾, so that when he is angry he says, "O Allah, curse him and destroy him," and similar words. ﴿As he invokes Him for good﴾, meaning, as he invokes his Lord for good, asking Him to grant him blessing and well-being. If Allah answered his invocation against himself, he would perish, but Allah does not answer it, by His grace. ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾ in invoking against what he dislikes, so that it would be granted to him in that matter. A group of the people of tafsir (exegesis) said, and Ibn 'Abbas said: he is impatient, without patience in ease or in hardship.

His words, Mighty and Majestic be He, ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, meaning two indications pointing to Our existence, Our oneness and Our power. ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah made the light of the sun seventy parts and the light of the moon likewise, then He effaced sixty-nine parts from the light of the moon and placed them with the light of the sun [[Al-Suyuti attributed this to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5 / 248.]].

It is related that Allah commanded Jibril (Gabriel), so he passed his wing over the face of the moon three times, and its brightness was extinguished, while its light remained in it.

Ibn al-Kawwa' asked 'Ali about the blackness that is in the moon, and he said: it is the trace of the effacing [[Ibn Kathir said (3 / 28): Ibn Jarir narrated it through multiple good chains.]].

﴿And We made the sign of the day to be seeing﴾, meaning illuminating and shining, that by it one sees. al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs say "abṣara al-nahār" (the day became visible) when it shines so that one can see by it. ﴿So that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾. Meaning: if Allah had left the sun and the moon as He created them, the night would not be distinguished from the day, the fasting person would not know when to break his fast, the time of the Hajj would not be known, nor the time of the appointed terms, nor the time of rest and repose.

﴿And every thing We have explained in detail﴾.

See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5 / 248.]].

It is related that Allah commanded Jibril (Gabriel), so he passed his wing over the face of the moon three times, and its brightness was extinguished, while its light remained in it.

Ibn al-Kawwa' asked 'Ali about the blackness that is in the moon, and he said: it is the trace of the effacing [[Ibn Kathir said (3 / 28): Ibn Jarir narrated it through multiple good chains.]].

﴿And We made the sign of the day to be seeing﴾, meaning illuminating and shining, that by it one sees. al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs say "abṣara al-nahār" (the day became visible) when it shines so that one can see by it. ﴿So that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾. Meaning: if Allah had left the sun and the moon as He created them, the night would not be distinguished from the day, the fasting person would not know when to break his fast, the time of the Hajj would not be known, nor the time of the appointed terms, nor the time of rest and repose.

﴿And every thing We have explained in detail﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 13–15:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: his deeds, and what has been decreed for him; it is constantly with him wherever he is.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: his good and his evil are with him; it does not leave him until He calls him to account for it.

al-Hasan said: his right-handedness and his ill-omen.

And on the authority of Mujahid: There is no newborn except that on his neck is a scroll in which it is written whether he is wretched or happy.

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: By the "omen" (ta'ir) He meant what God has decreed for him, that he will do it and that he will come to it of happiness or wretchedness. It was called "omen" (ta'ir) according to the custom of the Arabs, in which they took omens and portents from the flights of birds, the ones passing to the right and the ones passing to the left. Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Qutaybi said: By the "omen" He meant his share of good and evil, from their saying: "The arrow of so-and-so flew with such-and-such" (tara sahm fulan bi-kadha). The neck was singled out from among the other limbs because it is the place of necklaces, collars and other things that adorn or disfigure, so the speech of the Arabs came to liken things that are bound to the necks.

﴿And We will bring out for him﴾: God, exalted is He, says: And We will bring out ﴿on the Day of Resurrection a book﴾. al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ya'qub read: "wa-yakhruju lahu" with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ra', meaning: and the omen will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book. Abu Ja'far read "yukhraju" with a ya' and a damma and a fatha on the ra'.

﴿He will meet it﴾: Ibn 'Amir and Abu Ja'far read "yulaqqahu" with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the qaf, meaning: the person will be met by that book, i.e., it will be given to him. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (unshadded), i.e., he will see it ﴿spread open﴾. In the reports: God, exalted is He, commands the angel to fold the scroll when the servant's life is complete, so it is not unfolded until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Read your book﴾: i.e., it will be said to him: Read your book. The saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾, i.e., as one who calls to account. al-Hasan said: Indeed He has been just to you, who made you the reckoner of your own self. Qatadah said: On that Day, whoever was not a reader in the world will read.

﴿Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own soul﴾: for it is its reward. ﴿And whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment﴾: because upon it is its punishment.

﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾: i.e., no bearer shall carry the burden of another's sins; that is, no one is seized for the sin of another.

﴿And We would not punish until We have sent a messenger﴾: as establishing proof and cutting off excuse. And in it is evidence that what is obligatory is made obligatory by revelation (al-sam') and not by reason (al-'aql).

﴿When We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones (mutrafeehaa), and they defiantly transgress therein; then the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it utterly.﴾ Mujahid read "amarna" with a doubled *mim* (*ammarna*), meaning: We gave authority over it to its wicked ones, so they disobeyed. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ya'qub read "aamarna" with a long vowel (*aamarna*), meaning: We increased them (in number).

The rest of the readers (al-Baqun) read it short and single (*maqsuran mukhaffafan*), meaning: We commanded them to obey, so they disobeyed. It may also mean: We made them rulers (*umara'*). It may also carry the sense of "We increased them," as one says: *amarahumu Allah*, meaning "Allah increased them." In a hadith: "The best property is a fruitful mare (*muhrah ma'murah*)," meaning one with many offspring.

[[Narrated by Ibn Sa'd in *al-Tabaqat* (7/56, Dar al-Tahrir edition, Cairo), Imam Ahmad in *al-Musnad* (3/468), al-Bayhaqi in *al-Sunan* (10/64), and the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (10/387). Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shaf* (p. 98): "It was related by Abd ibn Humayd, Ishaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Harith, al-Tabarani and Abu Ubayd, through the narration of Muslim ibn Badil from Iyas ibn Zuhayr from Suwayd ibn Hubayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ)." Al-Haythami said (5/258): "Ahmad and al-Tabarani related it, and the narrators of Ahmad are trustworthy."]] That is, having many offspring. [[Said by Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book *al-Gharib*. See Ibn Kathir (3/34) and al-Bayhaqi (10/64).]] It is said from this root: *amara al-qawmu ya'muruna amran*, when the people became numerous. It is not from *al-amr* (command) in the sense of the verb, for Allah does not command immorality (*al-fahsha'*).

Abu Ubaydah preferred the reading of the majority and said: "Because the three meanings are combined in it," meaning commanding, rulership and abundance.

﴿Mutrafeeha﴾: its affluent ones (*munaʿʿimeeha*) and its wealthy ones (*aghniyaaha*). ﴿So they committed sin therein, and the word became due against it﴾: the punishment became obligatory upon it. ﴿So We destroyed it utterly﴾: that is, We ruined it and destroyed those who were in it.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us; Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that Zaynab bint Abi Salamah narrated to him from Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, from Zaynab bint Jahsh, that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon her frightened, saying: "There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near! Today an opening has been made in the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj like this," and he made a ring with his thumb and the finger next to it. Zaynab said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?' He said: 'Yes, when wickedness increases.'"

[[Related by al-Bukhari in *al-Fitan*, chapter on Ya'juj and Ma'juj (13/106), and Muslim in *al-Fitan wa Ashrat al-Sa'ah*, chapter on the approach of trials and the opening of the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, no. (2880) (4/2207), and the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (14/397).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 17–20:

His saying: ﴿How many generations have We destroyed after Noah﴾, i.e., the generations that denied, warning the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And your Lord is sufficient as one who is Acquainted and Seeing with the sins of His servants﴾. ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Awfa said: "A qarn (generation) is one hundred and twenty years. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent at the beginning of a qarn, and at its end was Yazid ibn Muʿawiyah."

It is also said: a qarn is one hundred years. It was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from ʿAbdullah ibn Busr al-Mazini, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his hand on his head and said: "This boy will live a qarn" [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir: 15/58, and mentioned by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh al-Saghir p. (39), and narrated by Abu Nuʿaym in Maʿrifat al-Sahabah as in al-Tahdhib: 5/139.]]. Muhammad ibn al-Qasim said: "We kept counting for him until he completed one hundred years, and then he died."

al-Kalbi said: eighty years. It is also said: forty years.

﴿Whoever desires the hastening (world), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾, meaning the world, i.e., the hasty abode, ﴿Then We appoint for him Hell, which he will enter, blameworthy and expelled﴾, i.e., driven away and distanced.

﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its striving, while he is a believer, those – their striving will be appreciated﴾, i.e., accepted.

﴿To each – these and those – We extend from the bounty of your Lord﴾, i.e., We provide for both groups, those who desire the world and those who desire the Hereafter, ﴿And the bounty of your Lord is not restricted﴾, i.e., He provides for both of them together, then their states differ in the outcome. ﴿And the bounty of your Lord was not restricted﴾, meaning the provision of your Lord, ﴿forbidden﴾, i.e., withheld from His servants. So the intended "bounty" is the bounty of the world, for the disbelievers have no share in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 21–23:

﴿Look﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿how We have favoured some of them over others﴾ in provision and in deeds [the righteous] [[Omitted from "A".]], meaning: the seeker of the immediate (al-'ajilah) and the seeker of the Hereafter. ﴿And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.﴾ ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is others.

It was also said: its meaning is, O human being, do not set up [with Allah another god] [[Omitted from "A".]] ﴿lest you sit reproached and forsaken﴾: reproached, with no praise; forsaken, with no help. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿And your Lord has decreed﴾, meaning: and your Lord commanded. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Hasan.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: and your Lord made obligatory.

Mujahid said: and your Lord enjoined.

It is related from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim that he recited "wa-wassa rabbuka" (and your Lord charged), and said: they joined the waw to the sad, so it became a qaf [[Ibn al-Jawzi said in "Zad al-Masir" (5/22): This contradicts what has been agreed upon by consensus, so it is not to be heeded. The report was narrated by Ahmad ibn Mani' from Ibn 'Abbas with a weak chain, due to the weakness of Furat ibn al-Sa'ib. It was also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/63) from al-Dahhak, and in its chain is Abu Ishaq al-Kufi, who is 'Abdullah ibn Maysarah al-Harithi, whom Ibn Ma'in, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, al-Nasa'i and al-Daraqutni declared weak. And Hisham, the narrator from this Abu Ishaq, although trustworthy, is described as a mudallis (one who conceals defects), and he narrated this report with 'an'anah (using 'from'). See: al-Matalib al-'Aliyah 3/348; Zad al-Masir, same place, note (1).]].

﴿That you worship none but Him, and be good to parents﴾, that is: and He enjoined kindness to parents, dutifulness toward them and tenderness toward them.

﴿If one or both of them reach old age with you﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yablughanna" with the alif of the dual. According to this reading, His saying ﴿one or both of them﴾ is a resumed statement, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71], and His saying: ﴿And they conceal their private counsel, those who did wrong﴾ [al-Anbiya': 3]; and His saying ﴿those who did wrong﴾ is an initial statement. The rest read "yablughanna" in the singular.

﴿So do not say to them "uff"﴾. In it there are three dialects. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read it with a fatha on the fa'. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Hafs read it with a kasra and tanwin. The rest read it with a kasra on the fa' without tanwin. Their meaning is one, and it is an expression of aversion.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: the origin of "tuff" and "uff" is the dirt on the fingers when you rub them together.

It was said: "uff" is the dirt that gathers in the folds of the body, and "tuff" is what gathers on the fingers.

It was said: "uff" is earwax, and "tuff" is the dirt under the fingernails.

It was said: "uff" is the dirt under the nail, and "tuff" is anything small you lift from the ground with your hand.

﴿And do not scold them﴾, and do not rebuke them.

﴿And speak to them a generous word﴾, good, beautiful and gentle. Ibn al-Musayyab said: like the words of a sinning slave to a harsh master.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 17, verse 24:**

﴿And lower to them the wing of humility﴾, i.e., soften your side toward them and be humble. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: "Be gentle with them, so that you do not refuse them anything they love." ﴿Out of mercy﴾, that is, out of compassion. ﴿And say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small﴾. He meant: if they are Muslims.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: this verse has been abrogated (*mansukh*, i.e., superseded by the principle of *naskh*) by His words: "It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists" [al-Tawba: 113].

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Samʿan informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, who said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, who said: Hammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman – meaning al-Sulami – from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The parent is the middle gate of Paradise; so guard it if you wish, or neglect it."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in *al-Birr wa al-Silah*, chapter "The Virtue of Pleasing One's Parents": 6/24-25, and he said: "This is a sound hadith." We were informed by Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Zarrad, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Idris al-Jurjani informed us, who said: Abu al-Hasan ʿAli ibn al-Husayn al-Maliyni informed us, who said: Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Habib ibn ʿUdayy narrated to us, who said: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Yaʿla ibn ʿAta', from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The pleasure of Allah lies in the pleasure of the parent, and the displeasure of Allah lies in the displeasure of the parent."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in *al-Birr*, chapter "The Virtue of Pleasing One's Parents": 6/25, as a marfuʿ (attributed to the Prophet) and mawquf (attributed to a companion) report, and he said: "This one, the mawquf, is more sound." Also Ibn Hibban, no. 2026, p. 496 of *Mawarid al-Zaman*; al-Hakim authenticated it: 4/152; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*: 13/12. See *Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahiha*, no. 516: 2/29-31; *Majma' al-Zawa'id*: 8/136; *al-Kafi al-Shaf* p. 98; *Kashf al-Khafa'*: 1/520.]]

We were informed by Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi, who said: Abu Saʿid Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us, who said: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Siffar informed us, who said: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn Tamtam al-Dabbi narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Maslama narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who is a constant benefactor-reminder, one who is undutiful to parents, and one who is addicted to wine will not enter Paradise."[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in *al-Musnad*: 3/28, 44, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, and the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*: 13/17, in which occurs Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who is weak. The hadith has many corroborating reports from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, Abu Hurayra and Anas. See: *Sunan al-Nasa'i*, Book of Drinks, chapter "Narrations on Those Addicted to Wine": 8/318; *Sunan al-Darimi*, Drinks, chapter "The Addict to Wine": 2/112; Ibn Hibban, p. 498 of *Mawarid al-Zaman*; *al-Musannaf* of Ibn Abi Shayba: 8/544; *al-Musnad* of Imam Ahmad: 3/226; *Mushkil al-Athar* of al-Tahawi: 1/395. al-Albani authenticated it in *Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahiha*: 2/285-291. See also *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 5/266.]]

We were informed by Imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, who said: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Bamawayh al-Isfahani informed us, who said: Abu Saʿid Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Basri informed us, who said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, who said: Rib'i ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿid al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Disgraced is the nose of a man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 25:**

﴿Your Lord knows best what is in your souls﴾ regarding kindness to one's parents and disobedience toward them. ﴿If you are righteous﴾, dutiful and obedient, after any shortcoming on your part in fulfilling what the rights of your parents and others required of you. ﴿Then indeed He is ever Forgiving to the awwabin (those who turn back in repentance)﴾ after disobedience.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding this verse: it refers to a man who may speak sharply to his parents, intending nothing by it but good, and for this he is not held to account.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The awwab (al-awwab, the one who often turns back) is the one who sins, then repents, then sins again, then repents."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The one who returns to good."

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "He is the one who returns to Allah in matters that trouble him and that befall him."

It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "They are those who glorify Allah (al-musabbihun). Its proof is His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo the praise with him﴾ [Saba: 10]."

Qatadah said: "They are those who pray."

'Awf al-'Uqayli [in manuscript "B": 'Awn] said: "They are those who perform the Duha prayer (ṣalat al-ḍuḥa, the forenoon prayer)."

Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn al-Husayn al-Rawqi [in manuscript "B": al-Dawraqi; the correct reading is what we have recorded] al-Tusi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us: Abu al-Nadr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham, the companion of al-Dastawa'i, from Qatadah, from al-Qasim ibn 'Awf, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the people of Quba' while they were performing the Duha prayer, and he said: "The prayer of the awwabin is when the weaning camels' feet are scorched by the forenoon heat" [(Reported by Muslim in the Book of the Prayer of Travellers, chapter "The Prayer of the Awwabin when the Weaning Camels Are Scorched," no. 748: 1/516; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/145; and Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 2/264.)].

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: "The awwab is the one who prays between Maghrib and 'Isha'."

It is also related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The angels surround those who pray between Maghrib and 'Isha'," and this is the prayer of the earlier generations. [(See these opinions and others in al-Tabari: 15/68–71; Zad al-Masir: 5/26–27. al-Tabari preferred the view of the one who said: "The awwab is the one who repents from sin, returning from the disobedience of Allah to His obedience, and from what He dislikes to what He is pleased with; for awwab is an intensive form (fa'\u0101l) derived from the saying of one who says: 'So-and-so returned (aba) from such-and-such,' either from his journey to his home or from one state to another, as 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras said: 'Every absent one returns (yu'ibu) ... but the absent one of death does not return.' So he returns (ya'ub) and he is a man who has returned (a'ib) from his journey, and awwab from his sins.)].

﴿And give the near relative his right﴾, meaning the maintaining of ties of kinship (silat al-rahim, keeping ties with one's relatives). By this he meant the kinship of the person, and most scholars held this view.

From Ali ibn al-Husayn: he meant by it the kinship of the Messenger (ﷺ).[[The more correct of the two interpretations is the one that takes it to mean God's command to His servants to maintain the ties of their own relatives on the side of their fathers and mothers. This is because God, may He be exalted, followed it immediately with His exhortation to His servants to show kindness to their fathers and mothers. It is therefore necessary that this be an exhortation to maintain the ties of their own lineage, not the lineage of others, which has not been mentioned. See: Tafsir (exegesis) al-Tabari: 15/72.]]

﴿And the needy, and the wayfarer; and do not squander wastefully﴾, that is: do not spend your wealth in disobedience.

Mujahid said: If a person spent all his wealth in what is right, it would not be squandering, but if he spent a mudd (a small measure of grain) in falsehood, it would be squandering.

Ibn Mas'ud was asked about squandering (tabdhir) and said: spending wealth in other than its proper place.

Shu'bah said: I was walking with Abu Ishaq on the road to Kufa when he came upon the gate of a house built with plaster (jiss) and baked brick (ajurr). He said: This is squandering.

As for the statement of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): spending wealth in other than its proper place.[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/72-74; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/274-275; Zad al-Masir: 5/27-28.]]

﴿Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils﴾, that is, their allies. The Arabs say of everyone who adheres to the custom of a people that he is their brother. ﴿And the devil has ever been ungrateful to his Lord﴾, meaning he has been denying His blessings.

﴿And if you turn away from them﴾ was revealed concerning Mihja, Bilal, Suhayb, Salim and Khabbab, who would at times ask the Prophet (ﷺ) for what they needed, and he had nothing to give. He would turn away from them out of shyness and remain silent, so this was revealed.[[Zad al-Masir: 5/29; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/30. There are other statements about its occasion of revelation in both of these sources.]] That is: if you turn away from those whom I have commanded you to give to, ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for﴾, meaning awaiting provision from God which you hope will come to you. ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾, soft-spoken, and this is the promise: promise them a good promise. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 32–33:

﴿And do not approach fornication. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way.﴾ ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right.﴾ And its right is what we have related: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in one of three cases: a man who disbelieves after his belief, or commits adultery after his marriage (ihsan), or kills a soul without a soul, so he is to be killed for it." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Diyat, chapter "The Imam orders pardon in blood": 6/301, from Abu Umamah; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Fitan, chapter "What has come that the blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in one of three": 3/373, and he said: "a hasan hadith"; and Ibn Majah in al-Hudud, chapter "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in three," no. (2533): 2/847; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/148. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud something similar.]

﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority.﴾ That is: power and authority over the killer to demand retaliation (qisas). This was said by Mujahid. Al-Dahhak said: his authority is that he has a choice: if he wishes, he may take retaliation from him; if he wishes, he may take the blood-money (diyah); and if he wishes, he may pardon.

﴿But let him not commit excess in killing.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: "fa-la tusrif" with the ta' (ت), addressing the heir of the slain. The others read it with the ya' (ي), in the third person: that is, "la yusrif" — the heir should not commit excess in killing.

They differed concerning this excess that is prohibited. Ibn Abbas and most of the exegetes said: its meaning is that he should not kill other than the killer. This is because in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them was slain, they would not be content with the killing of his slayer until they killed someone more noble than him.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: if the killer is one person, then they should not kill a group in place of one. The people of the Jahiliyyah, when the slain was a noble, would not be content with the killing of the killer [alone] [[Addition from manuscript "b".]] until they killed with him a group of his relatives.

Qatadah said: its meaning is that he should not mutilate the killer. [[These aspects of interpreting the verse are not outside the truth, and all of them fall within the meaning of the verse and in the prohibition of excess in killing. And Allah knows best.]]

﴿Indeed, he is ever supported.﴾ The pronoun refers to the slain in His saying: ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully﴾. That is: the slain is supported in this world by the imposition of retaliation upon his killer, and in the Hereafter by the expiation of his sins and the obligation of the Fire upon his killer. This is the view of Mujahid.

Qatadah said: the pronoun refers to the heir of the slain; meaning: he is supported against the killer by exacting retaliation from him or the blood-money.

It was also said concerning His saying: ﴿But let him not commit excess in killing﴾ that it intends the aggressive killer, saying: he should not transgress by killing without right, for if he does so, then the heir of the slain is supported by Me against him by exacting retaliation from him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 34–36:

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan, except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity. And fulfill the covenant.﴾ (By doing what Allah has commanded and refraining from what Allah has forbidden.) It is also said: by "covenant" He meant what a person binds himself to.

﴿Indeed, the covenant is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.﴾ Al-Suddi said: it is something demanded [of the one who made it]. It is also said: the covenant is questioned concerning its party, and it is said: "For what were you breached?" like the buried infant girl who is asked, "For what sin was she killed?" ﴿And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a balance that is straight.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited "bil-qistas" with a kasra on the qaf, while the rest recited it with a damma. Both are dialects. It means the balance, whether small or large, i.e., with the balance of justice. Al-Hasan said: it is the qabban (steelyard). Mujahid said: it is Roman (Byzantine). Others said: it is Arabic, derived from al-qist, which is justice; i.e., weigh with justice. ﴿That is better and more excellent in outcome (ta'wil)﴾, i.e., in consequence.

﴿And do not pursue (taqfu) that of which you have no knowledge.﴾ Qatadah said: Do not say, "I saw," when you did not see; "I heard," when you did not hear; or "I knew," when you did not know.

Mujahid said: Do not accuse anyone of what you have no knowledge of.

Al-Qutaybi said: Do not follow it with conjecture and assumption. Linguistically, it means to follow a trace; it is said: qafawtu fulanan aqfuhu, qafaytuhu and aqfaytuhu, when I followed his trace. It is from this that poetry (al-qafiyah) is named, because they follow the traces (of meter and rhyme).

Al-Qutaybi also said: it is derived from al-qafa (the back of the head/neck), as if one follows affairs from behind, i.e., one follows them and seeks to know them from their rear.

The true meaning: Do not speak, O human, based on conjecture and assumption.

﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about.﴾ It is said: the meaning is that a person will be questioned about his hearing, his sight, and his heart. It is also said: the hearing, sight, and heart will be questioned about what the person did.

His saying ﴿all of those﴾ means all these limbs and organs. According to the first view, "those" refers to their owners.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Abu Tahir Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, Abu Ali Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Raffa' narrated to us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn informed us, Sa'd ibn Aws al-Absi narrated to us, Bilal ibn Yahya al-Absi narrated to me that Shutayr ibn Shakal informed him, from his father Shakal ibn Humayd, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, teach me a seeking of refuge that I may seek refuge with." He took my hand and then said: "Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, the evil of my sight, the evil of my tongue, the evil of my heart, and the evil of my semen (maniyy)." He said: so I memorized it. Sa'd said: al-Maniyy is its water.

[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter on seeking refuge: 2/160; al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat: 9/464-465, who said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we know only through this chain"; al-Nasa'i in al-Isti'adhah, chapter on seeking refuge from the evil of sight: 8/260; al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/533, and al-Dhahabi agreed. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/168-169.]]

﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾, i.e., with insolence, pride, and self-admiration (*khuyala'*). It is an explanation of the walking, so it is put in the form of a verbal noun (*masdar*).

Its meaning: a person gains nothing through his pride and insolence, just as one who wishes to tear through the earth or to rival the mountains will achieve nothing.

It was said: this was mentioned because whoever walks in a haughty manner walks sometimes on his heels and sometimes on the fronts of his feet. So it is said to him: you will not pierce the earth if you walk on your heels, and you will not reach the mountains in height if you walk on the fronts of your feet.

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jouzjani informed us: Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us: al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi related to us: Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us: my father related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Uthman ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Ali, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked, he moved forward with energy, as if he were descending from a slope." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib, chapter on his (ﷺ) physical attributes: 1/116-117, and in his book *al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyya* pp. (85, 86) in the margin of the commentary of al-Bajuri. It was also narrated by Imam Ahmad in *al-Musnad*: 1/96, and by the author (al-Baghawi) in *Sharh al-Sunna*: 12/319. It is a sound hadith.]]

Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani informed us: Abu al-Qasim al-Khuza'i informed us: al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi related to us: Qutayba ibn Sa'id related to us: Ibn Lahi'a related to us, from Abu Yunus, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I have never seen anything more beautiful than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); it was as if the sun were running in his face. And I have never seen anyone quicker in his walking than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); it was as if the earth were folded up for him. We would exert ourselves, while he was not burdened at all." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib, chapter on the description of the Prophet (ﷺ): 10/131-132, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith." It was also narrated in *al-Shama'il* p. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 38–39:

﴿All of that — its evil is hateful in the sight of your Lord.﴾ Ibn ʿAmir and the people of Kufa recited it as "sayyi'uhu" with a raised hamza and a damma on the ha', in the construct form (ʿala al-idafah). Its meaning: all of what We mentioned from His saying: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him﴾ — "its evil" means: the evil of what We have enumerated to you is, in the sight of your Lord, hateful; because He has also enumerated good matters, such as His saying: ﴿And give the relative his right﴾ and ﴿And lower to them the wing of humility﴾, and other than that.

As for the others, they recited "sayyi'atan" with a fatha and tanwin, meaning: all of what We mentioned from His saying: ﴿And do not kill your children﴾ up to this place is an evil (sayyi'ah) with no good in it, since the whole refers to what is forbidden and nothing else. He did not say "makruhah" (feminine) because there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in it, and its implied meaning is: all of that was an evil, hateful. [And His saying ﴿makruhan﴾ is in the sense of repetition (al-takrir), not as a description; its meaning is: all of that was an evil, and was hateful.] [[The text between the brackets is omitted from "b".]] Or it returns to the meaning rather than the wording, because sayyi'ah means sin (dhanb), which is masculine.

﴿That﴾ — what We have mentioned — ﴿is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom (al-hikmah)﴾. Everything that God has commanded or forbidden is wisdom.

﴿And do not set up with God another god, lest you be cast into Hell, blamed and banished (madhuran)﴾: He addressed the Prophet (ﷺ) in these verses, and what is meant is the community (ummah). ﴿Madhmum madhdur﴾ — expelled, distanced from every good.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 40–44:

His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen you for sons and taken for Himself from the angels females?﴾ That is: He chose you and gave you the best, and for Himself He took what is not the best, meaning: He chose you ﴿for sons and has taken from the angels females﴾, because they used to say the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Indeed, you utter a grave saying﴾. He addresses the polytheists of Makkah.

His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an﴾, meaning: [what He mentioned of] [[Omitted from "ب".]] the lessons, wisdom, parables, rulings, proofs, and information, and the intensive form (tashdid) is for abundance and repetition. ﴿That they may remember﴾, that is: that they may remember and be admonished. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited it with a sukun on the dhal and a damma on the kaf (yadhdhakkaru becoming yudhakkiru), and likewise in al-Furqan.

﴿But it increases them not except in aversion﴾: Our diversifying and reminding increases them only in fleeing and distancing from the truth.

﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: ﴿If there were with Him other gods, as they say﴾. Hafs and Ibn Kathir recited "yaqulun" with the ya', and the others recited it with the ta'. ﴿Then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾, that is, they would have sought the gods, meaning, a way to Him ﴿to the Owner of the Throne﴾, by overpowering and subjugating Him, to remove His dominion, as the kings of the world do to one another.

It was also said: its meaning is that they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne by drawing near to Him.

Qatadah said: they would have known Allah and His virtue, and sought what would bring them near to Him.

The first is more correct. Then He declared Himself free of imperfection, saying, Mighty is the Speaker: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted high above what they say﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "taqulun" with the ta', and the others with the ya'. ﴿Exalted, great exaltation﴾. ﴿The seven heavens and the earth praise Him, and whoever is in them﴾. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Ya'qub recited "tusabbihu" with the ta', and the others recited it with the ya', because of the separation between the verb and the feminine noun.

﴿And there is not a thing except that it exalts His praise﴾. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "And there is not a living thing except that it exalts His praise."

Qatadah said: meaning the animals and the growing things.

'Ikrimah said: the tree glorifies, and the pillar does not glorify.

It is related from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib that he said: "Indeed the dust glorifies as long as it is not moistened; when it becomes moist it stops glorifying. Indeed the pebble glorifies as long as it is not lifted from its place; when it is lifted it stops glorifying. Indeed the leaf glorifies as long as it is on the tree; when it falls it stops glorifying. Indeed the garment glorifies as long as it is new; when it becomes soiled it stops glorifying. Indeed the water glorifies as long as it is flowing; when it stands still it stops glorifying. Indeed the wild beasts and the birds glorify when they cry out; when they are quiet they stop glorifying."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "And there is not a thing, inanimate, except that it exalts His praise, even the creaking of the door and the cracking of the ceiling."

Mujahid said: "All things glorify Allah, whether living, dead or inanimate, and their glorification is 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.'"

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna informed us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayr informed us, Isra'il informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: "We used to count the signs as a blessing, while you count them as a warning. We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey when the water ran low. He said: 'Seek out what remains of water.' They brought a vessel with a little water in it. He put his hand into the vessel and said: 'Come to the blessed purification and the blessing is from Allah.' I saw the water gushing from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We used to hear the glorification of the food while it was being eaten."

Some of the scholars of meanings said: the heavens, the earth, the inanimate things, and all the animals other than the rational ones glorify, in that what they indicate by their subtle composition and wondrous form points to their Creator, and this becomes like glorification from them.

The first is what is transmitted from the early generations (salaf).

And know that Allah, the Exalted, has a knowledge in inanimate things that none other than He comprehends, so it is fitting that its knowledge be entrusted to Him.

﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾, that is, you do not know the glorification of whatever is other than those who glorify in your languages and tongues. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving.﴾

﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: ﴿If there were with Him other gods, as they say﴾. Hafs and Ibn Kathir recited "yaqulun" with the ya', and the others recited it with the ta'. ﴿Then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾, that is, they would have sought the gods, meaning, a way to Him ﴿to the Owner of the Throne﴾, by overpowering and subjugating Him, to remove His dominion, as the kings of the world do to one another.

It was also said: its meaning is that they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne by drawing near to Him.

Qatadah said: they would have known Allah and His virtue, and sought what would bring them near to Him.

The first is more correct. Then He declared Himself free of imperfection, saying, Mighty is the Speaker: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted high above what they say﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "taqulun" with the ta', and the others with the ya'. ﴿Exalted, great exaltation﴾. ﴿The seven heavens and the earth praise Him, and whoever is in them﴾. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Ya'qub recited "tusabbihu" with the ta', and the others recited it with the ya', because of the separation between the verb and the feminine noun.

﴿And there is not a thing except that it exalts His praise﴾. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "And there is not a living thing except that it exalts His praise."

Qatadah said: meaning the animals and the growing things.

'Ikrimah said: the tree glorifies, and the pillar does not glorify.

It is related from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib that he said: "Indeed the dust glorifies as long as it is not moistened; when it becomes moist it stops glorifying. Indeed the pebble glorifies as long as it is not lifted from its place; when it is lifted it stops glorifying. Indeed the leaf glorifies as long as it is on the tree; when it falls it stops glorifying. Indeed the garment glorifies as long as it is new; when it becomes soiled it stops glorifying. Indeed the water glorifies as long as it is flowing; when it stands still it stops glorifying. Indeed the wild beasts and the birds glorify when they cry out; when they are quiet they stop glorifying."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "And there is not a thing, inanimate, except that it exalts His praise, even the creaking of the door and the cracking of the ceiling."

Mujahid said: "All things glorify Allah, whether living, dead or inanimate, and their glorification is 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.'"

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna informed us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayr informed us, Isra'il informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: "We used to count the signs as a blessing, while you count them as a warning. We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey when the water ran low. He said: 'Seek out what remains of water.' They brought a vessel with a little water in it. He put his hand into the vessel and said: 'Come to the blessed purification and the blessing is from Allah.' I saw the water gushing from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We used to hear the glorification of the food while it was being eaten."

Some of the scholars of meanings said: the heavens, the earth, the inanimate things, and all the animals other than the rational ones glorify, in that what they indicate by their subtle composition and wondrous form points to their Creator, and this becomes like glorification from them.

The first is what is transmitted from the early generations (salaf).

And know that Allah, the Exalted, has a knowledge in inanimate things that none other than He comprehends, so it is fitting that its knowledge be entrusted to Him.

﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾, that is, you do not know the glorification of whatever is other than those who glorify in your languages and tongues. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving.﴾

The Exalted said: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾. It veils their hearts from understanding it and from benefiting from it.

Qatadah said: it means the coverings (al-akinnah), and "masturan" is in the sense of "sitir" (concealing), like His saying: "Indeed, His promise is always fulfilled" [Maryam: 61], where the passive form carries the sense of the active.

It was also said: "masturan" means concealed from the eyes of people, so they do not see it.

Some of them explained it as a barrier from the visible eyes, as it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that when the verse "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab" was revealed, the wife of Abu Lahab came with a stone in her hand while the Prophet (ﷺ) was with Abu Bakr. She did not see him, so she said to Abu Bakr: "Where is your companion? I have been told that he has satirized me." He said: "By Allah, he does not speak poetry, nor does he compose it." So she returned saying: "I had come with this stone to crush his head." Abu Bakr said: "Did she not see you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, an angel remained between me and her, shielding me." [Narrated by Abu Ya'la and Ibn Abi Hatim. See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/44, 4/565-566; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/144.]

﴿And We place over their hearts coverings﴾ (aghtiyah, coverings) ﴿lest they understand it﴾, meaning out of aversion to their understanding it. It was also said: so that they do not understand it. ﴿And in their ears a deafness﴾, a heaviness, so that they do not hear it. ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an﴾, meaning when you say, "There is no god but Allah," in the Qur'an while you are reciting it, ﴿they turn their backs in aversion﴾. "Nufur" is the plural of "nafir," like "qa'id" and "qu'ud," and "jalis" and "julus," meaning those who flee in aversion.

﴿We know best what they listen to when they listen to you﴾. It was said: "bihi" is redundant (silah), meaning they seek to hear it, ﴿when they listen to you﴾ while you recite the Qur'an, ﴿and when they are in secret consultation﴾, conferring about your matter. It was also said: "dhu najwa" means they confer together. Some of them say, "He is a madman," some say, "He is a soothsayer," some say, "He is a sorcerer," and some say, "He is a poet." ﴿When the wrongdoers say﴾, meaning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and his companions, ﴿You follow none but a man under sorcery.﴾ "Mastur" means bewitched (matbub). Mujahid said: deceived (makhda'an). It was also said: turned away from the truth. It is said: "ma saharaka 'an kadha," meaning, "What has turned you away from such-and-such?"

Abu 'Ubaydah said: meaning a man who has a "sahr" (windpipe), and "al-sahr" is the lung; that is, he is a human like you, sustained by food and drink, eating and drinking. The poet said: "We are seen as those who are to be destined for an unseen fate... and we are nourished with food and drink," meaning, we are fed and sustained.

﴿And they said: "When we are bones"﴾ after death, ﴿and crumbled dust"﴾. Mujahid said: "Dust." It was also said: "Fragments." Al-Rufat is whatever has broken and decayed of anything, like crumbs and debris.

﴿"Shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to them: ﴿"Be stones or iron"﴾ in hardness and strength. This is not a command of obligation but a command of incapacitation, meaning: imagine in your hearts that you are stones or iron in strength.

﴿"Or a creation of what is greater in your breasts"﴾. It was said: "The heavens and the earth [and the mountains]." [[Omitted in "A".]]

Mujahid, Ikrimah [[In "B": Qatadah.]] and most of the exegetes said: it is death, for there is nothing in the soul of the son of Adam greater than death. That is: even if you were death itself, We would cause you to die and We would resurrect you.

﴿So they will say: "Who will restore us?"﴾, meaning, who will raise us after death? ﴿Say: "The One who originated you"﴾, meaning created you, ﴿the first time"﴾. Al-Kalbi said: "The polytheists used to harm the Muslims, so they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And tell My servants﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿to say﴾ to the disbelievers ﴿that which is best﴾, and not to retaliate against their foolishness." Al-Hasan said: "He says to him: may Allah guide you." This was before permission was given for jihad and fighting.

[[Indicating that it was abrogated by the verse of fighting or the sword, and it has been previously noted in more than one place that some scholars excessively claimed abrogation (naskh) of many verses by the verse of the sword, and the truth is that there is no abrogation in all of this.]]

It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when some of the disbelievers insulted him, and Allah commanded him to pardon. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 333.]]

It was also said: Allah commanded the believers to say and do that which is best, i.e., the characteristic that is best.

It was also said: "the best" refers to the word of sincerity, "There is no god but Allah."

﴿Indeed, Satan incites [discord] among them﴾, i.e., he corrupts and casts enmity between them. ﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been to mankind a clear enemy﴾, manifestly hostile.

﴿Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you﴾, by granting you success so that you believe, ﴿or if He wills, He will punish you﴾, by causing you to die in polytheism so that you are punished. This was said by Ibn Juraij.

Al-Kalbi said: "If He wills, He will have mercy upon you by saving you from the people of Makkah, and if He wills, He will punish you by giving them power over you."

﴿And We have not sent you over them as a guardian﴾, a protector and a responsible one. It was said: it was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 55–57:

﴿Your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is: your Lord is the One who knows those in the heavens and the earth, and He made them differ in their forms, their characters, their conditions and their religions (milal).

﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others.﴾ It was said: He made the people of the heavens and the earth differ, just as He preferred some of the prophets over others.

Qatadah said concerning this verse: God took Abraham as a close friend (khalil), spoke to Moses directly (taklim), and said to Jesus: "Be," and he was. And He gave Solomon a kingdom that would not be fitting for anyone after him, and He gave David the Psalms (Zabur), as He said: ﴿And We gave David the Psalms.﴾ The Zabur is a book which God taught David, containing one hundred and fifty surahs, all of them supplication, glorification and praise of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and in it there is no lawful or unlawful, no obligatory duties and no prescribed penalties (hudud).

Its meaning: you do not deny the preference of the prophets, so how do you deny the excellence of the Prophet ﷺ and his being given the Qur'an? This address is directed at those among the People of the Book and others who acknowledge the preference of the prophets, peace be upon them.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him﴾. This is because the polytheists were struck by a severe drought, until they ate dogs and carrion, so they sought help from the Prophet ﷺ that he might pray for them. God the Exalted said: ﴿Say﴾ to the polytheists: ﴿Call upon those whom you claim besides Him﴾ to be gods, ﴿they have no power to remove the harm﴾ of the drought and hunger ﴿from you, nor to change it﴾ to others, or to change the condition from hardship to ease.

﴿Those whom they call upon themselves seek the means of access to their Lord﴾: meaning, those whom the polytheists call upon as gods and worship.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: they are Jesus and his mother, Uzair, the angels, the sun, the moon and the stars. "Yabtaghun" means they seek of their Lord "al-wasilah," that is, nearness (qurbah). It was also said: al-wasilah is the highest rank, that is, they humble themselves before God seeking the highest rank.

It was also said: al-wasilah is everything by which one draws near to God the Exalted.

His saying: ﴿Which of them is nearest﴾ means: they look to see which of them is nearest to God so that they may seek the means through him. Al-Zajjaj said: "Which of them is nearest" seeks the means of access to God the Exalted and draws near to Him through righteous deeds. ﴿And they hope for His mercy﴾, that is, His Paradise, ﴿and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared﴾, that is, caution is to be sought from it.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: the verse was revealed concerning a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of jinn; then the jinn embraced Islam, and the humans who worshipped them did not know of their Islam, so they held fast to their worship. God rebuked them and revealed this verse. [[See: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, chapter "Those whom they call upon themselves seek the means of access to their Lord": 8/398; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/305.]]

And Ibn Mas'ud recited "ulā'ika alladhīna tad'ūn" with the letter ta' (tad'ūn).
