﴿And there is not a town﴾ but We shall destroy it ﴿before the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: We shall lay it waste and destroy its people, ﴿or punish it with a severe punishment﴾ with various kinds of punishment, when they disbelieve and disobey. Muqatil and others said: "Destroying it" refers to the believers, by causing them to die, and "punishing it" refers to the disbelievers, with various kinds of punishment.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "When fornication and usury become widespread in a town, God permits its destruction."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 15/107.]]

﴿That was written in the Book﴾, meaning in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), ﴿inscribed﴾, meaning written.

Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'The decree, and what has been and what will be until eternity.'"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Sunnah, chapter on qadar: 7/69; and al-Tirmidhi in qadar, chapter on what has come concerning contentment with the decree: 6/368-369, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith," and in the tafsir of surah "Nun": 9/233, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." It was also narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/317, and by al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, p. 79, where in the version of al-Tayalisi there is Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym, who is weak, but it has other chains by which it is strengthened. Al-Albani authenticated it in his commentary on al-Mishkat: 1/34.]]

God the Exalted revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ): "If you wish, I will give them respite, and if you wish, I will grant them what they asked for. But if they do not believe, I will destroy them as I destroyed those who came before them [[Omitted from manuscript "B".]] from the nations." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No, rather give them respite." So God the Mighty and Majestic revealed [the verse].[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/258; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/362; al-Tabari: 15/108; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 333-334; and al-Nasa'i in his tafsir: 1/656. Al-Haythami said: its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir authenticated it in his commentary on al-Musnad, no. 2333. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/306-307; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/50; Ibn Kathir: 3/48.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 59–60:**

﴿And We did not withhold from sending the signs﴾ which the disbelievers of Quraysh asked for, ﴿except that the former peoples denied them﴾, so We destroyed them. If your people do not believe after the signs are sent, I will destroy them, because it is part of Our way with the nations that when they ask for signs and then do not believe after the signs come, We destroy them and do not reprieve them. We have decreed the destruction of this nation with the punishment. Therefore He, exalted is His remembrance, said: "Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter" [al-Qamar: 46]. Then He said:

﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, meaning bright and clear. ﴿But they wronged themselves with it﴾, that is, they denied that it was from Allah, as He said: "because they used to wrong Our signs" [al-A'raf: 9], meaning they denied them. It is also said: they wronged themselves by denying it. He means: so We hastened to punish them.

﴿And We do not send the signs﴾, that is, the lessons and proofs, ﴿except as a warning﴾ to the servants, ﴿so that they may believe.﴾

Qatadah said: Allah, exalted is He, frightens people with whatever signs of His He wills, ﴿perhaps they will return﴾. [In manuscript "B": "the servants".]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾, that is, they are in His grip and cannot escape His will. So He is your guardian and protector from them. Therefore do not fear them, and proceed to what He has commanded you of conveying the message, as He said: "And Allah will protect you from the people" [al-Ma'idah: 67].

﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾. Most scholars hold that it refers to what the Prophet (ﷺ) saw on the night of the Mi'raj (ascension) of wonders and signs.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it was a vision of the eye which the Prophet (ﷺ) was shown. [Al-Bukhari narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas in the commentary on surah al-Isra': 8/398.] This is also the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Masruq, Qatadah, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Jurayj and most scholars.

The Arabs say: "I saw with the eye" (ru'yah) and "a vision" (ru'ya). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned it to the people, some of them denied it and rejected it, and so it was a trial for the people.

Some people said: he was taken by night in his spirit without his body. [See above in the commentary on this surah, p. 58, note (3).]

Some said: he had two ascensions: an ascension of sight with the eye and an ascension of vision with the heart.

Some said: by this vision he meant what the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, that he and his companions entered Makkah and he began travelling toward Makkah before the appointed time, but the polytheists blocked him and he returned to Madinah. His return that year, after he had been told he would enter it, was a trial for some of them, until he entered it the following year. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: "Certainly Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth" [al-Fath: 27]. [See these views on the interpretation of the vision in al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/309–310; Zad al-Masir: 5/53–54.]

﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾ means the tree of al-Zaqqum. Its meaning is: and the cursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an. The Arabs call any repulsive food "cursed food." It is also said: its meaning is "the one who eats it is cursed." The word "tree" is in the accusative as a conjunction with "the vision," meaning: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you and the cursed tree except as a trial for the people." So the trial in the vision was what we have mentioned.

The trial concerning the cursed tree is from two aspects. The first: Abu Jahl said, "Ibn Abi Kabshah threatens you with a fire that burns stones, then he claims that a tree will grow in it, and you know that fire burns trees."

The second: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Za'ba'ra said, "Muhammad frightens us with al-Zaqqum, and we know al-Zaqqum only as butter and dates." Abu Jahl said, "O girl, come and feed us al-zaqqum," so she brought dates and butter. He said, "O people, eat zaqqum, for this is what Muhammad frightens you with." So Allah described it in al-Saffat. [See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 334; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/310–311; Zad al-Masir: 5/55.]

It is also said: the cursed tree is the one that twines around trees and dries them out, namely dodder (kashuth). [Mentioned by Ibn al-Jawzi (5/56) from Ibn 'Abbas as well. See above the commentary on verse 26 of surah Ibrahim: 4/348, note (6).]

﴿And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression﴾, that is, great rebellion and enormous obstinacy.

﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate myself to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ That is: whom You created from clay, and I brought it. This is what was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas: that God, exalted is He, sent Iblis, and he took a handful of earth from its sweet and its salty parts, and from it God created Adam. So whoever was created from the sweet part is good (sa'id), even if he is the son of disbelievers, and whoever was created from the salty part is wretched (shaqi), even if he is the son of prophets. [Related by al-Tabari, 15/116, from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf (companion's statement).]

﴿He said﴾: that is, Iblis. ﴿Tell me﴾: that is, inform me. The kaf in ﴿araytaka﴾ is for emphasizing the address. ﴿Is this the one You have honored above me?﴾ That is, You have preferred him over me. ﴿If You respite me﴾: give me a reprieve ﴿until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize﴾ ﴿dhurriyyatahu﴾ (his descendants). That is, I will utterly destroy them through misguidance. It is said: "ihtanaka al-jaradu al-zar'a" (the locusts stripped the crops) when it ate all of it. It is also said that it derives from the Arabs' saying "hanaka al-dabbata yuhannikuha" when one ties a rope under the lower jaw of an animal to lead it; that is, I will lead them however I wish. And it is said: I will gain control over them through seduction. ﴿Except a few﴾: meaning the protected ones (al-ma'sumun) whom God, mighty and majestic, exempted in His saying: "Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them" [al-Hijr: 42].

﴿He said﴾ (God): ﴿Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense﴾: that is, your recompense and the recompense of your followers, ﴿a full recompense﴾: complete and perfect. It is said: "waffartuhu uwaffiruhu wafran" (I gave it in full). His saying: ﴿And incite﴾: and provoke, and urge, and make unsettled, ﴿whomever you can among them﴾: that is, among the descendants of Adam, ﴿with your voice﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: with your call to disobedience to God. And every caller to disobedience to God [is from the army of Iblis].

Al-Azhari said: its meaning is, call them with a call by which you unsettle them toward your side, that is, you lightly move them [the bracketed text is absent in manuscript "b"].

﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾. Sharing in wealth means: everything taken unlawfully or spent unlawfully. This is the saying of Mujahid, al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

'Ata' said: it is usury (riba). Qatadah said: it is what the polytheists used to forbid from the livestock, such as the bahirah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah and the ham.

al-Dahhak said: it is what they used to slaughter for their idols. [Whatever wealth is used in obeying Satan and disobeying God, such as spending wealth unlawfully or earning it unlawfully, or slaughtering for idols, or setting free (tasyib) or dedicating animals to Satan, and other such things that involve disobedience, the one who does them shares Iblis in them, so there is no reason to restrict it to some over others.]

As for sharing in children: it was related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is burying daughters alive (al-mu'uddah).

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: they are children born of fornication.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is that they made their children Jews, Christians and Magians.

There is another report from Ibn 'Abbas: it is their naming their children 'Abd al-Harith, 'Abd Shams, 'Abd al-'Uzza, 'Abd al-Dar and similar names. [All these aspects are included in the meaning of the verse without restricting it to any one of them.] 211/a

It was related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad that Satan sits upon a man's penis, and if he does not say "In the name of God," he has intercourse with his wife and ejaculates into her vagina just as the man does.

It was related in some reports: "Among you are those who are enticed (mughribun)." It was asked: "And who are the mughribun?" He said: "Those with whom the jinn share (in intercourse)."  [Weak; related by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul from 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her. See Kanz al-'Ummal 16/354, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi 10/289.]

It was related that a man said to Ibn 'Abbas: "My wife woke up and there was a flame of fire in her vagina?" He said: "That is from intercourse with the jinn."

In the reports: when Iblis was cast out to the earth, he said: "O Lord, You expelled me from Paradise because of Adam, so give me power over him and his descendants." He said: "You have power." He said: "I cannot do it except with You, so increase me." He said: "Incite whomever you can among them with your voice," and the verse. Then Adam said: "O Lord, You gave Iblis power over me and my descendants, and I cannot withstand him except with You." He said: "No child will be born to you except that I shall assign to him those who guard him." He said: "Increase me." He said: "A good deed is multiplied tenfold, and an evil deed is recompensed with its like." He said: "Increase me." He said: "Repentance is offered as long as the soul is in the body." He said: "Increase me." He said: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves," the verse [az-Zumar: 53]. [Al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab and Ibn 'Asakir in a similar form, from Thabit who said: "It reached us that Iblis..." See al-Durr al-Manthur 5/313.]

In a report: Iblis said: "O Lord, You sent prophets and revealed books, so what is my reading?" He said: "Poetry." He said: "What is my book?" He said: "Tattooing." He said: "And who are my messengers?" He said: "Soothsayers." He said: "And where is my dwelling?" He said: "Bathhouses." He said: "And where is my seat?" He said: "Markets." He said: "What is my food?" He said: "What has not had God's name mentioned over it." He said: "What is my drink?" He said: "Every intoxicant." He said: "And what are my snares?" He said: "Women." He said: "And what is my call to prayer?" He said: "Flutes." [Related by Ibn al-Jawzi in Dhamm al-Hawa, p. 155, through al-Tabarani's al-Mu'jam al-Kabir. It is munkar, transmitted solely by Yahya ibn Salih; the authentic part of it is: "and your food is what God's name has not been mentioned over." See Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah 4/67.]

God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And promise them﴾: that is, give them fair hopes in your obedience. It is said: say to them, "There is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection."

﴿And Satan promises them only delusion﴾. Al-ghurur is decorating falsehood with what is thought to be truth.

If it is asked: how did God mention these things when He says: "Indeed, God does not command immorality" [al-A'raf: 28]?

It is answered: this is in the manner of a threat, like His saying: ﴿Do what you will﴾ [Fussilat: 40], and like the saying of one who says: "Do what you wish, you will see." [See Zad al-Masir 5/59.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 65–69:

His saying ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning: a Guardian to whom affairs are entrusted. His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships﴾, meaning: He propels and makes the ships run for you ﴿upon the sea that you may seek of His bounty﴾, that you may seek of His provision ﴿Indeed He is ever, to you, Merciful﴾. ﴿And when adversity touches you upon the sea﴾, meaning hardship and the fear of drowning, ﴿those you invoke vanish﴾, meaning: they are lost and fall away, from among the deities ﴿except Him﴾, except Allah. So you find no helper other than Him and besides Him. ﴿But when He delivers you [safely] to the land, you turn away﴾, meaning: when He answers your supplication and saves you from the terror of the sea and brings you out ﴿to the land, you turn away﴾ from faith, sincerity and obedience, disbelieving in His blessings. ﴿And mankind is ever ungrateful﴾. ﴿Do you then feel secure﴾ after that ﴿that He will cause you to sink﴾, make you sink ﴿into the side of the land﴾, the region of the land, which is the earth, ﴿or send against you a storm of stones﴾, meaning: He will rain down upon you stones from the sky, as He rained down upon the people of Lot. Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Qutaybi said: al-Hasib (the storm of stones) is the wind that hurls pebbles, which are small stones. ﴿Then you will not find for yourselves any guardian﴾. Qatadah said: any preventer.

﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you therein﴾, meaning in the sea, ﴿another time﴾, once more, ﴿and send against you a violent wind [of shattering]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning a raging wind, which is a violent wind.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is the wind that shatters everything, meaning crushes and smashes it.

Al-Qutaybi said: it is the one that breaks trees, meaning snaps them.

﴿And drown you for what you denied. Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any pursuer﴾, meaning a helper or an avenger. "Tabi'" means "tabi'" (follower), meaning one who follows and demands vengeance. It was also said: one who will pursue us with denial.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "an nakhsifa wa nursila wa nu'idakum fanursila fanughriqakum" with the nun in all of them, in accordance with His saying "'alayna" (against Us). The others recited with the ya', in accordance with His saying "illa iyyahu" (except Him). Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub recited "fa-tughriqakum" with the ta', meaning the wind.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 70:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified, ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: it is that they eat with their hands, whereas non-human creatures eat with their mouths from the ground. And it is narrated from him that he said: it is by intellect ('aql).

Al-Dahhak said: by speech (nutq). 'Ata' said: by the uprightness and erectness of their stature, whereas beasts are hunched over their faces. It was also said: by beauty of form. It was said: men by their beards and women by their long tresses. It was said: by His subjecting all other things to them. It was said: by the fact that among them is the best nation brought forth for mankind [[See: Zad al-Masir: 5/63; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/294. Al-Qurtubi preferred that the superiority is through intellect, which is the foundation of moral accountability, by which one knows God, understands His speech, reaches His bliss, and presents His messengers. However, since intellect alone does not accomplish everything intended from the servant, messengers were sent and books were revealed. The example of the Shari'ah is the sun, and the example of the intellect is the eye: when it is opened and sound, it sees the sun and perceives the details of things. Some of the sayings mentioned are stronger than others. God has also placed in some animals qualities by which the son of Adam is likewise surpassed, such as the running of the horse, its hearing and sight, the strength of the elephant, the courage of the lion, and the generosity of the rooster. Honour and superiority, however, lie only in intellect, as we have explained. And God knows best.]].

﴿And We carried them on land and sea﴾, that is: We carried them on land upon beasts and on sea upon ships.

﴿And We provided them with good things﴾, meaning: delicious foods and drinks. Muqatil said: ghee, butter, dates, and sweets. He made the provision of others something that is not hidden.

﴿And We preferred them above many of those We have created, with [marked] preference﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is that He preferred them over many of those He created, not over all.

Some people said: they were preferred over all creation except the angels.

Al-Kalbi said: they were preferred over all creatures except a group of angels: Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, the Angel of Death, and their like.

Regarding the preference of angels over humans there is difference of opinion. Some said: they (humans) were preferred over all creation and over all the angels. The majority may be placed in the position of the whole, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? ... and most of them are liars﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 221-222), meaning all of them.

It is narrated in a hadith from Jabir, traced to the Prophet: "When God created Adam and his offspring, the angels said: 'O Lord, You created them; they eat, drink, and marry. So make this world for them and the Hereafter for us.' He, exalted is He, said: 'I will not make those whom I created with My hand and into whom I breathed of My spirit like those to whom I said: Be, and it was.'" [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" p. 100: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani in "al-Awsat" through the route of Muhammad ibn Mahan, who said: Talhah ibn Zayd narrated to us from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: ... 'Kana'. He said: No one narrated it from Safwan except Talhah, and Abu Ghassan; Talhah alone was narrated by Muhammad ibn Mahan. From Abu Ghassan Hajjaj al-A'war, the route of Hajjaj was reported in "al-Mu'jam al-Kabir," and its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat). It has a witness in 'Abd al-Razzaq's Tafsir from Ma'mar from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said ... as a statement of his own (mawquf). Al-Daraqutni said in "al-'Ilal": 'Abd al-Majid ibn Abi Dawud narrated from Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, similar to it. He said: Sharih ibn Yunus narrated it from 'Abd al-Majid as mawquf, and this is more correct. It has another witness in al-Tabarani's "Musnad al-Shamiyyin" and al-Bayhaqi's "al-Asma' wa al-Sifat," through the narration of 'Abd Rabbih ibn Salih from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym that he heard him narrate from Jabir..." The Khatib mentioned it in "Mishkat al-Masabih" 3/1597 and attributed it to al-Daylami in "Musnad al-Firdaws" and al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman."]].

The most appropriate thing to say is: the common believers are superior to the common angels, and the elite believers are superior to the elite angels. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—those are the best of creatures﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 7].

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "The believer is more honoured by God than the angels who are with Him" [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman" through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah from Abu al-Mihzam from Abu Hurayrah as a statement of his (mawquf). Ibn Majah also narrated it through this route as mawquf: 2/1301. Abu al-Mihzam is weak. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 100.]].

The Qur'an, ﴿On the Day We shall summon every people with their leader﴾: Mujahid and Qatadah said, "with their prophet." Abu Salih and al-Dahhak said, "with their Book that was revealed to them."

Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah said, "with their deeds."

Qatadah also said, "with their Book, in which their deeds are recorded, as indicated by the context of the verse."

﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾. The Book is also called an imam, as the Mighty and Majestic said: "And We have enumerated everything in a clear imam" [Ya-Sin: 12].

It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "with the imam of their time, who called them in the world to misguidance or to guidance." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73], and He said: "And We made them leaders calling to the Fire" [al-Qasas: 41].

It was also said: "with their object of worship."

It is narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "Every people gather around their leader, in good and in evil."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿with their imam﴾: it was said, "that is, with their mothers." In this there are three wise purposes. The first: for the sake of 'Isa, peace be upon him. The second: to honour al-Hasan and al-Husayn. The third: so that the children of fornication will not be disgraced.

[[See these sayings and others in: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/296-297; al-Tabari: 15/126-127; Zad al-Masir: 5/64-65; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/316-317. Al-Tabari said: "The sayings closest to the truth in our view are the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: On the day We summon every people with the imam they used to follow and be led by in the world, because the more common usage of the Arabs of 'imam' is for that which is followed and led by. Directing the meanings of Allah's speech to the more well-known meaning is preferable, unless a proof to the contrary is established, which must be accepted."]].

﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand, those will read their record, and they will not be wronged the slightest bit (fatil)﴾, meaning: not even the amount of a fatil will be diminished from their due.

[["Al-fatil" is that which is twisted. What is in the cleft of a date-stone is called fatil because it is in the shape of something twisted, and it is what you twist between your fingers from thread or dirt. The word is used as a proverb for something insignificant. A she-camel "fatla' al-dhira'ayn" means one with firmly twisted forelegs (muhkamah). See: Mufradat al-Qur'an by al-Raghib al-Isfahani, p. (371).]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 17, verse 72:**

﴿Whoever is blind in this [life]﴾. The scholars differed over the reference of "this" (hadhihi). Some said: it refers to the blessings that Allah the Exalted enumerated in these verses, from His words ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you﴾ up to His words ﴿and preferred them greatly﴾. The meaning is: whoever among you is blind to these blessions, which he has witnessed, ﴿then he is in﴾ the matter of ﴿the Hereafter﴾, which he has not witnessed or seen, ﴿blind and further astray in way﴾. This is narrated from Ibn Abbas. [[Narrated by al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/317.]]

Others said: it refers to this world. The meaning is: whoever in this world is blind of heart to the sight of Allah's power and His signs, and to seeing the truth, then in the Hereafter he is blind, meaning more intensely blind, and further astray in way, meaning more mistaken in path. [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/317.]]

It has also been said: whoever is blind in this world to reflection (i'tibar) will be blind in the Hereafter to excuse (i'tidhar).

al-Hasan said: whoever in this world is astray and a disbeliever, he will be blind and further astray in the Hereafter, because in this world his repentance is accepted, but in the Hereafter his repentance is not accepted. [[al-Tabari preferred the view that the meaning is: whoever in this world is blind to the proofs of Allah, that He alone created it, governs it, and directs what is in it, then in the matter of the Hereafter, which he has not seen or witnessed, and in what will occur there, he is blind and further astray, meaning more astray in path than he is in the matters of this world, which he has witnessed and seen. ... For Allah the Exalted did not specify, in His words "whoever is blind in this," the blindness of the disbeliever to some of His proofs in this world rather than others, so that it would be directed to his blindness to His blessings, by which He honoured him over the children of Adam... See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/128-129.]]

Some reciters (qurra') inclined these two letters (i.e., the vowel of the words ʿamā and aḍall, as in the pronunciation of ﴿أَعْمَى﴾ in both places), while others pronounced them with a fatha. Abu Amr used to pronounce the first with a kasra and the second with a fatha, so that the meaning is: ﴿then he is in the Hereafter, more intensely blind﴾, in accordance with His words ﴿and further astray in way﴾.

Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 17, verse 73:

His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We have revealed to you﴾ and so on. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of its revelation (*sabab al-nuzul*, the specific circumstance that prompted it):

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to touch the Black Stone, but the Quraysh prevented him and said: [We will not leave you alone] [[In manuscript "B": "We will not leave you alone."]] until you touch our gods and make contact with them. So he spoke to himself: "What harm is there if I do that, while Allah, the Exalted, knows that I dislike it, so that they will leave me alone and I can touch the Black Stone?" [[Narrated by al-Tabari (15/130) and Ibn Abi Hatim (cited in al-Durr al-Manthur, 15/318). Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 335. See also al-Qurtubi (10/299). Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir (5/67-68): "This is false. It is not permissible to suppose this of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), nor what is reported from Atiyyah, that he intended to give them a year's respite. All of that is impossible with regard to him, and with regard to the Companions, that they transmitted it."]]

It was also said: They asked him to touch their gods so that they would become Muslims and follow him, and he spoke to himself about that, so Allah revealed this verse. [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh, from Ibn Abbas and from Jabir through the route of al-Kalbi, who is weak. See al-Durr al-Manthur 5/318, and refer to the previous note.]]

Ibn Abbas said: The delegation of Thaqif came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We will pledge allegiance to you on condition that you grant us three things." He said: "And what are they?" They said: "That we are not made to bow (in prayer)-meaning in the prayer-and that we do not break our idols with our own hands, and that you let us enjoy al-Lat for a year without our worshipping it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no good in a religion without bowing or prostration. As for breaking your idols with your own hands, that is up to you. As for the tyrant, meaning al-Lat and al-Uzza, I will not let you enjoy them." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we would like the Arabs to hear that you have given us what you have not given anyone else. If you fear that the Arabs will say, 'You gave them what you did not give us,' then say: 'Allah commanded me to do so.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent, and the people hoped, through his silence, that he would grant them that. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse. [[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi (p. 100): "I have not found it. al-Tha'labi mentioned it from Ibn Abbas without a chain of transmission." Al-Wahidi also mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 335. Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, turned away from all these reports and did not mention them in his tafsir.]]

﴿And indeed they almost tempted you﴾: they would divert you ﴿away from that which We have revealed to you﴾ ﴿so that you would fabricate﴾: so that you would invent ﴿against Us other than it﴾. ﴿And then﴾: if you had done what they called you to, ﴿they would have taken you as a close friend (khalil)﴾: that is, they would have allied themselves with you and shown you friendship.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 74–76:

﴿And had We not made you firm,﴾ upon the truth by Our protection, ﴿you would nearly have inclined toward them a little.﴾ That is: you would have leaned toward them, ﴿a little.﴾ That is: approximately toward the act.

If it is said: The Prophet ﷺ was protected (ma'sum), so how could he come close to what they asked for, when what they asked for was disbelief?

It is said: That was a passing thought of the heart and was not a firm resolve, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, pardoned (in one version: "overlooked") the mere stirrings of the soul.

Qatadah said: The Prophet ﷺ would say after that: "O Allah, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye."

[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" (p. 101): "I have not found it; al-Tha'labi mentioned it from Qatadah as a mursal report." It has already been noted that this statement is sufficient to judge it fabricated, and the author's not relying on it and preferring another answer indicates his weakness in it. Compare al-Tabari: 15/131.]

The correct answer is that Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would nearly have inclined toward them a little﴾; Allah made him firm and he did not incline. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few﴾ [An-Nisa: 83]. [He showed grace, so they did not follow.]

﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] of life and double [punishment] of death.﴾ That is: had you done that, We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death; that is, We would have doubled the punishment for you in this world and the Hereafter.

It was also said: "al-Di'f" (the double) is the punishment, and it was called "di'f" because the pain in it is multiplied.

﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper.﴾ That is: a helper who would prevent you from Our punishment.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, they almost drove you from the land to expel you from it.﴾ Scholars differed regarding the meaning of this verse. Some said: this verse is Madani. Al-Kalbi said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, the Jews disliked his residing in Madinah out of envy, so they came to him and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you know this is not a land of the prophets; the land of the prophets is al-Sham (Syria). [It is the Holy Land, where Ibrahim and the prophets, upon them be peace, dwelt. If you are a prophet like them, then go to al-Sham.] What prevents you from going there is your fear of the Romans, and Allah will protect you from the Romans if you are His messenger." So the Prophet ﷺ encamped at a distance of three miles from Madinah; and in another narration: at Dhu al-Hulayfah, until his companions gathered to him and he set out. Then Allah revealed this verse. And "the land" here is Madinah.

[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" (p. 101): "I have not found it; al-Suhayli mentioned it in "al-Rawd al-Unf" from Abd al-Majid ibn Bahram from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm..." Ibn Kathir said (3/54): It was said it was revealed concerning the Jews when they suggested to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he settle in al-Sham, the land of the prophets, and leave Madinah. This view is weak, because this verse is Makki and his residence in Madinah came afterward. It was also said that it was revealed at Tabuk, but its authenticity is questionable. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from al-Hakim from al-Asamm from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Ataridi from Yunus ibn Bukayr from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm... and related the story, then said: "There is doubt in this chain, and the more apparent view is that this is not authentic, for the Prophet ﷺ did not campaign to Tabuk on the saying of the Jews, but rather in compliance with the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers adjacent to you...'" See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 10/301; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 336. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred the following narration over this one.]

Mujahid and Qatadah said: "The land" is the land of Makkah, and the verse is Makki. The polytheists intended to expel him from it, so Allah restrained them from him until He commanded him to emigrate, and he left of his own accord. This is the most fitting reading of the verse, because what precedes it is a report about the people of Makkah, and the surah is Makki. [This is what al-Tabari preferred in his tafsir: 15/133, and al-Qurtubi; see Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 336.]

It was also said: they are all the disbelievers, who intended to drive him out of the land of the Arabs by gathering together and banding against him. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, protected His Messenger ﷺ, and they did not attain what they hoped for. And "istifzaz" is to disturb and dislodge quickly.

﴿And then they would not remain after you﴾ — that is, after you, ﴿except a little.﴾ Ibn Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Ya'qub read ﴿khilafaka﴾, by analogy with His saying: ﴿Those who stayed behind rejoiced in their sitting [behind] after the Messenger of Allah (khilaf rasul Allah)﴾ [At-Tawbah: 81]; and the meaning of both is one. [That is, the meaning of "khilafaka" and "khalfaka"; Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr from Asim read the second. The author's wording suggests a lacuna, but there is none, since the manuscript's text reads "khalfaka". See Zad al-Masir 5/70.]

﴿Except a little﴾ — that is: they would not remain after you except a little until they perished. So according to the first view, it is the duration of their lives; and according to the second, it is the period between the Prophet ﷺ's departure to Madinah and their being killed at Badr.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 77:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿A practice (sunnah) with those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾, meaning: like Our practice. It is in the accusative by deleting the kaf (the particle "like"). And the practice of Allah regarding the messengers, when their peoples denied them, is that He does not punish them as long as their prophet is among them; but when their prophet comes out from among them, He punishes them.

﴿And you will not find any alteration in Our practice﴾, meaning, any change (tabdil).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 78:

His saying: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾. The scholars differed concerning "dulūk" (decline). It is related from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: "Dulūk is the setting (ghurūb)," and this is the view of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī.

Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar and Jābir said: "It is the sun's passing the meridian (zawāl)," and this is the view of ʿAṭāʾ, Qatādah, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan and most of the Successors (tābiʿūn).

The meaning of the word encompasses both, because the root meaning of dulūk is inclination, and the sun inclines when it passes the meridian and when it sets.

Yet taking it to mean passing the meridian is the stronger of the two views, because many hold it, and because if we interpret it so, the verse comprises all the times of prayer: "decline of the sun" includes the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers; "until the darkness of the night" includes Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ; and "the recitation of dawn" is the Ṣubḥ prayer. [[See the detailed discussion in: Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 10/303-307; Zād al-Masīr 5/72-74; Aḥkām al-Qur'ān of al-Jaṣṣāṣ: 5/31-32; Aḥkām al-Qur'ān of Ibn al-ʿArabī: 3/1219 and following.]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾, meaning: the appearance of its darkness. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The beginning of the night." Qatādah said: "The time of the Maghrib prayer." Mujāhid said: "The setting of the sun."

﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾, meaning: the Ṣubḥ prayer. It was called "recitation" (qurʾān) of dawn because it is not valid except with recitation (qurʾān).

The grammatical position of "qurʾān" is of two aspects. The first: it is in coordination (ʿaṭf) with "the prayer," i.e., "and establish the recitation of dawn," as said by al-Farrāʾ. The people of Basra said: it is in the sense of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e., "and keep to the recitation of dawn."

﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾, meaning: it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī informed us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Nuʿaymī informed us: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us: Abu al-Yamān narrated to us: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me that Abū Hurayrah said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The prayer in congregation exceeds the prayer of one of you alone by twenty-five degrees, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Fajr prayer.'" Then Abū Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾." [[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Adhān, chapter "The virtue of the Fajr prayer in congregation": 2/137.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 79 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it﴾, meaning: stand up after your sleep. Tahajjud (rising from sleep to pray) occurs only after sleep. It is said: "tahajjada" when one rises after having slept, and "hajada" when one sleeps.

The intended meaning of the verse is standing in the night for prayer.

The night prayer was obligatory upon the Prophet ﷺ at the beginning, and upon the community, due to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, stand [in prayer] through the night, except a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1]. Then the lightening came down, and the obligation was abrogated (mansukh) with respect to the community by the five daily prayers, and the recommendation remained. He, may He be exalted, said: "So recite what is easy of it" [al-Muzzammil: 20]. The obligation remained with respect to the Prophet ﷺ [[al-Qurtubi said: (10/308-309): In this there is a difficulty for two reasons: calling an obligation a voluntary act, which is a metaphor and not a literal meaning. Second: the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Five prayers which Allah has enjoined upon the servants," and the saying of the Exalted in the hadith of the Night Journey: "They are five, and they are fifty; the word does not change with Me," and this is an explicit text, so how can it be said that an additional prayer beyond the five was made obligatory upon him? This is not valid, even though it has been narrated from him, upon him be prayers and peace: "Three are obligatory upon me..."]].

It is narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Three are obligatory upon me and are a sunnah for you: the witr [and the siwak] [[Omitted from "B".]] and the night prayer." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and in its chain is Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-San'ani, who is a liar; see Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/264. From Ibn Abbas, it was narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/231, al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 2/468, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/300. al-Dhahabi said: al-Hakim did not comment on it, and it is strange and munkar, and Yahya (weakened it); al-Nasa'i and al-Daraqutni weakened him. al-Haythami said: Ahmad and al-Bazzar narrated it with chains, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat; in their chains is Jabir al-Ju'fi, who is weak, and Abu Janab al-Kalbi is a mudallis. See also: Nasb al-Rayah 2/115; Talkhis al-Habir 3/118; Fayd al-Qadir 3/309; Majma' al-Zawa'id 8/264.]]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿as an extra [prayer] for you﴾, meaning: an additional [act] for you, i.e., an excellence exceeding all the other obligations which Allah has enjoined upon you.

Some people held that the obligation was abrogated with respect to him as it was with respect to the community, so it became a voluntary act (nafilah). This is the view of Mujahid and Qatadah, because Allah, exalted is He, said "as an extra for you" and did not say "obligatory upon you" [[See: Zad al-Masir 5/75-76; al-Qurtubi 10/308-309; Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 5/32-33.]].

If it is said: what is the meaning of the specification, since it is an addition for all Muslims just as it is for him ﷺ?
It is said: the specification is in that the voluntary acts of servants are an expiation for their sins, and the Prophet ﷺ had been forgiven what preceded of his sin and what followed, so his voluntary acts did not operate in expiating sins, and thus there remains for him an increase in the elevation of ranks.

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Juzjani informed us: Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us: Abu Sa'id al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Qutaybah and Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, both saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood [in prayer] until his feet swelled. It was said to him: "Do you burden yourself with this, when Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed?" He said: "Shall I not be a grateful servant?" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin": 8/584; and in Tahajjud, chapter on the Prophet's ﷺ night standing: 3/14; Muslim in Sifat al-Munafiqin, chapter on increasing deeds and striving in worship, no. (2819): 4/2171; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/44; the narration of al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah p. (159).]]

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Qays ibn Makhramah, that he informed him, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, that he said: "I will surely watch the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tonight," so I lay down at his threshold or his tent. He stood and prayed two light rak'ahs, then prayed two long rak'ahs, then prayed two rak'ahs less than the previous two, [then prayed two rak'ahs less than the previous two, then prayed two rak'ahs less than the previous two] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]], then he prayed witr; that was thirteen rak'ahs. [[Narrated by Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on supplication in the night prayer and its standing, no. (765): 1/531-532; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 4/19.]]

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, that he informed him that he asked Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "How was the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Ramadan?" She said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not exceed eleven rak'ahs in Ramadan or in other than it. He prayed four, so do not ask about their beauty and length; then he prayed four, so do not ask about their beauty and length; then he prayed three." Aisha said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you sleep before you pray witr?" He said: "O Aisha, my eyes sleep but my heart does not sleep." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tahajjud, chapter on the Prophet's ﷺ standing in Ramadan and other than it: 3/33; Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the night prayer, no. (738): 1/509; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/504.]]

Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Isfara'ini informed us: Abu Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq informed us: Yunus ibn Harun ibn Abd al-A'la informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus, Ibn Abi Dhi'b and Umar ibn al-Harith informed me that Ibn Shihab informed them, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ "used to pray between finishing the Isha prayer and Fajr eleven rak'ahs, giving the salam after every two rak'ahs, then he would pray witr with one. He would prostrate for a duration in which one of you could recite fifty verses before raising his head. When the muezzin fell silent from the Fajr call and the dawn became clear to him, he would stand and pray two light rak'ahs, then lie down on his right side until the muezzin came to him for the iqamah, and then he would go out." Some of them add to others. [[Narrated by Muslim in the same place, no. (736): 1/508; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 4/7.]]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Munib informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We did not wish to see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the night praying except that we saw him, and we did not wish to see him sleeping except that we saw him." And he said: "He would fast during the month until we say he will not break any of it, and he would break [his fast] until we say he will not fast any of it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tahajjud, chapter on the Prophet's ﷺ standing after his sleep: 3/22, and in other places; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 4/47.]]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾. "Perhaps" (asa) from Allah, exalted is He, is binding, because He does not fail to give His servants what He has made them hope for, or to do with them what He has made them expect.

The praised station is the station of intercession for his community, because the first and the last will praise him therein. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani narrated to us: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri informed us: Hayah informed us, from Ka'b, from Alqamah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you hear the muezzin, say the same as he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten upon him. Then ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me, for it is a station in Paradise that should belong only to one of Allah's servants, and I hope that I am he. Whoever asks Allah for al-Wasilah for me, intercession becomes lawful for him." [[Narrated by Muslim in Salah, chapter on the recommendation of saying the same as the muezzin, no. (384): 1/288-289; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 2/274.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Ali ibn Abbas narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says, when he hears the call: 'O Allah, Lord of this complete call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and al-Fadilah, and raise him to the praised station which You have promised him,' my intercession becomes lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adhan, chapter on supplication at the call: 2/284.]]

Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Abd al-Rahim [[In "A": Abd al-Rahman. The text in "B" and from "Sharh al-Sunnah" is as given.]] ibn Munib informed us: Ya'la informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every prophet has a granted supplication, and I have kept my supplication as an intercession for my community, and it will reach those among you, God willing, who die not associating anything with Allah." [[Narrated by Muslim in Iman, chapter on the Prophet's ﷺ keeping his supplication as intercession for his community, no. (199): 1/189; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 5/6.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Minhal said: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The believers will be held back on the Day of Resurrection until they become distressed by that, and they will say: 'If only we sought intercession from our Lord, so that He would relieve us from our place.' So they will come to Adam and say: 'You are Adam, father of mankind; Allah created you with His hand, made you dwell in His Garden, made His angels prostrate to you, and taught you the names of all things. Intercede for us with your Lord, that He may relieve us from this place.' He will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention his sin which he committed, his eating from the tree when he had been forbidden it. But go to Noah, the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth.'

They will come to Noah, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention his sin which he committed, his asking his Lord about what he had no knowledge of. But go to Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful.' They will come to Abraham, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention the three lies he told. But go to Moses, a servant whom Allah gave the Torah, spoke to, and brought near as a confidant.'

He said: They will come to Moses, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention his sin which he committed in killing a soul [[In "B": he killed the Copt.]]. But go to Jesus, the servant of Allah, His messenger, the Spirit of Allah and His Word.'

They will come to Jesus, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that' [...] but go to Muhammad, a servant whom Allah has forgiven what preceded of his sin and what followed."

al-Baghawi said: He said: "They will come to me, and I will ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His house [[Al-Khattabi said in *A'lam al-Hadith* (4/1257): "His saying, 'in His house,' gives the impression of a place, like the wording in the earlier narration: 'and He is in His place.' The meaning of his saying, 'I will ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His house, and it will be granted to me to enter upon Him,' is: in His house, which He has prepared for His friends (awliya'), and that is Paradise, as in the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Allah calls to the abode of peace﴾ [Yunus: 25]. And as it is said: 'the House of Allah' and 'the Sanctuary of Allah,' meaning the House of Allah which He made a place of return for the people, and the Sanctuary which He made a safe place for them..." See also: *Fath al-Bari* 13/428, and *Umdat al-Qari* 24/132.]]. It will be granted to me to enter upon Him. When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me for as long as Allah wills that He leave me. Then He will say: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad, speak and you will be heard, intercede and your intercession will be accepted, and ask and you will be given.' He said: So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with a praise and glorification which He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will go out and bring them out, and I will admit them to Paradise."

Qatada said: "I also heard him say: 'I will go out and bring them out of the Fire and admit them to Paradise. Then I will return and ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His house, and it will be granted to me to enter upon Him. When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me for as long as Allah wills that He leave me. Then He will say: Raise your head, O Muhammad, speak and you will be heard, intercede and your intercession will be accepted, and ask and you will be given.' He said: So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with a praise and glorification which He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will go out and admit them to Paradise. [Then I will return a third time, and ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His house, and it will be granted to me to enter upon Him. When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me for as long as Allah wills that He leave me. Then He will say: Raise your head, O Muhammad, speak and you will be heard, intercede and your intercession will be accepted, and ask and you will be given. He said: So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with a praise and glorification which He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will go out and admit them to Paradise.]" [[Between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]]

Qatada said: "And I have also heard him say: 'I will go out and bring them out of the Fire and admit them to Paradise, until no one remains in the Fire except those whom the Qur'an has detained,'" meaning: for whom eternal abiding (khulud) has become obligatory. He said: "Then he recited this verse: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾." [He said: "And this praiseworthy station" [[Between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] is the one which your Prophet ﷺ was promised."] [[Al-Bukhari related it in *Tawhid*, chapter "Faces on that Day will be radiant..." 13/422.]]

And with this same chain he said: "Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us [[Between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, Ma'bad ibn Hilal al-Ghazzi related to us, who said: We went to Anas ibn Malik and he related the hadith of the intercession in its meaning, and said: 'I ask permission of my Lord and it is granted to me, and He inspires me with praises by which I praise Him, which do not come to me now. So I praise Him with those praises and fall down before Him in prostration. It is said: O Muhammad, raise your head, speak and you will be heard, [ask and you will be given,] [[Between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I say: O Lord, my community, my community! He says: Go, and bring out from the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a barleycorn of faith. So I go and do that. Then I return, and I praise Him with those praises, then I fall down before Him in prostration, and he mentioned the like. It is said: Go and bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom or a mustard seed of faith. So I go and do that. Then I return, and I praise Him with those praises, then I fall down before Him in prostration, and he mentioned the like. Then it is said: Go and bring out whoever has in his heart less, less, less than the weight of a mustard seed of faith. So I go and do that.'" When we left Anas, we passed by al-Hasan and greeted him, and we related the hadith to him up to this point. He said: "Go on." We said: "He did not add anything for us beyond this." He said: "He related it to me, and he was then gathered in its entirety, twenty years ago, just as he related it to you." Then he said: "Then I will return the fourth time, and praise Him with those praises, then fall down before Him in prostration. It will be said: O Muhammad, raise your head, speak and you will be heard, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I say: O my Lord, will You permit intercession for one who said: There is no god but Allah? He says: By My might, My majesty, My greatness and My magnificence, I will certainly bring out from it whoever said: There is no god but Allah." [[Al-Bukhari related it in *Tawhid*, chapter "The speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection with the Prophets," 13/473; and Muslim in *Iman*, chapter "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank," no. (193), 1/183-184.]]

It was related from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: "The sun will draw near on the Day of Resurrection until the sweat reaches the middle of the ear. While they are in that state, they will seek help from Adam, then from Musa, then from Muhammad ﷺ [so he will intercede, that judgment may be passed among the creation. He will walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door. On that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station, which all the gathered people will praise]." [[Al-Bukhari related it as a suspended narration (mu'allaq) in *Zakat*, chapter "Whoever asks people in order to increase his wealth," 3/338. It was related with a complete chain by al-Tabari in his *Tafsir* 15/146, al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani in *al-Awsat*, and Ibn Mandah in *al-Iman* 30/833, and he said: "This is a sound chain according to the method of al-Bukhari." See also: *Fath al-Bari* 3/339; *al-Durr al-Manthur* 5/325.]]

And al-Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad [[Between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] ibn Mamawayh informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan related to us, Muhammad ibn Hamawayh related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad related to us, al-Layth related to us from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am the first of them to come out [when they are raised], and I am their leader when they come as a delegation, and I am their speaker when they are silent, and I am their intercessor when they are held back, [and I am their bringer of good news when they despair]. Honor, the keys, and the banner of praise will on that day be in my hand. I am the most honored of the children of Adam before my Lord. A thousand servants will go around me, as if they were hidden eggs or scattered pearls." [[Al-Tirmidhi related it in *Manaqib*, chapter "What has come concerning the virtue of the Prophet ﷺ," 10/79, and said: "This is a good, strange hadith," and in some copies: "strange." Al-Darimi related it in the *Muqaddimah*, chapter "What the Prophet ﷺ was given of virtue," 1/26-27. The author related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* 13/203-204 and said: "This is a strange hadith," and in its chain is al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who is weak. See also: *Mishkat al-Masabih* 3/1605.]]

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, al-Hakam ibn Musa related to me, Ma'qil ibn Ziyad related to us from al-Awza'i, Abu Ammar related to me, Abdullah ibn Farrukh related to me, Abu Hurayra related to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and the first from whom the grave will be split open, and the first intercessor, and the first whose intercession is accepted." [[Muslim related it in *Fada'il*, chapter "The virtue of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over all creation," no. (2278), 4/1782; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah* 13/203-204.]]

The reports concerning intercession are many. The first to deny it was Amr ibn Ubayd, and he was an innovator (mubtadi') by the consensus of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) [[See the argument of the Khawarij (an early sect) for denying intercession for the people of major sins, their doubt, and the refutation of them in: *Majmu' Fatawa Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya* 1/116, 146-149; al-Qurtubi 10/310.]].

It was related from Yazid ibn Suhayb al-Faqir, who said: I had been captivated by an opinion of the Khawarij, and I was a young man. We set out in a group, intending to perform Hajj. We passed by Medina, and there was Jabir ibn Abdullah relating to the people from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned the people of Hell (al-Jahannamiyyin). I said to him: "O companion of the Messenger of Allah, what is this that they are relating? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, whomever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced⁠﴾ [Al 'Imran: 192], and ﴿Every time they wish to leave it, they will be returned to it⁠﴾ [al-Sajdah: 20]?" He said to me: "O young man, do you recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Have you heard of the station of Muhammad, the praiseworthy station, which Allah will raise him to?" I said: "Yes." He said: "It is the station of Muhammad, the praiseworthy, by which Allah will bring out whomever He brings out of the Fire [then he described the placing of the Sirat and the passing of the people over it], and that some people will come out of the Fire after they have been in it." He said: "So we returned and said: Do you think this shaykh lies about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" [[Muslim related it in *Iman*, chapter "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank," no. (191), 1/179.]]

It was related from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took Ibrahim as a khalil (intimate friend), and indeed your companion is the habib (beloved) of Allah and the most honored of creation before Allah." Then he recited: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station⁠﴾. [He said: "He will seat him upon the Throne."] [[Al-Haythami said in *Majma' al-Zawa'id* (8/55): "In the Sahih of it: 'And indeed your companion is the khalil of Allah' only, within a hadith related by al-Tabarani, and in its chain is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]] [[In "B": khalil.]] [[Omitted in "B".]]

[And from Mujahid concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station⁠﴾, he said: "He will seat him upon the Throne." [[Between the brackets is omitted in "B". The report from Mujahid was related by al-Tabari 15/145.]]]

And from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "He will seat him upon the Kursi (Footstool)." [[Al-Tabari said: The first opinion, explaining the praiseworthy station as intercession, is more correct, since the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is authentic concerning it. And even if this is the correct view, what Mujahid said is not rejected, neither by report nor by reasoning, because there is no report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor from any of his companions, nor from the Successors, that rules it out. See: *Tafsir al-Tabari* 15/145-147; *Tafsir al-Qurtubi* 10/311-312.]]

The Almighty said: ﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit﴾. What is meant by the "entrance" and the "exit" is the entering and the exiting. The people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) differed regarding it.

Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "Cause me to enter a sound entrance": Medina. "And cause me to exit a sound exit": Mecca. It was revealed when the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to migrate (hijrah).[[Narrated by Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi from Ibn Abbas. See Ibn Kathir: 3/59. This is also the view preferred by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: (15/150).]]

Al-Dahhak said: "And cause me to exit a sound exit": from Mecca, safe from the polytheists. "And cause me to enter a sound entrance": Mecca, triumphant over it through the conquest.

Mujahid said: Cause me to enter, through the matter of Yours with which You sent me, which is prophethood, a sound entrance, which is Paradise; and cause me to exit from the world, having fulfilled what was obligatory upon me of its rights, a sound exit.

It is narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "Cause me to enter a sound entrance": Paradise. "And cause me to exit a sound exit": from Mecca.

It was also said: Cause me to enter Your obedience and cause me to exit from what is forbidden. It was also said: its meaning is, "Cause me to enter wherever You cause me to enter with truthfulness, and cause me to exit with truthfulness," that is, do not make me among those who enter with one face and exit with another, for the one with two faces is neither safe nor honored in the sight of Allah.

He described the entering and the exiting as "sound" because of what the exit and the entrance lead to, namely victory, honor, and the ascendancy of the religion, just as He described a foot as "sound" when He said: ﴿that they have a sound footing with their Lord﴾ [Yunus: 2].

﴿And appoint for me from Yourself an authority, a helper﴾. Mujahid said: "authority" means a clear proof. Al-Hasan said: a strong kingdom with which You support me against whoever opposes me,[[In manuscript "A": "'adani" (opposed me).]] and an evident might through which I establish Your religion. So Allah promised him that He would strip the kingdom of Persia, Rome and others and give it to him.

Qatadah said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) knew that he had no capacity for this matter except with an authority [helper],[[Omitted from "A".]] so he asked for an authority as a helper: the Book of Allah, its limits, and the establishment of His religion.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 81:

The Most High said: ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and falsehood has vanished﴾, that is, Satan. Qatadah said, and al-Suddi said: "The truth" is Islam, and "the falsehood" is shirk. It was also said: "The truth" is the worship of Allah, and "the falsehood" is the worship of idols.

﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾, meaning departing. It is said: "his soul departed (zahaqat nafsuhu)", that is, it went out.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abd Allah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols (nusub). He began striking them with a stick [in his hand] and saying: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished." "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor restore." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, chapter: "And say, the truth has come and falsehood has vanished...": 8/400.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 82–83:

213/ His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾. It has been said: "min" (from) is not for partitive meaning, and its meaning is: "And We send down of the Qur'an that which is entirely a healing," i.e., a clarification (bayan) from error and ignorance, by which the disputed matter is made clear, the ambiguous is made evident, one is healed from doubt (shubha), and one is guided out of bewilderment (hayra). Thus it is a healing of hearts through the removal of ignorance from them, and a mercy for the believers.

﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾, because the wrongdoer does not benefit from it, whereas the believer is one who benefits from it, so it is a mercy for him.

It has also been said: the increase in loss for the wrongdoer is in that every verse that is revealed renews denial on their part, and their loss increases.

Qatadah said: No one sits with this Qur'an except that he rises from it with an increase or a decrease. God's decree, which He decreed, is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away﴾ from remembering Us and calling upon Us, ﴿and turns aside with his side﴾, i.e., he distances himself from Us by himself, meaning he abandons drawing near to God through supplication. 'Ata' said: he becomes arrogant and proud. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "wa-na'a" with a kasra on the nun and the hamza; Abu Bakr read the nun with a fatha and the hamza with a kasra; Ibn 'Amir and Abu Ja'far read "wa-na'a" like "ja'a." It has been said: it has the meaning of "na'a" (turned aside). It has also been said: "na'a" is from al-nawu, which means rising and standing up.

﴿And when evil touches him﴾, i.e., hardship and harm, ﴿he is despairing﴾, i.e., hopeless and despondent. It has been said: its meaning is that he supplicates and calls upon Him in time of harm and hardship, but when the answer is delayed, he despairs. A believer should not despair of the answer even if it is delayed, and so he should not abandon supplication.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 84–85:**

The words of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner (shakilatihi)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "According to his way (nahiyatihi)."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah [[Omitted from "A".]] said: "According to his intention (niyyatihi)."

Muqatil said: "According to his disposition (khaliqatihi)."

Al-Farra' said: "According to his way (tariqatihi) which he was created with (jubila 'alayha)."

Al-Qutaybi said: "According to his nature (tabi'atihi) and his innate constitution (jibillatihi)."

It was also said: "According to the path he has chosen for himself." It comes from *shakl*; one says, "You are not on my shakl, nor my shakilah." All of these meanings are close to one another. The Arabs say, "A *tariq dhu shawakil*" (a road with many branches) when its roads branch off from it. The meaning of the verse is: each acts in accordance with what resembles him, as it is said in the proverb: "Each person's deed resembles him."

﴿So your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way (sabilan)﴾: i.e., who has the clearest way (tariqan).

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And they ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is of the affair of my Lord﴾, and the rest of the verse.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] informed us: Qays ibn Hafs informed us: 'Abdul-Wahid — meaning Ibn Ziyad — informed us: al-A'mash informed us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abdullah, who said: "While I was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a field (harth) [[The place of cultivation.]] of Madinah, and he was leaning on a palm-frond stalk (asib) [[A palm-frond stalk.]] that he had with him, he passed by a group of Jews. Some of them said to others: 'Ask him about the Spirit.' Others said: 'Do not ask him, for he will not bring anything you dislike.' Then some of them said: 'We will certainly ask him.' A man among them stood up and said: 'O Abu al-Qasim, what is the Spirit?' He remained silent. I said: 'He is being revealed to.' So I stood up. When the revelation had withdrawn from him, he recited: ﴿And they ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is of the affair of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, Surah al-Isra', chapter "And they ask you about the Spirit": 8/401, and by Muslim in the Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter on the Jews asking the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Spirit, no. (2794): 4/2152.]] Al-A'mash said: "It is thus in our recitation."

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The Quraysh gathered and said: 'Muhammad grew up among us with trustworthiness and truthfulness, and we have never accused him of lying. Yet he has claimed what he has claimed. So send a group to the Jews in Madinah and ask them about him, for they are People of the Book.' So they sent a group to them. The Jews said: 'Ask him about three things. If he answers all of them, or does not answer any of them, then he is not a prophet. But if he answers two and does not answer one, then he is a prophet. Ask him about a group of youths who disappeared in the earliest times — what was their affair, for they had a wondrous story. And ask him about a man who reached the east and the west of the earth — what was his account. And ask him about the Spirit.'" So they asked him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will inform you tomorrow of what you asked," and he did not say, "If Allah wills." Then the revelation was delayed — Mujahid said: "Twelve nights." It was also said: "Fifteen days." 'Ikrimah said: "Forty days." The people of Makkah were saying: "Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and now we have reached the morning, and he has not told us anything." Thus the Prophet (ﷺ) was saddened by the delay of the revelation, and what the people of Makkah were saying distressed him. Then Jibril came down with the words: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," unless [adding], "If Allah wills"﴾. And concerning the story of the youths, ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs as a wonder?﴾ was revealed. And concerning the one who reached the east and the west, ﴿And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn﴾ was revealed. And concerning the Spirit, ﴿And they ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is of the affair of my Lord﴾ was revealed. [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq, al-Tabari, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi, all in *al-Dala'il*. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/357; Ibn Kathir: 3/72; Asbab al-Nuzul p. (338).]]

They differed about the Spirit concerning which the question was asked. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is Jibril, and this is also the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

It is narrated from 'Ali that he said: "It is an angel who has seventy thousand faces, each face has seventy thousand tongues, and he glorifies Allah the Exalted with all of them."

Mujahid said: "It is a creation in the forms of the children of Adam, having hands, feet and heads; they are neither angels nor people who eat food."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Allah the Exalted has not created a creature greater than the Spirit, apart from the Throne. If He willed to swallow the seven heavens, the seven earths and whoever is in them in a single morsel, He would do so. The form of its creation is like the form of the angels, and the form of its face is like the form of the sons of Adam. It will stand on the Day of Resurrection to the right of the Throne. It is the nearest of creatures to Allah the Exalted today, at the seventy veils; and on the Day of Resurrection it will be nearest to Allah. It is among those who intercede for the People of Tawhid (monotheism). Were it not that between it and the angels there is a veil of light, the people of the heavens would be burned by its light."

It was also said: "The Spirit is the Qur'an."

It was also said: "What is meant by it is 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, for he is the Spirit of Allah and His Word." Its meaning is: it is not as the Jews say, nor as the Christians say.

Some people said: "It is the spirit placed in creation by which a human lives, and this is the most correct view."

Some people spoke about it, and some of them said: "It is the blood. Do you not see that when an animal dies, nothing leaves it except the blood?"

Some people said: "It is the breath of the living creature, as evidenced by the fact that it dies when breath is held back."

Some people said: "It is an accident (*'arad*)."

Some people said: "It is a subtle body (*jism latif*)."

Some of them said: "The Spirit is a meaning in which light, goodness, elevation and permanence are combined. Do you not see that when it is present, the human is described by all these attributes; and when it departs, all of them are gone?" [[See these views in: Zad al-Masir: 5/82; al-Tabari: 15/156–157; Ibn Kathir: 3/62.]]

The most preferred of these sayings is that its knowledge be entrusted to Allah the Exalted, and this is the view of the Ahl al-Sunnah (people of the Sunnah). 'Abdullah ibn Buraydah said: "Indeed Allah has not made any honored angel or any sent prophet aware of the Spirit."

The words of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿Say: The Spirit is of the affair of my Lord﴾. It was said: "Of the knowledge of my Lord."

﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾: i.e., in comparison with the knowledge of Allah. [[See: Zad al-Masir: 5/83.]] It was said: "This is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ)."

It was also said: "It is addressed to the Jews, for they used to say: 'We were given the Torah, and in it is much knowledge.'"

It was also said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) knew the meaning of the Spirit, but he did not inform anyone of it, because his leaving off informing them about it was a sign of his prophethood."

The first view is more correct, because Allah the Exalted has reserved its knowledge for Himself.
