Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 86:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away what We have revealed to you﴾, meaning the Qur'an. Its meaning: just as We withheld the knowledge of the Spirit from you and from others, so too, if We willed, We could surely take away what We have revealed to you, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Then you would not find for yourself any guardian against Us in respect of it﴾, i.e., anyone who would undertake to restore the Qur'an to you.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 17, verses 87–88:**

﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord.﴾ This is a *istithna' munqati'* (disjunctive exception). Its meaning is: "But We do not will that, [rather We spare it] as a mercy from your Lord."

﴿Indeed, His favour upon you has been great.﴾ If it is asked: "How can the Qur'an be taken away when it is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?"

It is said: What is meant is its erasure from the *masahif* (copies of the Qur'an) and the removal of what is in the hearts.

'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Recite the Qur'an before it is lifted, for the Hour will not come until it is lifted." It was said to him: "These *masahif* are lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of people?" He said: "It will travel over it by night, so what is in their hearts is lifted, and they wake up not retaining anything and not finding anything in the *masahif*. Then they will turn to poetry."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman*, and al-Tabarani narrated a similar report, also as a *mawquf* (halted at a Companion) with a sound chain. See: *al-Durr al-Manthur* 5/334, *Fath al-Bari* 13/16. Ibn al-Jawzi said in *Zad al-Masir* (5/84): "Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi rejected the soundness of this hadith, citing the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him: 'Allah does not take away knowledge by snatching it away...' (agreed upon). Then he said: The report of Ibn Mas'ud is transmitted through several chains which are fair (*hasan*), so it is possible that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, meant by knowledge other than the Qur'an, for knowledge continues to decline until the lifting of the Qur'an is the last of the matter."]]

And on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: "The Hour will not come until the Qur'an returns to where it was revealed. It will have a humming around the Throne like the humming of bees. The Lord will say: 'What is the matter with you, when He is the most knowing?' It will say: 'O Lord, I am recited but I am not acted upon.'"[[Attributed in *Kanz al-'Ummal* (4/2033) to al-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws*. al-Suyuti noted that attribution to it indicates weakness.]]

**His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:** ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to help one another.﴾ "They are not able to do that." ﴿Even if they were to help one another﴾: "supporting and aiding one another."

It was revealed when the disbelievers said: "If we willed, we would say the like of this," so Allah the Exalted refuted them.[[See: *al-Bahr al-Muhit* 5/78.]]

Thus the Qur'an is inimitable (*mu'jiz*) in its arrangement, its composition, and its reports of the unseen. It is speech at the highest level of eloquence (*balaghah*), unlike the speech of created beings, because it is uncreated. And if it were created, they would have produced its like.

It will say: 'O Lord, I am recited but I am not acted upon.'"[[Attributed in *Kanz al-'Ummal* (4/2033) to al-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws*. al-Suyuti noted that attribution to it indicates weakness.]]

**His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:** ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to help one another.﴾ "They are not able to do that." ﴿Even if they were to help one another﴾: "supporting and aiding one another."

It was revealed when the disbelievers said: "If we willed, we would say the like of this," so Allah the Exalted refuted them.[[See: *al-Bahr al-Muhit* 5/78.]]

Thus the Qur'an is inimitable (*mu'jiz*) in its arrangement, its composition, and its reports of the unseen. It is speech at the highest level of eloquence (*balaghah*), unlike the speech of created beings, because it is uncreated. And if it were created, they would have produced its like.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 89–90:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly displayed for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, from every aspect, of lessons, rulings, promise, warning, and other things, ﴿but most of the people refused except disbelief﴾, meaning denial. [[Omitted from "A".]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "We will never believe you"﴾, meaning, "We will never affirm you," ﴿until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾. The people of Kufa and Ya'qub read *tafjura* (تَفْجُرَ) with a fatha on the *ta'* and a damma on the *jim*, lightened, because *al-yanbu'* (الْيَنْبُوعَ) is singular. The rest read it with shaddah, from *al-tafjir* (التَّفْجِيرِ). They agreed on the shaddah in His saying, ﴿then causes the rivers to gush forth within it abundantly﴾ (تَفْجِيرًا), because *al-anhar* (الْأَنْهَارَ) is plural, and the shaddah indicates multiplication, and because of His saying *tafjiran* (تَفْجِيرًا) after it.

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas that Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu al-Bukhturi ibn Hisham, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-As ibn Wa'il, and Nabih and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, gathered, along with whoever gathered with them, after the sun had set, at the side of the Ka'bah. Some of them said to others: "Send to Muhammad, talk to him, and dispute with him, until you are excused regarding him." So they sent to him: "The nobles of your people have gathered for you so that they may speak with you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them quickly, thinking that some new matter had arisen for them regarding his affair. He was eager for them and loved their guidance. He sat with them, and they said: "O Muhammad, we sent for you so that we might be excused regarding you. By Allah, we do not know of any man among the Arabs who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people. You have reviled the forefathers, condemned the religion, made foolish the minds, cursed the gods, and split the community. No ugly matter remains except that you have brought it between you and us. If you came with this speech seeking wealth, we will gather for you from our wealth until you are the richest of us. If you seek honour, we will make you our chief. If you want kingship, we will make you our king. And if this matter that is upon you is a *ra'i* (رَئِيٌّ), a jinn companion you see, which has overpowered you so that you cannot repel it, we will spend our wealth for you in seeking a physician until we cure you of it or are excused regarding you." They used to call the jinn follower the *ra'i*.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What I have is not what you say. I did not bring what I have brought to you seeking your wealth, nor honour over you, nor kingship over you. Rather, Allah sent me to you as a messenger, revealed to me a Book, and commanded me to be for you a bringer of good news and a warner. So I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord and given you sincere counsel. If you accept from me, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter. If you reject it from me, I will be patient over the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you."

They said: "O Muhammad, if you will not accept from us what we have offered you, then you know that no one is more constricted in lands than us, and no one is harder pressed in living than us. So ask your Lord who sent you to remove these mountains from us, for they have confined us, to spread out our lands for us, and to cause rivers to gush forth in them like the rivers of Syria and Iraq. And let Him raise up for us those of our forefathers who have passed away, and let Qusayy ibn Kilab be among them, for he was an elderly man who spoke truthfully. We will ask them about what you say: is it true or false? If they confirm you, we will confirm you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not sent with this. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with. If you accept it from me, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter. If you reject it, I will be patient over the command of Allah."

They said: "If you will not do this, then ask your Lord to send us an angel to confirm you, and ask Him to make for you gardens, palaces, and treasures of gold and silver, by which He will make you independent of what we see you doing, for you walk in the markets and seek livelihood as we seek it."

He said: "I was not sent with this. Rather, Allah sent me as a bringer of good news and a warner."

They said: "Then make the sky fall upon us, as you claimed that your Lord, if He willed, would do."

He said: "That is up to Allah. If He wills to do that to you, He will do it."

One of them said: "We will never believe you until you bring us Allah and the angels as a guarantee."

When they said that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah stood with him. He was the son of his paternal aunt, Atikah bint Abd al-Muttalib. He said: "O Muhammad, your people offered you what they offered you, and you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for things for themselves by which they would recognize your station with Allah the Exalted, and you did not do it. Then they asked you to hasten what you warn them of, of the punishment, and you did not do it. By Allah, I will never believe you until you take a ladder to the sky and climb up on it while I watch, until you arrive there, and bring with you a written scroll and a group of angels who testify for you to what you say. By Allah, even if you did that, I would think that I should not believe you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his family, grieved by what he saw of their aversion. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And they say, "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾ [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/295–297; Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/164–166; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. (338–340); Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/63–64.]] meaning: the land of Makkah. ﴿a spring﴾, meaning: springs.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 92–93:

﴿Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read *kisafan* with a fatha on the *sin*, meaning "pieces." It is the plural of *kisfah* (a piece or side), like *kisrah* and *kisar* (a fragment and fragments). The others read it with a sukun on the *sin*, in the singular form, and its plural is *aksaf* and *kusuf*. The meaning is: You make it fall on us as a single layer [[Text in brackets "[wahidan]" is absent from manuscript "A".]]. It was also said that he meant its side falling upon us. It was also said that its meaning is likewise "pieces," and it is the broken plural (*jam' al-taksir*, the irregular plural pattern), like *sidrah* and *sidr* in surat al-Shu'ara' and Saba'. Hafs reads *kisafan* with a fatha. In surat al-Rum, Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read it with a sukun.

﴿Or You bring God and the angels as a *qabil*﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: *kafilan*, meaning they will stand surety for what you say. Al-Dahhak said: *damina*n (guarantors). Mujahid said: it is the plural of *qabilah* (tribe), meaning with all kinds of angels, tribe by tribe. [[Text in brackets is absent from manuscript "B".]] Qatada said: *'ayanan*, meaning you see them face to face, i.e., openly seen. [[Text in brackets is absent from manuscript "B".]] Al-Farra' said: it is from the Arab saying "I met so-and-so *qabilan* and *qubulan*," meaning face to face.

﴿Or you have a house of gold﴾, i.e., of gold. Its root meaning is adornment. ﴿Or you ascend﴾, climb ﴿into the sky﴾. This is the statement of 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya. ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending﴾, your climbing up, ﴿until you bring down to us a book that we can read﴾, in which we are commanded to follow you. ﴿Say: Glory be to my Lord﴾. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read *qala* ("he said"), meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). The others read it as an imperative, meaning: Say, O Muhammad. ﴿Am I anything but a human messenger?﴾ He was commanded to glorify and exalt God, in the sense that if God willed to send down what they asked for, He would do it. But God does not send down signs according to what humans propose. "I am only a human, and what you ask is not within human capacity."

Know that God the Exalted has given the Prophet (ﷺ) signs and miracles that suffice instead of all of this, such as the Qur'an, the splitting of the moon, water gushing from between the fingers, and similar things. Most of that people were obstinate; their aim was not to seek evidence so that they might believe. So God rejected their demand.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said﴾ out of ignorance ﴿"Has God sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ He means: the disbelievers used to say, "We will not believe you because you are a human. Why did God not send an angel to us?" God answered them: ﴿Say: "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth"﴾ ﴿Say: "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth"﴾ settling and dwelling there, ﴿We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger"﴾ of their own kind, because the heart inclines more toward its own kind than toward other kinds.

﴿Say: "God is sufficient as a witness between me and you"﴾ that I am the messenger of God to you [[In manuscript "B": "that I am His messenger to you."]] ﴿Indeed He is ever Aware of and Seeing of His servants﴾. [214/a] His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whomever God guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He leads astray, you will not find for them allies besides Him﴾ who could guide them ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces﴾

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; al-Hasan ibn Shuja al-Sufi, known as Ibn al-Mawsili, informed us; Abu Bakr ibn al-Haytham reported to us; Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sa'igh narrated to us; Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas: that a man said, "O Messenger of God, how will the disbeliever be gathered upon his face on the Day of Resurrection?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The One who made him walk on his feet is able to make him walk on his face." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary on Surat al-Furqan, chapter "Those who will be gathered upon their faces to Hell": 8/492; and by Muslim in the book on the hypocrites, chapter "The disbeliever will be gathered upon his face," no. (2806): 4/2161.]]

And it has come in a hadith: "They will protect their faces with them from every thorn and stump." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the commentary on Surat al-Isra, 8/579, who said: "This is a hasan hadith"; and by Ahmad in his Musnad: 2/354, 363; and by al-Tabari in his commentary, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Mardawayh. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/341.]]

﴿Blind, mute, and deaf﴾

If it is asked: how did He describe them as blind, mute, and deaf, when He also said: "And the criminals will see the Fire" [al-Kahf: 53], and said: "There they will call for destruction" [al-Furqan: 13], and said: "They will hear from it raging and roaring" [al-Furqan: 12], thereby affirming sight, speech, and hearing?

It is said: they will be gathered in the state that God described, and then these faculties will be returned to them.

Another answer: Ibn Abbas said: "Blind, meaning they do not see what would please them; mute, meaning they do not speak with any proof; deaf, meaning they do not hear anything that would please them."

Al-Hasan said: this is when they are driven to the place of standing (al-Mawqif) until they enter the Fire.

Muqatil said: this is when it is said to them: "Be silent in it and do not speak to Me" [al-Mu'minun: 108], and then all of them become blind, mute, and deaf: they do not see, do not speak, and do not hear.

﴿Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides﴾ Ibn Abbas said: "whenever it quiets," meaning its blaze calms down. Mujahid said: "is extinguished." Qatadah said: "weakens." It was also said: it means calm without any actual decrease in the pain of the disbelievers, because God, exalted is He, said: "Its punishment will not be lightened for them" [al-Zukhruf: 75]. It was also said that "whenever it subsides" means: whenever it wishes to subside. ﴿We increase them in blaze﴾ meaning: fuel.

It was also said: the meaning of His saying "whenever it subsides" is: when their skins have been roasted and burned, they are returned to their former state, and the kindling of the Fire is increased to burn them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 98–99:

﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we have become bones and crumbled dust, shall we truly be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ Allah, the Exalted, answered them, saying: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth,﴾ ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth,﴾ in their greatness and strength, ﴿is able to create the like of them,﴾ in their smallness and weakness. A parallel to this is His statement, Exalted is He: "The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind" [Ghafir: 57].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 100–101:

﴿Say: "If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord..."﴾ That is, the bounty of my Lord. It is also said: the provision of my Lord. ﴿Then you would surely withhold^ for fear of spending﴾ That is, you would be stingy and hold back ﴿for fear of spending.﴾ That is, for fear of poverty, as Qatadah said.

It is also said: for fear of exhaustion. It is said: "anfaqa al-rajul" means he became destitute and his wealth was gone, and "nafaqa al-shay'" means it was gone.

It is also said: "You would withhold from spending for fear of poverty."

﴿And man has always been stingy﴾ That is, miserly, holding back from spending.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We gave Moses nine clear signs﴾ That is, clear proofs, manifest. These are the nine signs.

Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: they are the staff, the white hand, the knot that was in his tongue which He loosened, the splitting of the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood.

Ikrimah, Qatadah, Mujahid and Ata said: they are the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff, the hand, the years of drought, and the reduction of fruits.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi mentioned: the effacing (of faces) and the sea, instead of the years of drought and the reduction of fruits. He said: "A man among them would be with his wife in his bed, and he had turned into two stones, and a woman among them would be standing baking, and she had turned into a stone."

Some of them said: they are the verses of the Book.^[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/171–173; Zad al-Masir: 5/92–93; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/343–344; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/67–68.]]

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Attar informed us: Yusuf ibn Abd Allah ibn Mahan informed us: al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abd Allah ibn Salamah, from Safwan ibn Assal al-Muradi, that a Jew said to his companion: "Come, let us ask this Prophet." The other said: "Do not say 'Prophet,' for if he hears, we will have four eyes." So they came to him and asked him about this verse: ﴿And We gave Moses nine clear signs﴾. He said: "Do not associate anything with Allah, do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, do not commit adultery, do not consume usury, do not practise sorcery, do not walk with an innocent person to a ruler so that he may kill him, do not waste, do not slander a chaste woman, do not flee from the battlefield, and upon you, specifically the Jews, (is this): do not transgress on the Sabbath." So they kissed his hand and said: "We testify that you are a Prophet." He said: "What prevents you from following me?" They said: "Dawud (David) supplicated his Lord that there would never cease to be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we follow you, the Jews will kill us."^[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir, Surat al-Isra': 8/580, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also by al-Nasa'i in Tahrim al-Dam, chapter on sorcery: 7/111–112; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/239–240; and al-Tabari in the Tafsir: 15/172. Ibn Majah narrated it in abridged form from Safwan ibn Assal that a group of Jews kissed the hand and feet of the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said (3/68): "This is a problematic hadith. Abd Allah ibn Salamah has something in his memory, and they have spoken about him. Perhaps the nine signs were confused with the ten words, for they are the commandments in the Torah, which have no connection to establishing the proof against Pharaoh. And Allah knows best."]]

﴿So ask﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the Children of Israel, when he came to them﴾ Moses. It is possible that the address is to him (the Prophet ﷺ) while the intended meaning is others. It is also possible that He addressed Moses (peace be upon him) and commanded him to ask, so that their lie before their people would be made clear.

﴿Pharaoh said to him: "Indeed I think you, O Moses, are bewitched"﴾ That is, one who has been affected by magic; they bewitched you. Al-Kalbi said this.

Ibn Abbas said: "deceived."

It is also said: "turned away from the truth."

Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaydah said: "a sorcerer," so the passive participle was placed in the sense of the active participle.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: "one who has been given knowledge of magic, so these wonders you perform are from your sorcery."^[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/174.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 102:

﴿He said﴾ Moses, ﴿"You certainly know"﴾. The common reciters (al-'Amma) read the taa' with a fatha, as an address to Pharaoh. Al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and this is also reported from 'Ali. He said: "The wicked one did not know that Moses was upon the truth; had he known, he would have believed. Rather, it is Moses who knew."[[Al-Tabari said: "However, the reading upon which the reciters of the cities agree is other than this, and it is not permissible in our view to oppose the proof of what has come with the reading on which there is consensus." Tafsir: 15/174.]] Ibn 'Abbas said: "Pharaoh knew it, but he was obstinate." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ [An-Naml: 14].

This reading, the fatha on the taa', is more sound in meaning, and most reciters follow it, because Moses cannot be argued against with his own knowledge. The damma reading from 'Ali is not firmly established, since it was narrated from a man of the tribe of Murad, from 'Ali, and that man is unknown. None of the reciters adopted it except al-Kisa'i.[[Likewise Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir (5/94): "The first reading, with the fatha on the taa', is more sound, due to the choice of the majority, and because Moses had displayed from the miracles what necessitated Pharaoh's knowledge of his truthfulness, so Pharaoh only responded with excuses and evasion. It is as if he said: 'You have known by proof and evidence "that none has sent down these" —meaning the signs'."]]

﴿"Only the Lord of the heavens and the earth has sent these down"﴾, meaning these nine signs, ﴿as clear evidences﴾. Basa'ir is the plural of basira, meaning that by them one sees (clearly).

﴿"And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed"﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "cursed." Mujahid said: "destroyed." Qatadah said: "ruined." Al-Farra' said: "that is, turned away and prevented from good." It is said: "What turned you away (tabaraka) from this matter," meaning what prevented you and diverted you from it.[[See: Zad al-Masir: 5/94-95.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 103–106:

﴿So he intended to drive them out of the land⦆ That is: Pharaoh intended to drive Moses and the Children of Israel out, that is, to expel them ﴿from the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt. ﴿So We drowned him and those with him, all together﴾, and We saved Moses and his people.

﴿And We said after him﴾, that is, after the destruction of Pharaoh, ﴿to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt and al-Sham, ﴿and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in a crowd (lafif)﴾, that is, all together, to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection. Al-lafif (lit. "a mixed gathering") means a great multitude when they are mixed together from every kind. It is said: "The armies gathered (laffat al-juyush)" when they became mixed together. The gathering of the Resurrection is likewise, in which are the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked.

Al-Kalbi said: "When the promise of the Hereafter comes" means the coming of Jesus from heaven. "We will bring you together in a crowd" means: the mixed-up ones (al-nuzza') from every people, from here and from there, gathered together.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings﴾ to the obedient, ﴿and a warner﴾ to the disobedient.

﴿And a Qur'an which We have divided (faraqnahu)﴾. It was said: its meaning is that We sent it down in installments (nujum), not all at once, as evidenced by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wa-Qur'anan farraqnahu﴾ with the doubled letter (tashdid), while the common reading is with the single letter (takhfif). That is: We made it detailed (fassalnahu). It was also said: We made it clear (bayyannahu). Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that We distinguished through it between truth and falsehood. ﴿So that you might recite it to the people at a slow pace (ala muktin)﴾, that is, at a measured and deliberate pace, with proper arrangement (tartil) and unhurried recitation (tarassul), over twenty-three years. ﴿And We sent it down in stages (tanzil)﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 103–106:

﴿So he intended to drive them out of the land⦆ That is: Pharaoh intended to drive Moses and the Children of Israel out, that is, to expel them ﴿from the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt. ﴿So We drowned him and those with him, all together﴾, and We saved Moses and his people.

﴿And We said after him﴾, that is, after the destruction of Pharaoh, ﴿to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt and al-Sham, ﴿and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in a crowd (lafif)﴾, that is, all together, to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection. Al-lafif (lit. "a mixed gathering") means a great multitude when they are mixed together from every kind. It is said: "The armies gathered (laffat al-juyush)" when they became mixed together. The gathering of the Resurrection is likewise, in which are the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked.

Al-Kalbi said: "When the promise of the Hereafter comes" means the coming of Jesus from heaven. "We will bring you together in a crowd" means: the mixed-up ones (al-nuzza') from every people, from here and from there, gathered together.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings﴾ to the obedient, ﴿and a warner﴾ to the disobedient.

﴿And a Qur'an which We have divided (faraqnahu)﴾. It was said: its meaning is that We sent it down in installments (nujum), not all at once, as evidenced by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wa-Qur'anan farraqnahu﴾ with the doubled letter (tashdid), while the common reading is with the single letter (takhfif). That is: We made it detailed (fassalnahu). It was also said: We made it clear (bayyannahu). Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that We distinguished through it between truth and falsehood. ﴿So that you might recite it to the people at a slow pace (ala muktin)﴾, that is, at a measured and deliberate pace, with proper arrangement (tartil) and unhurried recitation (tarassul), over twenty-three years. ﴿And We sent it down in stages (tanzil)﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verses 107–109:

﴿Say: Believe in it or do not believe.﴾ This is in the manner of a warning and a threat. ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it﴾. It was said: they are the believers among the People of the Book, those who were seeking the religion before the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then embraced Islam after his mission, such as Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Salman al-Farisi, Abu Dharr, and others. [[See: al-Tabari: 15/181; Zad al-Masir: 5/97.]]

﴿When it is recited to them﴾, meaning: the Qur'an [[This is because the context of the speech concerns the Noble Qur'an, and no mention of other scriptures has preceded it, so the speech is directed to it. This refutes the view of those who said that what is meant is what was revealed to the People of the Book from Allah. See: al-Tabari: 15/181; Zad al-Masir: 5/97.]] ﴿they fall down upon their chins﴾, meaning they fall upon their chins. Ibn ʿAbbas said: by "chins" he meant the faces. ﴿in prostration﴾. ﴿And they say: Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.﴾ Meaning: it is occurring and has come to pass.

﴿And they fall upon their chins weeping﴾, meaning they fall upon their faces weeping. Weeping is recommended when reciting the Qur'an. [[Many hadiths and reports from the early generations have been transmitted on this. Among them, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Recite the Qur'an and weep; and if you cannot weep, then feign weeping" (narrated by Ibn Majah, no. 4196, in al-Zuhd, and its chain is weak). And from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): that he led the congregation in the dawn prayer and recited Surah Yusuf and wept until his tears flowed down onto his collarbone. In another narration: that this happened in the night prayer, which indicates that he repeated it. And from Abu Raja' who said: "I saw Ibn ʿAbbas, and under his eyes was something like a worn-out thong (the thin strap on a sandal over the top of the foot) from tears." See: al-Nawawi, al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an, pp. 68–69; and see al-Qurtubi: 10/342.]] ﴿and it increases them in humility﴾, meaning in submission to their Lord. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping﴾ [Maryam: 58].

We were informed by Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi: Abu ʿAmr ibn Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Muzani informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Junayd narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali narrated to us: ʿAsim informed us, from ʿAli ibn ʿAsim: al-Mas'udi narrated to us, namely ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, mawla (client) of Abu Talhah [[In "B": mawla Talhah. In Sharh al-Sunnah: mawla Al Talhah.]], from ʿIsa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Fire will not enter one who wept out of fear of Allah, until the milk returns to the udder; and the dust in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell will never gather in the nostrils of a Muslim." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter "What has come concerning the virtue of dust in the way of Allah": 5/260–261, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Jihad, chapter "The virtue of one who acts in the way of Allah": 6/12; authenticated by al-Hakim: 4/260; and Ibn Hibban, no. 1598, p. 385, in Mawarid al-Zam'an. Also Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/505, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/364.]]

We were informed by Abu al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri: Abu al-Qasim ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-Khaliq al-Mu'adhdhin informed us: Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan informed us: Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi narrated to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Bahili informed us: Abu Habib al-Ghanawi narrated to us: Bahz ibn Hakim narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Three eyes are forbidden to the Fire: an eye that wept out of fear of Allah, an eye that stayed awake in the way of Allah, and an eye that lowered its gaze from what Allah has forbidden." [[Narrated by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/365; in its chain is al-Kudaymi, who is weak. On this topic, there is also a narration from Abu Rayhanah, recorded by al-Hakim: 2/83. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/287): "Narrated by Ahmad and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat, and the narrators of Ahmad are trustworthy; al-Nasa'i narrated a part of it; and Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah: 5/206, and Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 5/350.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 110:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Gracious (al-Rahman)⦆. Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated in Mecca one night, and he began to weep and say in his prostration: "O Allah, O Rahman." Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad forbids us from our gods, yet he calls upon two gods!" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 15/182. See also: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 341; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/348; al-Qurtubi: 10/342.]] Its meaning: they are two names for one [Being].

﴿Whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names⦆. "Ma" (whichever) is redundant (sila); its meaning: whichever of these two names you call upon, or any of His names, ﴿to Him belong the most beautiful names⦆.

﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent in it⦆. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent in it⦆. He said: It was revealed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was hiding in Mecca. When he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur'an. When the polytheists heard it, they would revile the Qur'an, the One who revealed it, and the one who brought it. So Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer⦆, meaning your recitation, so that the polytheists hear it and revile the Qur'an; ﴿nor be silent in it⦆, meaning from your companions, so that you do not make them hear it; ﴿and seek a way between that⦆. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the chapter on the Tafsir of Surah al-Isra, "And do not be loud in your prayer nor be silent in it": 8/404-405; and Muslim in the chapter on loud recitation... no. 446: 1/329.]]

And with this same chain, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: Musaddad narrated to us, from Hushaym, from Abu Bishr with his chain, the like of it, and he added: ﴿and seek a way between that⦆: "Make them hear, but do not be loud until they take the Qur'an from you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tawhid, chapter on the saying of Allah: "He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness": 13/463.]]

Some said: the verse concerns supplication. This is the view of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and al-Nakha'i, Mujahid and Makhul. Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning His saying: "And do not be loud in your prayer nor be silent in it," she said: That was revealed concerning supplication. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the chapter on the Tafsir, "He sent it down with His knowledge...": 8/405.]]

And Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: Some Bedouins of the Banu Tamim, when the Prophet ﷺ finished the prayer, would say: "O Allah, grant us wealth and children," and they would say it aloud. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer⦆. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 15/184; al-Suyuti attributed it also to Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir; see al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/351.]] That is: do not raise your voice in your recitation or in your supplication, nor be silent in it. [[Al-Tabari preferred the first view, that of Ibn 'Abbas, because it is the soundest chain transmitted from a Companion concerning it, and the most similar of the views to what the apparent wording of the revelation indicates. That is because His saying, "And do not be loud in your prayer nor be silent in it," comes after His saying, "Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Gracious..." and after the rebuke of the disbelievers for their disbelief in the Qur'an, and their distance from it and from faith. If that is so, then what is more appropriate and more similar to His saying, "And do not be loud in your prayer nor be silent in it," is that its cause be drawn from the context of the speech that surrounds it, unless there is a meaning that requires diverting it from that, or some indication of diversion from what is in its context. Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/188.]]

Al-mukhafatah (silence) is lowering the voice and remaining silent. "And seek a way between that": between loudness and concealment.

Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Khuza'i informed us, Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us, Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabah al-Ansari, from Abu Qatadah, that the Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr: "I passed by you while you were reciting and lowering your voice." He said: "I am making someone hear whom I am speaking to privately." He said: "Raise it a little." And he said to 'Umar: "I passed by you while you were reciting and raising your voice." He said: "I am waking the sleeper and driving away Satan." He said: "Lower it a little." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the chapter on voluntary prayer, on raising the voice in recitation during night prayer: 2/96; and al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on the times of prayer, on what has come concerning recitation at night: 2/526, and he said: "A gharib hadith. Yahya ibn Ishaq transmitted it with a connected chain from Hammad ibn Salamah, while most people transmitted this hadith from Thabit, from Abd Allah ibn Rabah, as a mursal report." Al-Mundhiri said: "This Yahya ibn Ishaq is al-Bajali al-Silhini, and Muslim used him as evidence in his Sahih." Al-Albani authenticated its chain in his notes on al-Mishkah: 1/380, because the one who connected it is trustworthy.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 17, verse 111:**

﴿And say: "All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son."﴾ Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to praise Him for His oneness (tawhid). The meaning of "al-hamdu lillah" (all praise is for Allah) is: extolling Him with what He is worthy of.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: That is, "All praise is for Allah, who informed me that He has not taken a son."

﴿And He has no partner in the dominion, and He has no ally out of weakness.﴾ Mujahid said: He is not humbled, so as to need an ally by whom He would be strengthened.

﴿And magnify Him with all magnificence.﴾ That is: glorify Him, exalting Him above having a partner or an ally.

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: al-Imam Abu al-Tayyib Sahl [ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani narrated to us: Nadr ibn Hammad Abu al-Harith al-Warraq narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us] [[The text between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]] from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first people to be called to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection are those who praise Allah in times of ease and in times of hardship." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 12/19, and in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir 1/103. Al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/502. Abu Nu'aym narrated it in Hilyat al-Awliya': 5/69. In Mishkat (al-Masabih), it is attributed to al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, 2/714, and in its chain is Nasr ibn Hammad, who is weak. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/95): al-Tabarani narrated it in three works with several chains; in one of them is Qays ibn al-Rabi', who is trustworthy, while Shu'bah, al-Thawri and others narrated from him, and Yahya al-Qattan and others declared him weak; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih. Al-Bazzar narrated it in similar wording with a good (hasan) chain. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/49, and al-Albani declared it weak in Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah: 2/93-94.]].

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah al-Na'imi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah al-Salihi informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Bishran informed us: Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatadah, that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-hamdu lillah is the head of gratitude; no servant thanks Allah without praising Him." [[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/424, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Jami' li-Shu'ab al-Iman as cited in Mishkat: 2/714, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/50. Al-Khattabi in Gharib al-Hadith and al-Daylami in al-Firdaws narrated it with a chain whose narrators are trustworthy, but it is munqati' (discontinuous) between Qatadah and Ibn 'Amr. See Fayd al-Qadir by al-Manawi: 3/418.]].

Abu al-Fadl ibn Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi informed us: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Ansari informed us: Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us: Yahya ibn Khalid ibn Ayyub al-Makhzumi related to us: Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir ibn Bishr al-Khuzami al-Ansari related to us, from Talhah ibn Khirash, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the best supplication is al-hamdu lillah, and the best remembrance is La ilaha illa Allah." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter on what has been related that the supplication of a Muslim is answered, 9/325, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the narration of Musa ibn Ibrahim." Also narrated by al-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wa'l-Layla, pp. 840-841; and Ibn Majah in al-Adab, chapter on the merit of those who praise Allah, no. 3800, 2/1249. Ibn Hibban authenticated it in Mawarid al-Zaman, p. 578. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak: 1/503, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/449, and al-Albani mentioned it in Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah: 3/484.]].

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi informed us: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd related to us: Zuhayr related to us: Mansur related to us, from Hilal ibn Yasaf... [the chain as given]: from al-Rabi' ibn 'Umaylah, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most beloved words to Allah the Exalted are four: La ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, Subhan Allah, and al-hamdu lillah; it does not harm you with which of them you begin." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Adab, chapter on the disliking of giving ugly names, no. 2137, 3/1685. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/9.]].
